# Decisions

Why Magnum works the way it does. One entry per decision, newest last, each with the
alternative that was rejected. Change a decision by adding a new entry that supersedes it, not by
editing history. Code, config comments and prompts reference these by their heading. The last
section, Learned rules, is the self-improving loop's (the skill editor's entries and the reverts of
skill versions); people add theirs to the sections before it, at the end of the one it belongs to.

## Runtime and scope (2026-10-02)

- **One Go binary, daemon plus CLI, SQLite registry, no IPC server.** The CLI and the daemon share the
  registry; mutating commands write a request row and `SIGUSR1` the daemon. Rejected: a gRPC/HTTP
  daemon API (one more port and auth surface for no gain on a single machine).
- **Reviews run in interactive herdr panes, never headless.** You can watch, take over or answer an
  agent; sessions persist so re-reviews keep context. Rejected: `codex exec` / `claude -p` batch runs
  (no continuity, nothing to look at when it goes wrong).
- **Three-agent pipeline with a judge.** Candidate reviewers (Claude `/code-review`, Codex `review`)
  propose; one persistent Codex judge proves or rejects every candidate, adds its own pass and posts
  exactly one review. Rejected: posting each reviewer's output (duplicate and contradictory comments).
- **GitHub is the only proof a review was posted.** Each round carries a marker
  `<!-- magnum:run=<id> head=<sha7> -->`; verification looks for it by the expected login on the
  expected commit. Agent status is only a hint for when to check. Rejected: trusting the agent's
  "done" text.
- **Everything lives in the repository**: `config.toml`, prompts, the judge skill, `state/` (gitignored),
  the herdr plugin manifest. Only the launchd plist lives outside. Rejected: `~/.config/magnum` and
  `~/.agents/skills` symlinks (moving parts in three places).
- **All GitHub calls go through `gh api`**, including App token minting. A freshly built unsigned Go
  binary is blocked by Little Snitch on this machine; `gh` is already trusted. Rejected: direct
  `net/http` with a per-build firewall rule.

## Identity and verdicts

- **Polling always uses a `gh` user identity; posting uses the watch's identity** (a user or a GitHub
  App). App installation tokens cannot call `/user`, so App identity is verified through
  `/installation/repositories` and the posted review's `user.login`.
- **A bot never approves by accident.** The default no-findings verdict for an App identity is
  `COMMENT`; `APPROVE` and `REQUEST_CHANGES` must be enabled per repository with a `[[repo]]` block
  (`no_findings_event`, `blocking_event`), which overrides the identity's defaults (2026-10-04).
  Rejected: per-identity only (one App serves many repos with different trust levels).
- **A PR follows its watch's identity until its first review is posted**; afterwards it keeps the
  login that owns the review thread. `magnum review --as` pins one PR explicitly, and a round for a
  changed identity parks the old sessions first because their panes carry the old gh config
  (2026-10-04, after a false "identity leak").
- **A review posted by another login that carries our marker pauses the whole watch** (identity leak).
  Run ids carry 6 random hex characters so a stranger cannot spoof the marker (2026-10-04).
- **A PR follows its watch's identity, also after its first review** (2026-10-04; supersedes "A PR follows
  its watch's identity until its first review is posted"). Moving a watch from one App to another left
  every PR the old App had reviewed posting as the old App. Now a PR nothing reviewed yet still follows
  the watch on every poll, and a reviewed one migrates when its next round is dispatched: `prs.identity`
  becomes the watch's, the old identity joins `pr.<id>.former_identities` (newest last), `pr.identity_migrated`
  is recorded, and the round parks the old sessions through the identity-change path. The round treats the
  former logins as its own history: the previous review (marked `Former`, so the round never dismisses it
  with its own credentials), the threads of the reply contract, the judge's earlier findings
  (`former_logins` in its prompt). Logins compare as accounts: a user `x` and the App `x[bot]` are two. Verification
  still accepts only the new login, so a former login's review with an old marker is neither the round's
  review nor a leak, while one carrying the round's own marker still is a leak. Once the new review is
  posted, each former identity dismisses with its own credentials its own CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews (when it
  dismisses its stale ones) and, for an App without `keep_approvals`, its approvals. A PR pinned with
  `magnum review --as` (`pr.<id>.identity_pinned`) and a paused round never migrate. Rejected: a fresh
  history for the new login (the replies and open findings of the old reviews would be lost) and
  dismissing the old reviews with the new identity (only an identity's own reviews are its to withdraw).

- **Severity decides the verdict** (2026-10-04). 59 of 68 posted findings were P2, and the verdict did
  not follow from them. The skill defines `P1` as blocks the merge (wrong behaviour on a realistic
  path, security, data loss, a broken build or deploy), `P2` as should be fixed before the merge and
  `P3` as optional, with two examples each, and re-ranks candidate priorities by them. The blocking
  event is used if and only if a `P0` or `P1` is posted (an earlier one still open counts), a review
  with only `P2`/`P3` findings is a `COMMENT`, and only a review without findings uses the no-findings
  event. Rejected: the no-findings event (an approval) for `P3`-only reviews, which reads as "nothing
  left to do" while findings are open.
- **The posted review stands on its own and covers exactly its head** (2026-10-04). Every finding
  carries its reproduction inline (the failing input, command or test body, fenced, about 25 lines;
  a test that pins the bug as a `suggestion` on a test file in the diff), because all seven reviews of
  one repository mentioned reproductions the author could not see and four cited `/tmp` or other local
  paths. Local paths are forbidden in posted text and verification warns (`round.local_paths`) when it
  finds one. Checks sit in a collapsed `<details>` block, and failures the review machine caused
  (missing tables, deadlocks, the wrong Ruby) go to the result file's `environment_failures`
  (`round.environment`) and the notes, never into the review. The judge reviews `head_sha` only: the
  skill's "re-read the base and head before posting" predated the restart logic and let a judge call
  four findings fixed by a commit it was not reviewing. Rejected: failing the round on a local path
  (the review is otherwise valid; the warning is for the operator).
- **One run, one review** (2026-10-04). One of 19 reviews was posted twice with identical comments. The
  skill lists the PR's reviews right before its POST and stops when one carries the run's marker;
  verification keeps the first review with the marker, records `round.duplicate_review` and deletes
  pending duplicates (`DELETE .../reviews/{id}` works only for an unsubmitted review). A submitted
  duplicate stays, with a warning, because GitHub cannot delete it. Rejected: dismissing it (dismissal
  applies only to approvals and change requests, and the comments stay either way).

## Checkouts and pools

- **Always detached checkouts of `refs/magnum/pr/<N>`**, never the PR branch, so a PR you hold in a
  manual worktree is still reviewable in a magnum slot and nothing magnum does can push.
- **Big repositories get a pool of warm slots** (`[[pool]]`, min/max, provisioned with the repo's own
  setup script and their own databases); everything else gets a worktree per PR next to its clone,
  with worktrunk hooks or a `[[repo]]` block for setup. Rejected: cloning per PR (minutes per round).
- **A dirty checkout holds a magnum-owned slot only with evidence of a human**: a foreign agent in the
  slot or its workspace, your activity after the checkout, or head drift. Otherwise the changes are
  the round's own residue (test runs rewriting `schema.rb`, copied files), are discarded and recorded
  as a `slot.discarded` event listing the paths. Manual worktrees keep the strict rule (any change
  holds unless `--force`). Rejected: holding on any change (pools starved after one round),
  discarding silently (the pre-review behaviour).
- **Destructive steps re-run their guard when resumed** after a crash; orphan database drops need a
  complete discovery (every worktree list and the MySQL listing succeeded) and a rescan right before
  dropping. Unsuffixed databases are never dropped.
- **Files magnum writes into a checkout go through `os.Root`** so a tracked symlink in the PR cannot
  redirect a write outside the worktree; `.mise.local.toml` is rendered from parsed TOML with token
  keys stripped in every representation.
- **A PR that changes the schema is reviewed on its schema** (2026-10-05, after 4 of 9 rounds of the pool
  repository recorded skipped DB specs: a missing table, missing columns, TEXT instead of MEDIUMTEXT, a
  missing column the PR added). The checkout's schema step only marked the slot `dirty_schema` for its
  release, so the reviewers ran the PR's specs against the base schema. When the round's checkout leaves
  the pool slot `dirty_schema` (the PR changes `schema_paths` since its merge base, the test the schema
  step uses), the pool's `reset_db` commands now run before the reviewers as the first commands of the
  readiness step: `zsh -lc` in the checkout with the slot's env, recorded in `readiness.json`, the
  `round.readiness` event and the judge's `readiness` list as `reset_db` checks. The reset has the
  release's budget for `reset_db` (`slots.ResetDBTimeout`, 30 minutes) of its own, and `ready_timeout`
  starts after it, so `prepare` and `ready` keep theirs whole however long a dev load, a test load and a
  seed take; a reset command that outlives the budget is stopped and the ones after it are skipped. A
  failure does not stop the round; the skill has the judge skip the checks that need the PR's tables and
  record it under `environment_failures`. The slot stays `dirty_schema`, so the release still loads the
  base schema, and a later round of the PR reloads too (also after a push that reverted the change: the
  databases still hold the PR's earlier schema). `[[pool]] reset_db_on_schema_change = false` keeps
  `reset_db` to the release; `magnum doctor` warns about a pool with `schema_paths` and no `reset_db`.
  Not rerun when a push restarts the reviewers mid-round. Rejected: running `prepare` instead (a pool may
  have none, and `db:test:prepare` loads the test database only), counting the reset against
  `ready_timeout` (5 minutes: a slow reset was cut, or left `prepare` and `ready` skipped), and a key of
  its own for the reset's budget (the release's timeout already bounds `reset_db`).
- **The daemon reads a pull request's files only as small regular files** (2026-10-09). The daemon read
  the files a pull request controls with os.ReadFile, which follows a committed symlink and has no size
  limit. A PR that committed Gemfile.lock, db/schema.rb, tmp/.worktree-db-slug or .codex/config.toml as a
  symlink to /dev/zero made the daemon allocate memory until it was killed, and the resumable step that
  read the file ran again after the restart. A FIFO left there by the PR's setup code blocked the
  goroutine in its open for good, and a symlink to a file outside the checkout was read as the checkout's
  own file. Now `fsx.ReadRegular(path, limit)` does an Lstat first and refuses a symlink or a special file
  (`fsx.ErrNotRegular`) and a file past the limit (`fsx.ErrTooLarge`) before it opens anything. It opens
  with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and checks SameFile against the Lstat, so a file swapped in after the check
  is refused and a FIFO is never waited on. It reads through `io.LimitReader(limit+1)` and passes a
  missing file's error back unwrapped. These readers use it: lockHash (16 MiB per lockfile), schemaVersion
  (16 MiB), the slug marker's readers through the new `slots.ReadMarker` (4 KiB: verifyMarker,
  perPRDBSlug, inventory's readSlug) and checkoutHooks (1 MiB). A refused lockfile is an error, not a
  hash: the deps step fails at once, post_checkout does not run, and lock_sha keeps its old value. A
  refused schema.rb is an error, which the round's CheckSchema already treats as "reload". A refused
  marker fails verify_marker, falls back to DBSlug for a per-PR worktree, and leaves inventory's ownership
  discovery incomplete, so no orphans are computed. A refused config.toml means magnum cannot tell, so the
  hooks review is declined. The curator's proposal.md and changes.json are capped at MaxFileBytes, and the
  harness at MaxFileBytes per file and at MaxStateBytes together with the notes. These caps are checked
  before any read; before, the files were read whole and then measured. Only the path's last element is
  checked; parent directories resolve as usual, and the file they lead to must still be a regular file
  under the cap. Kept: rubyPin's own root-confined read, which follows a symlink that stays inside the
  checkout and parses the first 64 KiB of a longer file; ReadRegular would refuse both. Rejected: a fixed
  "refused" token in lockHash (the next PR with a refused lockfile would skip post_checkout), and a token
  that changes on every call (post_checkout would run bundle install against the /dev/zero link until
  DepsTimeout); an os.Root per checkout for every read (the files sit at fixed names, and a
  parent-directory symlink can only reach a regular file under the cap); 1 MiB caps for lockfiles and
  schema.rb (large applications already have files of about 0.6 MiB, and a lockfile over the cap blocks
  every checkout of the repository).
- **A park cut short by ctrl+c or the daemon's stop still puts the PR back in closed** (2026-10-09, an
  audit found that the promise of the releasing entry did not hold). cleanup's apply moves a closed PR to
  releasing before it parks the sessions, and a failed park moves it back. But the rollback ran on the
  same context as the park, so a park that failed because that context ended (ctrl+c on `magnum cleanup`,
  the daemon stopping) also failed the rollback, and the PR stayed releasing. Now the rollback runs on
  `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`, as the slots compensations do. Rejected: leaving it for the next plan's
  resume of a releasing PR (that resumes a release nothing had begun, and the sessions were never parked).
- **A panic ends its unit, not the daemon** (2026-10-09). No daemon goroutine recovered a panic, and crash
  recovery sent the interrupted PR again without charging an attempt. So a panic tied to one PR's data
  crash-looped the daemon and killed every round in flight each time. Now Engine.safely (util.go) runs
  each goroutine body and recovers its panic. It logs slog.Error with the panic value and debug.Stack()
  (redacted), writes an engine.panic event (on the PR's subject for a round, the stop and the open; on the
  notes subject for a curation; daemon-level otherwise), and settles the unit on a detached context. A
  settle that panics too is only logged. The units: a round (roundPanicked: if the PR is still claiming or
  reviewing, its active runs end as abandoned or failed 'the round panicked', the slot goes back to held,
  a kept approval is withdrawn as after any failed round, and retryOrAttention charges an attempt, so
  maxAttempts leads to needs_attention), afterRound's stop orders and a `magnum abort|ignore` stop (the
  requests fail, out of the in-flight set), `magnum open` (the request fails), a heavy job (it fails alone
  and its key is free again), the retro (KVRetroLast says it panicked, and a daily retro records the day
  so it does not restart every tick), a notes curation (it waits curateRetry, as a stopped one does), an
  urgent toast, the eval and pane observers, and the signal handler (it stops the daemon, since SIGTERM
  would otherwise stay caught and unanswered). In the pipeline, a stage role's goroutine (runRoleSafely)
  and the judge's own pass turn a panic into a ReportFailed report (rolePanicked: a round.panic event, the
  turn in flight interrupted with the judge's session kept, the run failed), so the round goes on without
  that report. A changed file's history worker turns a panic into the history's error, which only warns
  and names no path. Rejected: re-raising after recording (that keeps the crash loop); recovering around
  Tick (it is not a goroutine boundary, and a lock held at the panic could hang the loop instead of
  restarting it).
- **Usage errors name the command, and every usage line names exactly its command's flags** (2026-10-09).
  `magnum approve`, `request-changes` and `unapprove` printed `usage: magnum <ref> [...]` without their
  own name, and they said "which PR?" when given two PRs. `review` and `open` accepted --workspace and
  --cwd (the plugin context) without listing them. Now their Use strings start with the name, actUsage
  prints that whole line, more than one PR gets "one PR at a time", and review and open list `[--workspace
  id] [--cwd path]`. Two tree-walking tests guard every command. First: a command whose usage line names a
  <placeholder> outside [...] exits 2 when run without arguments and prints `usage: magnum <command> ...`.
  Each slots subcommand prints its own line, built from its Use string (a same-day follow-up). Second: each
  usage line names the flags its command defines, and no other. Rejected: printing cobra's UseLine in the
  runs wrapper on every exit 2 (the commands print their own lines, so the line would appear twice).
- **cleanup's questions go to stderr, and are asked only when stdin and stderr are terminals**
  (2026-10-09). `magnum cleanup` and `magnum slots remove` asked their y/N and typed-slug questions on
  stdout, whenever stdin alone was a terminal. `magnum cleanup > plan.txt` therefore wrote a destructive
  question into the file and waited for an answer nobody could see. Now the questions go to stderr; the
  plan and the report stay on stdout. They are asked only when stdin and stderr are both terminals
  (inspCanAsk). Otherwise nothing is applied, and the command says "stdin or stderr is not a terminal;
  re-run with --yes". Rejected: also requiring stdout to be a terminal (writing the plan to a file while
  answering on the terminal is fair use).
- **On a terminal, release --json and unapprove --json need --yes** (2026-10-09). On a terminal, `magnum
  release` asks y/N before it parks the sessions and resets the worktree, and `magnum unapprove` asks
  before it dismisses the operator's approval. --json skipped both questions, so the command applied
  without asking. Now, on a terminal, --json without --yes is a usage error (exit 2, "--json needs --yes
  to apply"), like cleanup's --json, which applies only with --yes. Nothing is released, queued or asked.
  Off a terminal (scripts, the herdr plugin's `here release`), nothing changes. Rejected: asking on stderr
  under --json (a JSON consumer on a terminal would block on a question it does not expect).
- **An unset opsHolder runs nothing** (2026-10-09). opsHolder's zero value was opsMine ("both locks are
  ours: run the work here"). cleanup and release went on to the in-process work, with a nil unlock, for
  any holder other than busy or daemon. The zero value is now opsUnknown, and a failed acquireOps returns
  it. cleanup, release and merge-check now test for opsMine explicitly and refuse any other holder
  ("nothing was run"); merge-check also names its opsDaemon case (it works beside the daemon). slots.go's
  inProcess still treats any other holder as its own (a follow-up).
- **`magnum pin/unpin --slot` writes the PR's pinned flag before it touches the slot** (2026-10-09, after
  an audit: requestPin threw away the error from UpdatePR on the slot's PR, then pinned or unpinned the
  slot and reported success, so a PR could stay pinned while its slot was unpinned, or the reverse). Now a
  failed write fails the request with `pinned <slot>: write the PR's pinned flag: <err>`, and the slot
  stays as it was. Rejected: changing the slot first and undoing it on failure (the slot is the side that
  holds or frees work, so it goes last).
- **The slots' registry lookups take only ErrNotFound for no row** (2026-10-09, after an audit: Reserve
  took any SlotByPR failure as "the PR has no slot", so it could assign a second slot or report "no free
  slot", and Checkout's verify step skipped the assignment's head update on any OpenAssignmentBySlot
  failure, so the assignment kept an older head). Both now switch on errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) and
  return any other error, wrapped with the PR or the slot, as slotPR, ensureAssignment and poolRow already
  do.
- **`magnum slots provision --count` is at most 999 and never overflows the max check** (2026-10-09, after
  an audit: `live+count > pool.Max` wrapped for a --count near the largest int, passed, and started a
  provisioning loop with no end). The flag now refuses a count below 1 or above 999 (slotsMaxCount, the
  slot numbers slotsNumber recognizes) as a usage error. The max check reads `count > pool.Max-live`.
- **No git command of magnum's runs the clone's hooks** (2026-10-09). Every git call ran with the clone's
  hooks on. A PR's setup script (bundle install or npm install through the pool's scripts) can set a
  relative core.hooksPath (husky's .husky/_, lefthook) or write .git/hooks. Every later checkout, fetch or
  ref update then ran code from the PR's tree outside the sandbox. Now gitx's runner, CloneWith and the
  pipeline's restore of an edited checkout set core.hooksPath=/dev/null. The setting goes in the
  environment as GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 (git 2.31 or later ranks
  these with `git -c`), and the git processes git starts inherit it. gitx.Env exports this environment for
  code that runs git outside gitx. Magnum relies on no hook, and Git LFS content comes through the smudge
  filter, which is not a hook. Rejected: `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` on the command line. The effect is
  the same, but it changes the argv of every git command, and test fakes in about a dozen test files
  across packages match that argv by prefix.
- **A per-PR clone's origin must be the repository on github.com** (2026-10-09). slots.originMatches was a
  looser copy of gitx's check. It compared ParseRemote's owner/name on any host and otherwise fell back to
  a substring match. So a clone whose origin was on gitlab.com or evil-github.com, or a local path that
  names owner/name, passed the clone step. Now ensureClone calls gitx.OriginMatches, the check FindClone
  already used (now exported): the host must be exactly github.com, and owner and name are compared
  case-insensitively. Any other origin fails with ErrOriginMismatch ("want github.com/<repo>").
- **Heavy commands never inherit the daemon's secrets** (2026-10-09). Pool scripts and per-PR hooks run
  code the PR controls (bundle install on the PR's Gemfile), and they ran with the daemon's whole
  environment. DefaultStripEnv was removed only from the rendered .mise.local.toml, and an App's
  private_key_env PEM was passed through. Now runLogged, which runs every heavy command (runHeavy's pool
  scripts and shellCmd's per-PR hooks, through mise or /bin/sh), unsets gitx.ScrubbedEnv, DefaultStripEnv
  and the new Deps.SecretEnv. A value that [pool] env or [[repo]] env sets on purpose is still passed.
  Deps.SecretEnv takes the identities' private_key_env names from the app. Rejected: an allowlist
  environment (mise, rbenv, bundler and pnpm need much of the user's environment: PATH, HOME,
  SSH_AUTH_SOCK, proxies).
- **Every string a screen draws is cleaned once, where it comes in** (2026-10-09). sanitizeRow and
  sanitizeStatus kept their fields in hand-written lists. Several fields reached the screens raw. On the
  board: a PR's findings (Verdict, Posted, SHA), its standing approval (Head, URL), NeedsMe and
  ReviewDecision. On the dashboard: the daemon's Skew, the failing watches, the queue's and the slots'
  GitHub states, the queue's review facts, the notes and the title's facts (some of these were cleaned
  where they were drawn). The picker drew PR titles and authors with oneLine, which keeps ESC and BEL. Now
  all of them are cleaned (cleanFacts, cleanReviewFacts and cleanDelta; sanitizePicks for the picker's
  entries, its reloads and its Lookup). TestSanitizersCleanEveryStringField puts "\x1b[31mX\x07" into
  every string field reachable from PRBoardRow, StatusData and PickEntry, nested ones included, and fails
  when any survives the sanitizers, so a new field needs no list. An enum field can be exempted by its
  path (unsanitizedEnums). The list is empty: every string is drawn somewhere, GHState too, through the
  refusals' "is merged". The footer cleans its text once: setFlash and failure run cleanText (the text may
  be an action's output or the daemon's answer), and the load and save error lines go through errLine.
  Rejected: cleaning at each draw site (the list of sites grows with every screen).
- **The dashboard reads a slot's pin and state from their own fields** (2026-10-09). The dashboard read a
  slot's pin from the display string SlotState ("held [pinned,hold:<reason>]"). A hold reason that
  contained "pinned" therefore made x refuse ("is pinned: unpin first"), made p refuse ("already pinned"),
  and made the review question say that the review unpins the slot. The slot's mark read the first word of
  the same string. tui.SlotRow gains State and Pinned, which the `magnum status` screen sets from the
  slot. SlotState is now for display only.
- **A queued provision request is held to the pool's room, as the CLI's --count is** (2026-10-09). The
  daemon's provision handler checked live+count > pool.max. A huge count carried by a queued request wraps
  that sum, so the check passed and the heavy worker provisioned slots without end. Now the handler
  refuses a count above max minus the live slots, with the CLI's wording: "<repo> allows at most N slots
  and has M; lower --count or raise max in config.toml".
- **Pool scripts and per-PR hooks never inherit an App's private key** (2026-10-09). The app wiring never
  set slots.Deps.SecretEnv, so the variables named by the identities' private_key_env reached the setup,
  post-checkout and teardown scripts and the per-PR hooks, which run the PR's code outside the sandbox.
  Now wire() passes every non-empty private_key_env, and the slots manager unsets them with the GitHub
  tokens.
- **The rendered local mise file keeps the main clone's spelling** (2026-10-11). Magnum read and rendered
  only `.mise.local.toml`, but mise reads `mise.local.toml` too. A main clone with only the undotted file
  got nothing rendered into a per-PR worktree, and a pool slot got a `.mise.local.toml` with the pool's
  env alone, which showed up as untracked in a repository whose `.gitignore` names only `mise.local.toml`;
  a copy_files entry naming the undotted file copied it with its secrets, strip_env never applied. Now
  slots.MiseLocalName picks the main clone's file: `.mise.local.toml` when it exists, because mise loads
  it after the undotted one ("`.mise.local.toml` overrides `mise.local.toml`",
  https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html), else `mise.local.toml`, which is also what a pool slot gets
  when the main clone has neither (the undotted name is the default). The file is rendered, trusted and
  copied by cleanup's manual-worktree reset under that name, and copy_files skips both spellings. A render
  removes the other spelling when its first line is magnum's marker (the marker now says "local mise
  file"; the old `.mise.local.toml` wording still counts), so a clone that renames its file leaves no
  rendered file behind; a file without the marker, or a symlink, is kept. The removal guard (holdChanges,
  which counts untracked files once a human was in the slot) skips the rendered file: a main clone renamed
  its file to the undotted name while PR branches still carried a `.gitignore` that ignores only the
  dotted one, so magnum's own file held removals as dirty. Only a file with the marker is skipped, and
  only in the hold: the removal still counts it, since `git worktree remove` needs `--force` to delete an
  untracked file. The readiness Ruby check reads `.mise.toml`, then `mise.toml` (the same precedence),
  then `.ruby-version`, and names the file it read. Rejected: keeping the dotted name for every render
  (untracked in a repository that ignores only `mise.local.toml`, and it hides the clone's own undotted
  file).
- **A pool slot's database slug is its name sanitized** (2026-10-11). A pool row stored its raw name as
  db_slug and SlotDBSlug returned the stored value as it was, while the setup derives its databases' slug
  from WT_BRANCH the way talkable's database.yml does (DBSlug: every character but letters, digits and `_`
  as `_`, at most 30) and writes that slug to tmp/.worktree-db-slug, so a pool with slot_name
  `example-review{n}` failed verify_marker (`example_review1` against `example-review1`). Now SlotDBSlug
  sanitizes the stored value (else the name), so a row that stored a raw dashed name resolves to the same
  slug; provisioning, its revival and adopt store and compare the sanitized slug; and the drop guard's
  AllowRegexp is slot_name sanitized the same way (`^example_review[0-9]+$`), so a removal can drop those
  databases. A name that already is a slug (`review3`) gives the same value everywhere.
- **A slot reruns post_checkout when any lockfile it holds or the commands change** (2026-10-14). On
  2026-10-12 the operator added `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` and `yarn build:css` to a pool's
  post_checkout after ten rounds had failed with `Propshaft::MissingAssetError`. The commands never ran
  and five more rounds failed the same way: only a change of lock_sha, a hash of Gemfile.lock and
  pnpm-lock.yaml, reran post_checkout, and the repository's yarn.lock was not hashed, nor were the
  commands. Now lockHash hashes each file of slots.LockFiles the checkout holds at its root
  (Gemfile.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, package-lock.json, bun.lock, composer.lock, go.sum,
  Cargo.lock, poetry.lock, uv.lock; each as its name, length and bytes), then the pool's post_checkout
  commands in their order, each with its length. A missing file adds nothing, so a checkout whose files
  and commands stay as they are keeps its hash, also when a name joins the list later (only the slots
  whose checkout has the new file reinstall); a test pins the hash of one input. The hash's input grew
  with this change, so every slot runs post_checkout once at its first checkout or release after the
  build. A lockfile that is refused (a symlink, a special file, past 16 MiB) fails the deps step as
  before, now under every listed name. Kept: provisioning and adopt record the same hash after the
  setup, so a slot's setup still counts as post_checkout's first run, and a new slot whose setup does not
  do what post_checkout does gets it at the first change of a lockfile or of the commands. Rejected:
  lockfiles below the root (no pool has a workspace of packages) and a column of its own for the
  commands' hash (one comparison covers both).
- **A release that breaks an unpinned pool slot lets its PR go** (2026-10-14). A schema reload that
  failed twice at release moved the slot to broken and left its pr_id as it was. On 2026-10-14 review11
  kept talkable#12012 and review18 kept #12011, so their next pushes waited for `magnum slots repair` in
  dispatch's slot gate while an unpinned pool PR can take any free slot, and a whiteboard request for
  #12012 was refused the same way. Now resetSchema moves the slot with the new store.BreakSlot: in one
  transaction it reads the pin and, for an unpinned slot, clears pr_id and closes the open assignment
  (end reason "broken") with the move to broken, so the PR claims another slot at its next round and
  the cleanup of a closed PR finds no broken slot to skip. A slot pinned while the reload ran keeps its
  PR and assignment, since a pin keeps its PR's rounds in its slot. The slot keeps the reload's error as
  last_error, and `magnum slots repair` provisions it again as before; a held release (no PR) breaks as
  before. Left out: after a failed reload, preferring the tick's further evictions of slots that need no
  reload (on 2026-10-14 one waiting PR's two evictions broke two slots in one minute on the same
  reload). needSlot takes the least recently used slot of EvictableSlots, and whether a release reloads
  depends on the pool's reset_db_on_schema_change, the dirty_schema flag and the development database's
  schema_migrations, which only the release reads; it needs that read and a record of the failure across
  the tick's jobs, not a sort key.
- **`magnum fix` claims a slot when the pool took the PR's back** (2026-10-27, section 5.4 of the companion
  fix design). On 2026-10-27 the review of talkable#11907 stood on its head, but the pool had evicted its
  slot, and `magnum fix` refused with "has no checkout of its reviewed head: its slot was handed back"; the
  operator had to restore the PR with `magnum open` first. Now the fix job claims a slot as `magnum open`
  does. The part of openPR that reserves a free pool slot (or makes a per-PR worktree), checks out the
  reviewed head and loads that head's schema into a fresh pool slot moved into claimFor, which openPR calls
  with its own words and the fix job's claimAtReviewedHead with `magnum fix`'s; it never pins and never
  takes an open hold, and openPR keeps its pin, hold, sessions, answers, events and release reason as they
  were. prepareFix lets a PR without a slot through once its review stands on the head (a head that moved
  still gets "nothing to fix", before any slot is looked for, so nothing is claimed or evicted), refuses one
  that is pinned where a pin refuses (autofix, a next cycle), and, for a job that will start, refuses while
  the pool has no free slot: needSlot starts freeing one, as for an open, and the answer is "no free <repo>
  slot right now; run `magnum fix <pr>` again shortly". runFix runs a new `fix.claim` step before the guard
  for a job without a slot (fixClaim), and fixGuard takes the slot the PR then has as the job's. The claimed
  slot moves to held, as a round leaves one: the job's reservation keeps eviction off it while the fixer
  works, and the pool can take it back once the loop ends, where a claimed slot would stay out of eviction
  until a restart. What the claim did to the slot's databases goes into the fix.start event (its message and
  `schema` in its data): a schema that could not be loaded is no failure, as for an open, but the fixer's
  specs then run on the last PR's, and the answer, given before the claim runs, cannot say it. A claim that
  fails releases the slot it reserved ("fix failed", as a failed open releases with "open failed") and ends
  the loop as a failed fix. So does one that `magnum abort` (or an ignore) cuts short, released as "fix
  stopped": kept, the slot would carry the last PR's checkout record, which a later `magnum open` takes as the
  PR's own and does not check out again. One a shutdown cuts short leaves the slot held. The free-slot check
  reads the pool before the answer, because the fix job answers its request before it runs, where an open
  answers from its own goroutine; a slot another round takes between that check and the claim ends the loop
  quietly with the same sentence (fix.ended and an info toast, as a stop ends one: nothing failed, and the
  sentence names the retry). The whiteboard job keeps its refusal of a PR without a slot. Rejected: claiming
  in the request (the checkout and a schema load take minutes on the tick's goroutine), reserving the slot in
  the request and checking it out in the job (two reservations for one claim, and a reserved slot to hand
  back when the loop's row cannot be written), and answering the request after the claim (the CLI waits for
  a fix's answer only briefly). Tests, failing first: TestAFixOnAPRWhoseSlotWasHandedBackClaimsOneAtTheReviewedHead,
  TestAFixWithoutAFreeSlotRefusesAndNamesTheRetry, TestAFixWhoseClaimCouldNotLoadTheSchemaSaysSo,
  TestAFixThatLosesItsFreeSlotEndsQuietly and TestAnAbortDuringTheClaimHandsTheSlotBack; with them
  TestAFixWhoseClaimFailsHandsTheSlotBack, TestAPinnedPRWithoutASlotHoldsAutofixButNotMagnumFix,
  TestAFixOnASlotlessPRWhoseHeadKeptTheVerdictClaimsAtItsHead and
  TestAFixOnASlotlessPRWhoseHeadMovedRefusesAndClaimsNothing (its pool's only slot evictable, so an eviction
  started before the refusal would show). Mutations that drop the free-slot check, the move to held, the
  release, the pinned refusal or the stood claim, or that look for a slot before the head check, each fail
  one.

## Scheduling

- **No backfill.** PRs open before the first sync are `baseline` until their next push or a manual
  `magnum review`. Rejected: reviewing every open PR on first start (a usage-limit event).
- **Throttle**: 5 min quiet after a push, 30 min between rounds per PR (2 h for drafts), coalesce to
  the latest head, a daily cap, `magnum review` overrides all of it.
- **Burst-aware quiet period** (2026-10-04): three or more pushes within 30 minutes switch the quiet
  period to 15 minutes, because agent-driven PRs commit in bursts and a round started between two
  commits is stale when it lands.
- **A push during the reviewer stage restarts the round in place** (same sessions re-prompted on the
  new head with the `restart` prompt, reviewers interrupted with Esc, shell panes with ctrl+c, at most
  `max_round_restarts` = 2 per round); **a push during the judge's turn lets the round finish**, the
  posted review gets "_Reviewed <sha>; N commits arrived during the review, re-review follows._"
  appended, and the delta re-review skips the 30-minute spacing (2026-10-04). A head that is an
  ancestor of the target is not a push. Rejected: aborting on every push (frequent pushers would never get a review) and
  waiting for a long quiet period (every PR waits, reviews are still stale when they land).
- **Re-reviews run the judge at `high` effort and confine the Claude reviewer to the delta**;
  the first review stays at `xhigh` (2026-10-04; measured 33–40 min rounds).
- **A paused agent kind blocks only rounds that use it.** Codex capacity counts the Codex roles a
  round actually runs.
- **`skip_paths` on a watch** skips PRs whose changed files all match (docs-only PRs); file lists come
  from one REST call per head, cached. `magnum ignore` is the manual version (mute, kill the round,
  free the slot). Comment-only code changes cannot be detected without reading the diff and stay a
  manual `I`.
- **The Codex budget gates dispatch** (2026-10-04; Codex's weekly limit went from 0% to 99% in 26 hours
  and the daemon had no signal for it). The health tick reads the newest rate-limit snapshot in Codex's
  own session files at most once a minute (`[usage] codex_home`) and records it in kv. At `codex_soft`
  (80%) a first review whose roles run Codex waits with a gate reason; re-reviews, continues and
  `magnum review` still run, because they finish work already promised. At `codex_hard` (95%) the kinds
  backed by Codex pause through the tool-pause path (reason `budget_cap`, one urgent toast), and the
  budget check, not the pause's expiry, lifts it once the budget is below the cap or the window reset.
  Rejected: counting rounds ourselves (Codex knows its account's usage, including the user's own
  sessions) and stopping everything at the soft cap (re-reviews of PRs in flight matter most).
- **Requested reviews run without delay** (2026-10-04). A review request from a person is an ask for a
  review now, yet it waited out the same quiet period, re-review interval and daily cap as a push. A
  ReviewRequestedEvent on the PR's timeline (read with Details, `timelineItems(REVIEW_REQUESTED_EVENT,
  last: 10)`) for the poll login, any posting identity's login (an App's in both its GraphQL and REST
  forms) or a team the watch lists in `request_teams`, and a draft marked ready for review, start a round
  `[daemon] request_debounce` (1m) after the later of the request and the last push, skipping the quiet and
  burst quiet periods, both re-review intervals, the delta threshold and the daily cap. A request is
  edge-triggered: it is recorded once (`pr.<id>.request_at`, `request_by`, `pr.review_requested`), counts
  only when newer than the repository's first sync, the build's first start and the PR's last round start,
  and a review of the head posted after it answers it (a request during a round that covers the head
  starts nothing more). A ready transition on a head already reviewed starts nothing. The wait reads
  `requested by alice → 14:05` (or `→ now`). Rejected: reacting to the pending `reviewRequests` list (GitHub
  keeps a user's request until that user reviews and drops the App's once it reviews, so presence cannot
  tell a new ask from an old one) and marking the PR forced (that also overrides mutes, quiet hours, the
  watch's filters and the budget's soft cap).
- **Small deltas wait for more** (2026-10-04). Every non-trivial push re-ran three agents, also for a
  two-line fix. The compare call the trivial-delta check makes (one per head change, reviewed commit to
  head) also measures the delta: changed lines that are code, judged line by line by the same classifier
  (comments, blank lines, whitespace moves and documentation count nothing; reordered code counts), and
  added, renamed or copied files (`pr.<id>.delta`). An automatic re-review runs after the quiet period once
  the delta reaches `[daemon] rereview_min_lines` (30) or adds a file; a smaller one waits for more pushes, at
  most `rereview_max_wait` (2h) after its first unreviewed push. A file without a complete patch, a failed
  compare and a request or `magnum review` skip the threshold; 0 turns it off and a `[[watch]]` can override
  both keys. The wait reads `small delta 8/30 lines → 16:40`. Rejected: GitHub's additions and deletions
  (comments and docs would count) and summing per-push deltas (one compare of the reviewed commit and the
  head is exact and costs no extra call).
- **The daily cap counts automatic rounds only** (2026-10-04). Requested rounds and `magnum review` record
  their start (the re-review interval and request edge read it) but never count against
  `max_rounds_per_pr_per_day`, whose default rises from 6 to 12 now that it limits only what the daemon
  starts on its own. A refunded requested round restores the previous start, so its request runs again.
  Rejected: a separate cap for requested rounds (a person asked for each of them).
- **Idle agents of reviewed PRs are parked** (2026-10-04; 21 agent processes, about 2.8 GB, idled 10.8
  hours on average). Once every live agent of a `reviewed` PR has been idle (not working or blocked) for
  `[daemon] park_idle_after` (2h) its sessions are parked on the heavy worker under the PR's
  reservation; the next round resumes them as after any park. Pinned or held slots and a keystroke within
  `human_cooldown` keep them. Rejected: `min_warm` as the threshold (it governs slot eviction; 30 minutes
  is too short for agents that keep a conversation for the next push).
- **Idle agents of PRs that wait long are parked too** (2026-10-05, after two `rereview_pending` PRs held 8
  live agents idle for up to 2 hours under `magnum pause`). A `queued` or `rereview_pending` PR is parked
  like a reviewed one, after `park_idle_after` of idling, when the wait the last dispatch recorded for it
  (`pr.<id>.wait`) is `magnum pause` or an infrastructure pause, a drain for a restart, the daily round cap,
  or any wait that ends more than `park_idle_after` from now; the next round resumes the sessions. A wait
  without an end (the next dispatch, a slot, capacity, a mute) is not long. A pinned or held slot still
  keeps its agents whatever the PR waits for, since a person works there, so a wait on a pinned or held
  slot never parks. Rejected: parking every waiting PR after `park_idle_after` (a quiet period or the
  next dispatch ends within minutes, and a resume costs the round its warm agents).
- **A push that edits the review agents' instructions is not docs, and a comment line that interpolates is
  code** (2026-10-09, amends "A push of comments, whitespace or docs is not re-reviewed"). `docDeltaPath`
  counted every `.md` file as docs. A push that only edited an `AGENTS.md`, a `CLAUDE.md`,
  `CLAUDE.local.md` or a page under `.claude/` or `.codex/` therefore settled as reviewed with no round.
  The gates of a standing automatic approval run only when magnum reviews a new head
  (`standingGateRefusal`), so the operator's approval kept counting on a head that changed what steers the
  review agents, which `agentConfigRefusal` exists to refuse. Also, the comments class keeps no string
  state, so a `#` or `//` line inside a string counted as a comment although its interpolation runs: a
  Ruby heredoc line `# #{...}`, a Python f-string line `# {...}`, a JavaScript template line `// ${...}`,
  a GitHub Actions `run:` line `# ${{ ... }}`. Now (1) `checkDelta` hands `assessDelta` a predicate built
  on `agentConfigPath` (the gate's own list: the instruction files at any depth and the project config of
  the configured and built-in kinds), and a file it matches is never trivial. The push's size is unchanged
  (a Markdown file counts no code lines). The log says "delta: the push changes the review agents'
  instructions; the push is re-reviewed" with the path as the gate names it. `TrivialDelta` and
  `MeasureDelta`, which know no agent kinds, are unchanged. (2) A comment-looking line that holds its file
  type's interpolation token is code: `#{` for `.rb`, `.rake`, `.gemspec`, `.rbi`, `.erb`, `Gemfile` and
  `Rakefile`; `{` for `.py`; `${` for `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.kt`, `.sh` and `.tf`; `{{` for
  `.yml` and `.yaml` (it covers `${{ }}` and a Helm or Jinja `{{ }}`). Such a line leaves no block comment
  open after it. The base-merge measure of the PR's own diff (`ownChangedLines`) shares the rule. Plain
  comment lines stay trivial, and so does a Go comment that names `${HOME}`. Kept: such a push waits as a
  small delta (0 lines) for its round, at most `rereview_max_wait`, and the standing approval stands until
  that round decides. Rejected: tracking string state per language (heredoc terminators, triple quotes,
  template literals: a parser per language for a check whose doubt already means a re-review). Also
  rejected: a watch setting for the agents' files. The earlier rejection of docs that drive behaviour as a
  built-in exception still holds for a repository's own prompts, but these files steer magnum's own agents
  and its auto-approval gate, so they follow the gate's list.
- **A review agent's pane cannot act for the operator** (2026-10-09). `magnum approve --as`, `unapprove`,
  `mute`, `ignore` and `pause` act for the operator. A review agent reads the PR and runs any command it
  chooses, so text in a PR could steer it to approve as the operator, withdraw the operator's approval, or
  stop reviews of that PR or of every PR. These commands now refuse to run (exit 1, "run this from your
  own terminal: a review agent's shell cannot act for the operator") when MAGNUM_REPORT_DIR or
  MAGNUM_PR_URL is set. magnum sets these variables only in the panes of a PR's review workspace (engine
  paneEnv). `magnum post-review` and `magnum db-lock`, which the roles run, are not refused. This is
  defense in depth on top of the 2026-10-04 trade-off "Plain codex and claude binaries run without
  approval prompts by default": an agent can unset the variables, and what limits it is still magnum's
  design. Kept: approve without --as and request-changes post as the PR's posting identity and stay
  allowed. Rejected: refusing every magnum command in a pane (the roles need post-review and db-lock, and
  the read-only commands help them); detecting a pane through the process tree (herdr panes run ordinary
  shells, which the operator uses too).
- **A model switch cut short backs out of its own dialog** (2026-10-09, after an audit: SwitchModel
  pressed Esc on Claude's "Switch model?" dialog only on its timeout path, so a switch whose ctx ended
  during the poll left the dialog open, and the session's next prompt was refused as blocked). After the
  `/model` command is typed, any return with ctx ended reads the screen once more on
  context.WithoutCancel. It presses Esc when detectSwitchDialog shows the dialog. It records the switch
  (switched) when the status line already names the new model, which needs that model's name to be known
  (verify). The observer still leaves the pane alone until then. Rejected: polling until the dialog is
  gone (the caller's ctx has ended; a single read and one key keep the exit short).
- **Triage keeps every role where magnum approves as the operator** (2026-10-09, amends "Triage of small
  diffs"). Triage asks a model that reads the PR's untrusted diff which reviewers to drop, and the model
  may drop every role but the judge. MissingReports lists only the roles the round ran, so the gate that
  requires every reviewer to be heard found nothing missing. A small PR could then get the operator's
  automatic approval after a round of the judge alone. Now, when AutoApproveFor gives an approver for the
  PR's repository, triage asks no model, every role runs, and an Info log line says why. Elsewhere triage
  is unchanged. Rejected: counting the roles triage dropped in MissingReports (the gate would then refuse
  every triaged round, so on those repositories triage would only cost a model call).
- **A poll reads only its repository's open rows and the rows its radar lists** (2026-10-09). pollRepo
  listed and decoded every PR row the repository ever had on each tick. It uses only the radar's rows and
  the open rows, which a PR missing from the radar is confirmed against. Now it reads `gh_state = 'OPEN'
  OR node_id IN <the radar's node ids>` (new store.PRFilter fields GHOpen and OrNodeIDs, through
  json_each; engine.pollRows). A reopened PR is on the radar, so it keeps its row and returns to its
  state; a closed, merged, unknown or released row off the radar is no longer read. On 2,000 rows with 100
  open: 10.9 MB and 115,600 allocations per call become 0.49 MB and 5,700, about 7x faster (49-78 ms to
  7-9 ms under load). Rejected: an index on gh_state (a migration, and the repository's rows are already
  found through (repo_id, number)).

- **A review request on a manual repository says that no round starts** (2026-10-12). `recordRequest`
  wrote "the next round skips the timing rules and the daily cap" for every pending request, but a
  repository in its watch's `manual_repos` starts no round on a request by design (eligibility rejects the
  PR); an author asked for a review after a push and the event promised a round that never came, with
  nobody told (1 of 19 requests in a day). Now a pending request there says "manual repository: no round
  starts by itself; `magnum review <owner/repo#N>` runs one" (the event's data carries `manual`), and a
  person's request (a draft marked ready is no one's ask) raises one info toast, "magnum: <owner/repo>#<N>:
  review requested by <login> (manual repository)", keyed by the PR and the request's time. Dispatch is
  unchanged: whether a request should override `manual_repos` is the operator's call.

- **A park that fails backs off, and its cause is recorded once** (2026-10-14, amends "Idle agents of
  reviewed PRs are parked"). A failed `Agents.Park` was logged at info and tried again on the next tick: on
  talkable#11932 the park of the `claude-fix` session failed on every tick for 37 hours with "shell not idle
  after 10s (foreground: 2.1.296)", 1,434 tries (36% of the window's daemon log) and about 2,868 ctrl+c into
  a live Claude pane, long after the fix loop had ended, and nothing told the operator. Now the next try
  waits twice the last wait, starting from the tick interval (two ticks after the first failure, then four,
  eight and so on), up to 12 hours. A round started since (the PR's `last_round_started_at`) or a change of
  its live sessions (their ids and last prompts, not their agents' statuses, which the park's own ctrl+c can
  move) resets the wait, and a park that works forgets the failures and records `pr.parked` as before. The
  first failure of a cause records `pr.park_failed` (warn) with its class and the wait: `quit_timeout` (an
  agent's pane was no idle shell after its ctrl+c: `agents.ErrBusy` with herdr's timeout), `busy` (a run, an
  agent or a pane of the PR at work), `herdr` or `error`. Later failures of the same class record nothing
  until it changes. The backoff lives in the daemon's memory: a restart tries at once and records the cause
  again. The Codex-flag release, which parks through the same call and also tried every tick, shares it. A
  fix role's session is not exempt. The fix job's settle neither parks the fixer nor keeps it live on
  purpose: it leaves the session as a round leaves its reviewers, and "the fixer's conversation persists
  across cycles and loops" holds through a park, since the next fix job resumes the parked conversation and
  `magnum open --role claude-fix` restores it to read. The pane the operator reads is kept already: a loop
  that leaves findings to them ends in `needs_attention`, which the idle park never touches, and a keystroke
  within `human_cooldown` or `magnum open`'s pin keeps it as for any role. Rejected: exempting the fixer,
  since `Park` parks a PR whole, so every agent of a PR with a live fixer would stay up until the PR closes,
  on every own PR under `autofix = "own"`. Keeping the backoff in the registry, for at most one more try and
  event per restart.

- **`magnum resume --tool codex` overrules a stale Codex reading** (2026-10-15; three re-reviews waited at
  the hard cap behind the last session's 97% while the operator had switched to a Codex account with the
  whole week left, and `magnum resume`, which the wait's hint named, lifts only the automation pause). The
  budget comes from Codex's newest session file, so after a switch of the account it stays the old
  account's until a Codex session runs, which the pause prevents; and a `--tool codex` resume was undone at
  the next budget check, which re-read the same snapshot. Now a budget-cap pause lifted by `magnum resume
  --tool codex` (or `all`, through the daemon or offline) records `usage.codex_overruled_at`
  (engine.KVUsageCodexOverruledAt): both caps read as no reading until a snapshot stamped after it
  (budgetLevel is OK, so neither the hard cap's pause nor the soft cap's hold applies), the cap's toast is
  forgotten so a pause from the next reading toasts at once, and the next snapshot, from the next Codex
  session magnum or the operator runs, ends the overrule (settleOverrule) and is judged as usual: at the
  cap, the pause returns. The daemon takes the CLI's offline mark over at startup (loadBudgetOverrule).
  The resume's answer and a `tool.resumed` event say "the Codex budget caps wait for Codex's next
  reading"; `magnum status` says it on the codex line (`overruled_at` in the JSON) and in the pause's fix,
  and a kind's wait hint names `magnum resume --tool <kind>` instead of `magnum resume`. Rejected:
  reading the account from the login file (Codex can keep its credentials in the keyring, and the file's
  stamp says nothing about which account a session file's limits belong to); a Codex probe turn to
  refresh the reading (it spends, and it is what the resumed round does anyway); discarding the snapshot
  on resume (the status would show no gauge, and a restart would read the same file again).

- **Every tenth re-review of a PR is a full pass** (2026-10-15). After its first review nothing read a
  long-lived PR whole again: a re-review reads the commits since the last review in the judge's
  conversation, and a judge whose session is gone reads the earlier reviews, then only the new commits
  too (the recovery prompt). talkable#11483 (268 files, 24k added lines, open since April) had about 38
  rounds; on 2026-10-13 a colleague's whole-branch review found three latent defects in PR code outside
  the delta 90 minutes after magnum's re-review of that head said "no new problems". Now `[pipeline]
  full_pass_every` (default 10, 0 = off) makes the Nth automatic re-review, counted since the PR's first
  review or its last full pass, a full pass: the sessions are parked and every role starts fresh as
  `--fresh` does, the round runs as a recovery (its runs keep kind `recovery`), the reviewers get their
  first-review prompts at their full effort, triage judges the whole PR as for a first review, and the
  judge's own pass and recovery prompt carry the full-pass clause (`full_pass: true`): review the full PR
  diff again as a first review does (section 2 of the skill), then decide every earlier thread under the
  reply contract, earlier findings still counted, a finding the earlier reviews missed titled `(missed
  earlier)`, the body headed `Re-review <a> → <b> (full pass):`. The count reads the runs table: the PR's
  rereview and recovery rounds whose judge posted a review on a head other than the one reviewed before
  them (so no same-head, reply or CI-red round), numbered after the last full pass, which
  `pr.<id>.full_pass` records with its judge run and round when it posts (`pr.<id>.full_pass_round` marks
  one in flight, for the status comment and a continue of a paused one). Existing PRs count their past
  re-reviews, so talkable#11483 gets its full pass at its next automatic full re-review. A delta check counts
  but never becomes one (the small push keeps its check, and the next full re-review is the full pass); a
  forced or requested round counts, since no run says who asked for it, but never becomes one, nor does a
  re-review of the same head, a reply round or a CI check; the soft Codex budget cap holds a full pass as
  any automatic full re-review. `round.full_pass` says why one runs, `engine.round_start` says `re-review
  (full pass)`, the card's last round `full pass` and the status comment `In progress (full pass)`.
  `magnum review --full <ref>` asks for one by hand (`pr.<id>.fresh` = `full`). Rejected: a full pass by
  PR size or age alone (a large PR with two rounds needs none); a fresh judge with the delta scope (that
  is the recovery round, which reads the new commits only); a `full_pass` value of `runs.kind` (a 0027
  rebuild of runs, findings and declines for one flag); a kv counter that only automatic rounds increment
  (it would start at 0, so a PR with 38 rounds would wait 10 more re-reviews).
- **Every fifth re-review audits what no round probed** (2026-10-15). A review of the full-pass ideas by
  Codex: once the PR's evidence map ("The judge says what it examined") says which areas no round read or
  probed and which changed since one did, a full pass that reads the whole PR again is the expensive way
  to reach them, and a re-review never does, as it reads the delta. `[pipeline] audit_every`
  (`Config.Pipeline.AuditEvery`, default 5, 0 = off, a negative value refused) makes the Nth automatic
  re-review of a PR whose map holds `unknown` or `stale` entries an audit pass (engine audit.go), counted
  as the full pass counts (the runs table, no migration: rereview and recovery rounds that posted on a
  head other than their `prev_reviewed_sha`) after the later of the last full pass and the last audit
  pass, which kv `pr.<id>.audit_pass` records with its judge run, round and target when it posts
  (`pr.<id>.audit_round` marks one in flight, for a continue of a paused one and for the record; the next
  round's start resets it). The dispatcher decides it after `fullPassDue` (`roundJob.audit`), never with
  a full pass: when both are due the full pass runs, and an audit pass, a recovery that posts on a new
  head, counts toward the full pass's count. A forced or requested round, a post-merge review, a delta
  check, a re-review of the same head, a reply round and a CI check never become one, nor does a round on
  the reviewed head. prepare picks its areas (`pipeline.RoundInput.Audit`, `AuditArea`): at most three
  `unknown` or `stale` entries ranked by the words of their path, symbol and behaviour (an irreversible
  write: delete, update, restore, send and the like; authorization; money; an optional branch: nil,
  empty, fallback and the like), then a file the reviewed head's `prepass.json` lists, an unknown entry
  before a stale one and the oldest first; and the oldest `probed` entry on a file the pushes touched
  since the last audit or full pass (else the map's oldest head; one `gitx.ChangedBetween`), marked
  `rotation`, to run again. With no area left the round is an ordinary re-review. startSessions parks
  every session and starts every role fresh with a `round.audit_pass` event naming why and how many
  areas; the judge is a fresh judge (`ColdJudge`), so the round runs as a recovery whose reviewers
  re-review the delta at their rereview effort and whose judge works at its rereview effort. The round
  writes the areas to `audit.json` in its report directory (pipeline audit.go; the paths and behaviours
  come from the PR, so the prompt names only the file), and `judge-recovery.md` gets one clause
  (`agents.JudgeData.AuditFile`, `AuditAreas`): probe each through its real entry point with a control,
  one Checks line per probe, each probe that passes a `probed` entry of `evidence_file`; an area it could
  not probe is a lead, never a finding (no finding says an area is unknown); then review the commits and
  decide the earlier threads under the reply contract. `engine.round_start` says `re-review (audit pass)`
  with `audit_pass` in its data, and the card's last round says `audit pass` (`tui.RoundWhy.AuditPass`,
  mirrored in `magnum tui --json`). Rejected: coverage from the findings and Checks alone, which never say
  what passed; a method-level parser for what to audit, where the map's files and behaviours are enough
  to start; more whole-PR passes instead of focused ones; a fresh judge alone with the reviewers' old
  sessions kept (an audit is rare, and fresh sessions read the probes without the earlier rounds'
  conclusions).

- **A full pass also follows churn and age, overrides a delta check, and starts blind** (2026-10-15). A
  Codex review of the full-pass design found two gaps and a third point. Rounds measure how often the
  whole-PR view was lost, not how much the code changed: one round can replace a subsystem and ten can fix
  spelling. A delta check counted toward `full_pass_every` but never became a full pass, so a PR that only
  ever got small pushes put its full pass off without end. And the full pass started every session fresh,
  but the own-pass prompt had the judge read the earlier reviews first, so the fresh session took on the old
  framing before it read the code. Now a PR keeps a baseline, its last full pass (`pr.<id>.full_pass`, which
  gains the base, the files and the lines) or else its first review (`pr.<id>.review_baseline`; a PR
  reviewed before the rule takes its next review), with the PR's size then: changed files and added plus
  deleted lines, lockfiles and the watch's `related_ignore` left out, from `git diff --numstat` in the
  round's checkout at settle. Every review that posts on new commits adds them to `pr.<id>.full_pass_churn`
  (lines summed, touched paths as a union of at most 500, then only the count grows), measured as the
  re-review reads them: `prev_reviewed_sha...head` through GitHub's comparison, or, after a base merge or a
  rebase, the change of the PR's own diff before and after (`compareOwnDiffs`, which now keeps each file's
  lines); a comparison file's own line count (`github.FileDelta.Lines`) covers a patch GitHub left out. The
  churn counts what the posted reviews read, not the pending push. `fullPassDue` fires, in this order, on
  `magnum review --full`, `full_pass_every`, churn lines reaching the larger of `full_pass_lines` (500) and a
  quarter of the baseline's lines, touched files reaching the larger of `full_pass_files` (10) and a quarter
  of the baseline's files, or `full_pass_after` (168h) since the baseline of a large PR (50 files or 2,000
  lines then); 0 turns each rule off, the quarter and the large-PR sizes are fixed in code. A due full pass
  clears the delta classification before the roles are selected (`planFullPass`), so the round runs in
  full; a same-head, reply, CI-red or requested round keeps its scope. `round.full_pass` gains `rule`, and
  `engine.round_start` gains `full_pass_reason`. The own pass of a full pass is blind: it reviews the full
  diff as a first review does (sections 1, 2 and 4), names no earlier review, former login, thread or
  reply-contract decision, and leaves them to the candidates phase, whose recovery prompt lists the earlier
  reviews with the full-pass clause and says the own pass came before them; without an own pass
  (`judge_own_pass = "after"`) the order stays. Rejected: counting files outside the last full pass's delta
  (a full pass covers the whole diff, so every file is inside it); the count of fixed findings (the findings
  table records posted or rejected only, with no fixed state to count); charging the pending push to the
  churn (it needs a measure at dispatch, and the review that crosses the line is followed by the full pass
  at the next push).
- **An approval rests on a whole-PR read** (2026-10-15). A re-review reads the commits since the last
  review, and its clean verdict posted APPROVE, so after several re-reviews an approval rested on one whole
  read long ago and a chain of deltas, each read on its own. On talkable#11483 magnum approved after a delta
  re-review of the fix; a colleague's whole-branch round then found a second path to the same defect, and
  the operator asked for a full review, not a delta, before magnum approves. Now `[pipeline]
  approve_after_full_pass` (default 2, 0 = off, a negative value refused) is the number of re-reviews since
  the PR's baseline (its last full pass, else its first review; `rereviewsSinceFullPass`) at or above which
  an approval needs a full pass first. A round that holds (`approvalHoldDue` at the round's setup,
  `pr.<id>.approval_hold_round` while it runs, so a continue holds too; `round.approval_hold`, and
  `approval_hold` in `engine.round_start`) gets `pipeline.RoundInput.HoldApproval`: its no-findings event is
  COMMENT, and the rereview and recovery prompts say that a clean verdict posts as a comment and a full pass
  of the whole PR follows, with the body line `A full pass of the whole PR follows before approval.` after
  the verdict line (the prompt's words, not the skill's). When it posts with the verdict `clean` (the
  judge's stored result), `onPosted` records the held review (`pr.<id>.approval_hold`) and forces the PR
  as `magnum review --full` does (`forceReview`, as the fix loop forces its re-review, never seeing the
  operator's stalemates), so the next dispatch runs a full pass of the same head with every role fresh,
  `fullPassDue`'s rule `approval`, whose clean verdict approves and which is the new baseline; any later
  review drops the record. The hold applies to automatic and requested rounds alike (a delta check, a
  recovery, an audit pass, a re-review of the same head) and to the operator's own PR, whose clean verdict
  is a comment already, so the full pass still follows; a full pass, `magnum review --full`, a post-merge
  review, a reply round, a CI check, a dry run and an eval replay never hold. With the default, one round of
  fixes after the first review approves on its delta. Auto-approval as the operator waits on a held review
  (`autoGateRefusal`, as a wait that withdraws no standing approval). The status comment's posted line adds
  `A full pass follows before approval.` while the full pass waits, the full pass shows as `Full pass before
  approval of` with `In progress (full pass)`, and the card's last round says `full pass (before
  approval)` (`tui.RoundWhy.BeforeApproval`, `before_approval` in `magnum tui --json`). Rejected: a full
  pass before every approval (the one-fix path would cost a whole review twice); the judge reviewing the
  whole PR itself in the round that would approve (one reused session, while the reviewers see only the
  delta).

- **A full pass at least daily while a PR moves** (2026-10-15, amends "A full pass also follows churn and
  age"; the same evening the default became `"12h"`, so the first push of a workday after an evening's
  pass gets a whole read). The age rule ran a full pass once a week, and only on a PR of 50 files or 2,000 lines; the
  operator found a week too rare. `full_pass_after` now defaults to `"24h"` and applies to a PR of any
  size: an automatic re-review a day or more after the baseline (the last full pass, else the first review)
  runs as a full pass, however small the push, and the reason reads "24h since the first review
  (full_pass_after 24h)". The size floor and its constants went, since a small PR's full pass costs little
  and the rule is about time, not size. Rejected: a size floor as a key (two knobs for one wish), and a
  full pass on every push after a day (one a day is the floor, the churn rules add the rest).

- **A forced fresh round runs a due full pass, and a same-head round is never the baseline** (2026-10-16,
  amends "Every tenth re-review of a PR is a full pass" and "A full pass also follows churn and age").
  talkable#11483's round 46 was a `magnum review --fresh` of its reviewed head after round 45's judge died
  at the codex-cli bootstrap: the PR had 34 re-reviews since its first review and never a full pass, yet
  `fullPassDue` excluded every forced and same-head round, so the round ran no full pass, and its judge
  verified a kept-tiers fix on an empty delta right before a colleague found the third defect in that
  restore's tier handling (Operations: "A fix is probed on the shapes its writers leave"). The same round
  then became the PR's review baseline (`pr.<id>.review_baseline`, since the PR's first review came before
  the churn rules), so the age rule counted from a round that read no new commit. Now a forced round with
  the fresh flag (`magnum review --fresh`, `pr.<id>.fresh` = `1` on a forced PR) runs the full pass when any
  rule makes one due (`full_pass_every`, `full_pass_lines`, `full_pass_files`, `full_pass_after`, in that
  order), on a new head or the reviewed one, so it decides as an automatic re-review would, and the reason
  names the rule as before and ends `, on magnum review --fresh` ("re-review 35 since the first review
  (full_pass_every 10), on magnum review --fresh"). A forced round without `--fresh`, a plain same-head
  re-review, a reply round and a CI check stay excluded. And `settleFullPass` keeps nothing from a round of
  the reviewed head (`prev_reviewed_sha` = target, from the round's PR as it was at setup, no new field)
  that is no full pass: the baseline moves only on a full pass, or, when none exists, on the first review
  (of a PR reviewed before the churn rules, its first review of new commits since). New tests
  TestAForcedFreshRoundRunsADueFullPass (the 11483 shape with `full_pass_every` 10: a full pass of the
  reviewed head, its reason, the full pass record and no review baseline; `full_pass_lines` after 600 lines
  of churn, the churn gone after the full pass; `full_pass_after` 13 hours after the first review; none due:
  a fresh round of every role, no full pass), TestAForcedRoundWithoutFreshRunsNoFullPass (the same-head
  round and a forced round of a new head, then the automatic full pass) and
  TestASameHeadRoundNeverBecomesTheBaseline (without a baseline neither a fresh nor a same-head round makes
  one and the next review of new commits does; with one it stays). Rejected: a full pass on every forced
  round (a `magnum review` of a small head of that PR would re-read 24k lines); the count and the age alone
  on a fresh round, leaving the churn rules to the next automatic re-review (a forced fresh round and an
  automatic one should decide the same way).

- **An idle agent parks once keeping it live stops paying: 15 minutes after the round, the judge at
  `judge_fresh_after`, drafts too** (2026-10-19, asked for by the operator: "stop and resume agents as
  needed"; amends "Idle agents of reviewed PRs are parked" and "Idle agents of PRs that wait long are parked
  too"). The machine swapped (155 GB of footprint on 48 GB, swap 50.3 of 51.2 GB, pressure level warn), and
  magnum's panes held 13.4 GB, 9.2 GB of it in 47 idle agents of PRs no round used: reviewed PRs idling
  under the 2-hour park (4.9 GB), drafts after their review (1.8 GB, `ineligible`, which never parked),
  PRs that need attention (1.0 GB) and pinned PRs (1.5 GB); over 7 days idle agents were live 1,617
  agent-hours. Warmth is worth little to a Claude role: a resume adds 3-11 s (p50) to a round's first prompt,
  about 150 Claude round resumes in 14 days lost 1, and 54 of 57 claude-review reuses came after the
  5-minute prompt cache had expired anyway. A live Codex judge is worth more: all 57 of its live reuses came
  within 90 minutes, a fresh Codex launch dies at its first prompt 7-10% of the time, and the cold-judge
  rule starts it fresh after `judge_fresh_after` anyway. The next round of a PR comes within 15 minutes 21%
  of the time, within an hour 39%. Now a session's threshold is `[daemon] park_idle_after`, whose default
  drops from 2h to 15m, and for a judge role `[pipeline] judge_fresh_after` when that is longer (read from
  the key, never a second constant; `"0"`, always resume, leaves the judge `park_idle_after`). Its idle
  clock starts at the later of its own last activity (start, last status change, last prompt) and the end
  of the PR's last round, fix job or whiteboard job, which a new key records before the job drops its
  reservation (`pr.<id>.work_ended`, written by `reservedRound`, the fix job and the whiteboard job; no
  migration): a reviewer idle while the judge works is not idle until the round ends, and the fix cycle or
  the whiteboard that `launch` starts after the round's reservation is gone never meets a park in that
  gap. A PR with no record yet (the first run after this change) counts from the latest end of a run of its
  last round, else that round's start. A park job is planned at a tick and runs on the heavy worker, so it
  never takes the PR once a round, fix job or whiteboard job of the PR ended after its plan
  (`reserveParkWork`, which checks the end under the reservation's lock): taking it in that gap would
  refuse the fix cycle's start and end the loop needing attention. The park is two steps. While some live
  session of the PR is not past its threshold, the sessions past theirs that have a conversation to resume
  park alone, through the new `agents.Manager.ParkSessions`: Park's guards (no active run of the PR, a
  fresh snapshot, an agent working or blocked refused, and the pane of a selected session whose agent
  herdr no longer lists refused when it runs something), a refusal of a session without a conversation to
  resume (the engine selects by the same test: a session id, an agent role, a kind whose `session_source`
  is not `"none"`), then Quit's ctrl+c and wait until the pane is an idle shell. It ends as the PR's park
  ends, which closes the workspace before it retires the sessions: the session's own pane is closed first
  (a fresh check that only the shell is in its foreground; never another pane, and a workspace the close
  empties goes too), herdr dropping the agent with it, and only then is the session parked. A parked row
  whose pane herdr still showed with the quit conversation would be restored as live by the next start's
  `Recover`, which runs before the startup reconcile closes leftover panes, and the next round would reuse
  that row without a launch. The close and the retire run on a context a stop cannot cut, bounded at
  10 s, so a stop never lands between them; a crash after the close leaves a live row without a pane,
  which the observer turns into an ordinary lost session, still resumable. There is no polling barrier
  like the cold judge's (`quitAgentGone`): that one exists because a start follows its quit in the same
  reservation, which an early park never does. A pane the check refuses (something runs there) or herdr
  fails to close leaves the session parked with its pane for a later `closeRetiredPanes` (the next tick's
  or the reconcile's): the only window left, the same as the PR's park's, accepted for the same reason,
  since the agent had already exited when its pane became an idle shell. There is no hard mode: an agent that
  does not quit stays live and waits for the PR's park. Each session's early park writes its begin, ok and
  fail (`pr.session_park_begin`, `pr.session_parked`, `pr.session_park_failed`, info), and a batch where
  one session fails still returns, records and closes the panes of those it parked. A failure goes through
  the park's backoff, but the PR's park after an early park's failure starts the wait over
  (`parkBackoff.early`), so a reviewer that will not quit does not hold the judge's park and its hard mode
  past `judge_fresh_after`. The early park records `pr.parked` with the roles and `"partial":
  true`, names each role with the threshold it idled past, and says why each agent that stays stays
  ("parked claude-review, claude-simplify (park_idle_after 15m), idle since 14:05; codex-judge stays until
  judge_fresh_after (1h30m); ..."). Once every live session
  is past its own threshold, the PR's park runs as before (the `codex-review` shell retired, the workspace
  closed, the backoff and the hard park after a quit timeout), its event unchanged; `parkIdle` and the
  heavy worker's `parkJob` plan through one function (`planPark`), the job again under the PR's
  reservation. The PRs are those that parked before plus `ineligible` ones (a draft, a mute or a skip after
  its review; the next round resumes the sessions through `ensureAgent`); a session without a session id is
  never parked early and waits for the PR's park. The 2026-10-04 rejection of a short threshold ("too short
  for agents that keep a conversation for the next push") no longer holds: a park keeps the conversation,
  and the measured cost of resuming it is 3-11 s. `needs_attention` stays out (Codex's review of the draft):
  a session without a resumable id would be closed rather than parked, and the attention remedies send the
  operator to read that pane, so the fix-loop entry's "which the idle park never touches" stands; pinned
  and held slots keep their agents as before. Rejected: parking per session for every role with `Quit`
  alone, which lacks Park's guards and the pane close under the reservation; a polling barrier after the
  quit with a fallback that recorded the session lost when its pane would not close (tried in review: it
  changed how every start and recovery treat lost rows, and a restored or later lost row kept the
  marker that refused its legitimate agent); parking the reviewers as soon as the round
  ends (21% of next rounds come within 15 minutes, and a fix cycle or whiteboard often follows the round
