  since (a push that only merged the base), the review stands as `settlePush` says. The job keeps the head
  it works on (`fixJob.head`) apart from the review's commit. The guard, the pane's env, the loop row's
  `Since` and `Head`, and the slot's put-back use the head. The prompt keeps the review's URL and file,
  and the fix run's target is the head. The answer and the fix.start event say "of the review on f83d86a
  (the head 9e80a11 kept its verdict)". A head that kept the verdict but whose slot is still at the
  review's commit is refused before the fix starts, so the guard does not fail it. The board's `f` leaves
  the decision to the daemon when the head is the reviewed one. A loop's re-review that ends `replied`
  still ends the loop: that path is unchanged.
- **Whiteboards of reviewed PRs, written by a role after the review posts** (2026-10-14; amends "Magnum's
  Claude sessions run without MCP servers", 2026-10-07). The operator asked for a human-friendly way to read
  a reviewed PR, at their own choice: a review says what is wrong with a PR, not what the PR is. A dev.fast
  Whiteboard is that, an interactive document in Whiteboard Desktop with diagrams and code views pinned to
  the commits, explained by the authoring guide of `whiteboard mcp`; only a person's request to an agent
  made one before (one existed on this machine, written by hand through the MCP tools), and magnum had no
  code that named Whiteboard. Verified on 2026-10-14 with CLI 0.2.4: `whiteboard mcp` serves the authoring
  tools over stdio to one agent and needs a running server, Whiteboard Desktop or a headless `whiteboard
  server start` (the same `~/.dev` state directory); `whiteboard api whiteboard_status` exits 0 only then
  ("not ready in ~/.dev" otherwise) and `whiteboard app pick --session <id> --focus` opens one whiteboard in
  Desktop; `session_create` takes a `commits` target (`repositoryPath`, `head`, `base`), the PR's URL and
  `open: false`, which authors in the background without taking over Desktop, and its default
  `reuseExisting` returns the existing whiteboard of the same PR URL (`created: false`, `headMoved`);
  `session_set_target` moves a whiteboard to a new head and keeps its document; `repositoryPath` must be a
  git checkout, a `git worktree add` worktree works, the code views read it at the pinned commits, and a
  path that disappears later leaves the text and loses the views. Magnum's Claude sessions pass
  `--strict-mcp-config` and no `--mcp-config`, and a role's `args` come last in `Kind.Argv`, after the kind's
  `mcp_strict`, so the role's args carry one inline JSON string (`--mcp-config
  '{"mcpServers":{"whiteboard":{"command":"whiteboard","args":["mcp"]}}}'`) and magnum writes no file: the
  whiteboard role's session gets exactly one server, the one its args name, and the strict flag keeps the
  operator's own whiteboard plugin and every other server out. Now `[pipeline] whiteboard` (false) and
  `whiteboard_role` ("claude-whiteboard"; "" = no job, by hand or automatic), each with a `[[watch]]`
  override (`Config.WhiteboardFor`, `WhiteboardRoleFor`), and the built-in role `claude-whiteboard` (kind
  claude, opus, medium, `whiteboard.md`, no skill, 30m, no identity: it acts as the watch's poll identity,
  and a declared identity must be a gh one; validation refuses `runs`, `after`, `own_pass`,
  `max_session_rounds`, a judge, a fix or a shell role, and a watch's `roles` that names it). After a round
  that posted a review on a head, once the fix loop's hook ran, `whiteboardAfterRound` starts the job
  (`whiteboard.go`) when the PR is open, not muted, at the reviewed head and the head has no whiteboard;
  `magnum whiteboard <ref>` starts it by hand (`ReqWhiteboard`), `--open` and the board's `w` open the
  recorded one. Decided: a readiness check before every job (`whiteboard api whiteboard_status` through the
  daemon's runner, 15 s): a Whiteboard that is down is a skip (`whiteboard.skipped`, "Whiteboard is not
  running (start Whiteboard Desktop or `whiteboard server start`)"), never a wait, and the next posted
  review is the next chance; the job holds the PR under a reservation of its own (`roundHandle.whiteboard`)
  in the PR's slot, as the fix job does, with guard, start and wait steps, outside the daily cap, the
  interval, quiet hours and `max_concurrent_reviews`, and the wait code `whiteboard` reads "whiteboard in
  progress · <role>"; the record is the kv row `pr.<id>.whiteboard` (session, head, time, role), one
  whiteboard per PR that the next head's job moves with `session_set_target`, and a head that has its
  whiteboard gets no second (the request answers "<sha7> has its whiteboard <id>; magnum whiteboard <ref>
  --open opens it"); the writer's report is two lines, `session: <id>` and `head: <sha>`, or `failed: <one
  sentence>`, and anything else fails the run; a failure asks nothing of the operator (no attention, no
  toast: the whiteboard is optional), only `whiteboard.failed` says why; a push and `magnum abort` stop a
  job in progress as they stop a fixer, and a close on GitHub stops it too, unlike a fix job, because a
  whiteboard of a closed PR has no reader (`whiteboard.stopped`); a daemon restart fails the run it left at
  work ("whiteboard run lost in a restart"). The prompt carries URLs, SHAs and paths, never PR text: the
  writer reads the PR's title with gh in its pane, and the "Review" section it ends with quotes the posted
  review from its review.json. Rejected: magnum authoring the whiteboard itself (it has no model); the
  operator's whiteboard plugin (the strict MCP config keeps plugins out, and the plugin's tools are the
  operator's); a create from the PR URL alone, without a `commits` target (Whiteboard then fetches the PR
  itself, with Desktop's gh and git, in the slot's clone); a notification on failure (the whiteboard is
  optional); a whiteboard on every round (a reply round posts nothing).
- **A fixer's "needs your call" after a push toasts at once, one toast per loop cycle** (2026-10-14,
  amends "The fix loop: magnum fixes its own findings on your PRs"). A fix run pushed at 08:50:58Z and
  left one P1 for the operator; the settle recorded only `fix.needs_you`, and the toast and
  `needs_attention` came at 10:04:06Z, 73 minutes later, after the push's re-review, while the operator
  could have acted on the P1 meanwhile. A fixer that pushed nothing and left findings already asked at
  once (`fixAttention`). Now the settle's branch for a push with findings left to the author toasts too,
  as soon as the re-review is queued (`fixCallToast`: the urgent toast alone, the text of the no-push
  branch, whatever state a dispatch has moved the PR to since), and the event keeps saying that the
  re-review runs first. The PR itself goes to `needs_attention` only after the re-review, at the loop's
  end (`endLoopForAttention`), so a push of the operator's meanwhile, or a re-review that makes the call
  moot, changes nothing in the PR's state; when the re-review cannot be queued, `failFix`'s toast is the
  one. Decided: the toast's dedupe key is the loop cycle's own and the loop's end builds the same one, so
  the call is told once. The key used to end with the fix run's id, which the loop's end (`loopJob`: no
  run) lacks, so the end would have toasted the same call a second time; it is now
  `attention:<pr>:fix:<loop start>:<cycle>` (`fixAttentionKey`), and its window a day
  (`fixAttentionWindow`; `needsAttentionKeyed` takes the window), since a re-review can wait for hours
  and the 30 minutes of `attentionWindow` would let the end toast again (this one took 73). A second
  loop on the PR, or the next cycle, has another start or cycle and toasts as before. Rejected: moving
  the PR to `needs_attention` before the re-review (the forced re-review takes it out of that state
  again); one toast at the loop's end only (the delay above); a toast per event (the end's would
  repeat the first).
- **A refused fix names the slot's last error and the repair command** (2026-10-14). A by-hand
  `magnum fix` or whiteboard on a PR whose slot was broken answered "slot review11 is broken", with no
  cause and no command, where the dispatcher's wait for the same slot says "slot review11 is broken:
  <last error> (magnum slots repair review11)". Now one helper (`unusableSlotSentence`, in dispatch.go)
  builds that sentence and both use it: dispatch's slot gate and `prepareFix`, for a broken or lost
  slot. The slot's other states (busy, releasing) keep their short sentence, since `magnum slots repair`
  repairs neither. `prepareWhiteboard` is another change's and takes the helper after both have landed.
- **A whiteboard job yields the PR to the operator's review, fix and open requests** (2026-10-14; amends
  "Whiteboards of reviewed PRs"). The job held the PR for its whole run, 6 to 9 minutes in the first live
  runs, each started right after a review posted, which is when the operator acts on the review; meanwhile
  `magnum review` and `r`, `magnum fix` and `f` refused with "a round is already in progress (reviewed)" and
  `magnum open` and `o` answered "has a round running" and restored nothing. The whiteboard is optional, so
  the request wins. Now each of them, once every other refusal of its own passed, leaves a yield on the
  job's reservation (`roundStop.yields`, `yieldWhiteboard`) and cancels the job, as `magnum abort` leaves an
  order: the writer is interrupted, its run abandoned, the slot put back at the head, and
  `whiteboard.stopped` says "superseded by magnum review" ("by magnum fix", "by magnum open"); a writer
  whose run had ended is settled instead. The request stays in flight until the job let go of the PR, then
  goes back to the request dispatch still pending (`unreserveWhiteboard`, with a `Kick`), whose next pass
  answers it as if the job had never been, so it is answered once, with its own answer, and the tick never
  waits for the writer. A dry run of `magnum fix` stops nothing and says "would stop the whiteboard writer
  first". Rejected: the request's goroutine waiting for the job's end with a bound (the writer's quiet wait
  and the resync take up to half a minute, and the request would then run off the tick); answering the
  request at the stop (it would answer before its own path ran). `magnum abort` and `magnum ignore` keep
  their own stop. A CLI waits 30 s for a quick answer, which an interrupt, the quiet wait and the resync
  usually fit in; beyond that it reports the request pending and the daemon still answers it.
- **A restart stops a whiteboard writer that outlived the daemon** (2026-10-14; amends "Whiteboards of
  reviewed PRs"). `recoverWhiteboards` only abandoned the run and recorded `whiteboard.failed`, while herdr
  keeps the writer's pane across a crash, a drain that timed out or `daemon-restart --now`: the writer went
  on working in the slot with no reservation, and the next round could take the slot under it. Now the
  recovery stops it as the fix job's does (`stopFixerAt`): the run's role is interrupted on the PR until
  quiet (`interruptSessions`, `waitAgentsQuiet`), and the slot is put back at the run's head (`r.TargetSHA`)
  from a job built from the run and the PR's slot (`lostWhiteboardJob`); a slot no longer the PR's is
  logged, and one that cannot be put back is named in the event's message, as the fix job does.
- **`whiteboard.failed` names the writer's report, never its `failed:` sentence** (2026-10-14; amends
  "Whiteboards of reviewed PRs"). The event's message and the run's error carried the sentence after
  `failed:`, redacted and cut at 200 runes; the writer reads the PR, so the sentence can quote PR text, and
  logs and events never carry PR text. Now the message reads "<role> failed (its report: <path>)", the
  event's data keeps the report path as before, and the operator reads the sentence in the report.
- **`magnum whiteboard` is answered off the tick** (2026-10-14; amends "Whiteboards of reviewed PRs"). Its
  Whiteboard readiness check (`whiteboard api whiteboard_status`, 15 s) ran on the tick that handles
  requests, so a slow or hung `whiteboard` CLI held the daemon's tick for up to 15 s. Now the request runs on
  a goroutine of its own, as `magnum open` does (`requestWhiteboardAsync`): its refusals, the check, the
  reservation and the start, which completes the request with the same answers; it stays in flight
  meanwhile. The check after a posted review already runs on the round's goroutine.
- **A refused whiteboard names the slot's last error and the repair command** (2026-10-14; follows "A
  refused fix names the slot's last error and the repair command"). `prepareWhiteboard` refused a broken or
  lost slot with the bare state ("slot review1 is broken"); now it says what `prepareFix` and dispatch's
  wait say (`unusableSlotSentence`: "slot review1 is broken: <last error> (magnum slots repair review1)"),
  and the slot's other states keep their short sentence.
- **One `[pipeline] spend` key sets how hard every built-in role thinks** (2026-10-14). The operator
  rotates several Claude and Codex subscriptions: some weeks usage is tight and the roles should run at a
  lower effort, other weeks capacity is free and they should run at full effort, and each change meant
  editing several `effort` and `rereview_effort` keys of the user config (two were raised to `xhigh` on
  10-14, earlier runs had lowered claude-review and claude-simplify to `medium`). The operator asked for one
  toggle with three levels. Now `[pipeline] spend` takes `low`, `medium` (the default; "" counts as it) and
  `high` (`spendEffort`): `medium` keeps the efforts config.defaults.toml writes out; `high` makes every
  built-in role's `effort` and `rereview_effort` `xhigh`, the strongest level both Codex's
  `model_reasoning_effort` and Claude Code's `--effort` take (its help lists low, medium, high, xhigh,
  max; claude-judge already ran at `xhigh` through it); `low` takes each one notch down, `xhigh` to `high`
  and `high` to `medium`, with `medium` the floor and an unset value left unset. Load applies it after
  the role merge (`applySpend`, in `buildPipeline`) to each role named like a built-in role, for each of
  the two keys that no `[[role]]` block of the operator's set: the blocks of the user config and those of a
  base configuration of their own (`--config`, `MAGNUM_CONFIG`, a checkout's old `config.toml`) count as
  set, the embedded config.defaults.toml does not (`layer.builtin`), since it only writes the built-in
  values out. So an explicit key wins under every level, and a block that sets `effort` alone leaves its
  `rereview_effort` to the profile. A role that is not built in keeps its effort, none when it sets none.
  Validation refuses any other value (`pipeline: spend must be "low", "medium" or "high", got "max"`). `magnum roles`
  names the profile once, in its first line (`prompts_dir: …; spend: high`), and its EFFORT column shows the
  result; the daemon reads it at startup, so `magnum daemon-restart --drain` applies a change. Decided: the
  profile changes no model (the claude-judge comment names the model choices); `high` also gives the keys
  the built-in roles leave unset `xhigh` (claude-simplify's two, the `rereview_effort` of codex-review,
  claude-fix and claude-whiteboard), while `medium` and `low` leave them unset, so claude-simplify keeps
  running at the operator's own Claude Code `effortLevel` there. The operator's own `effort` and
  `rereview_effort` lines keep their values under every level until they are deleted. Not done: a
  per-watch override and the efforts outside `[[role]]` (`[learn]`'s classifier and editor, `[notes]`).
- **A spend level can set models and efforts per role, and levels can be the operator's own** (2026-10-14;
  amends "One `[pipeline] spend` key sets how hard every built-in role thinks"). A level is a budget mood,
  and a mood also picks models: with many Codex tokens the judge runs on the astra model, with few Claude
  tokens the reviewers run on Sonnet. The notch mapping changed no model, and a role block's own `model`
  and `effort` won over the level, so each change still meant editing the role blocks; the operator asked
  for full flexibility in one switch. Now a `[spend.<level>]` table (`Config.SpendLevels`, a map of level
  name to role name to `SpendRole`, whose four pointer fields keep the loader's unknown-key refusal exact)
  gives the roles of one level any of `model`, `effort`, `rereview_effort` and `max_subagents`; it names a
  built-in role or a declared `[[role]]` by name (`spend.high: unknown role "..."`), and a level's name
  matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,15}$`. The precedence, highest first: the active level's table, the role
  block's own keys, the notch mapping of `low`, `medium` and `high` (unchanged), the built-in defaults;
  `applySpend` applies the table after the mapping, to the role's inherited and set keys alike, the table
  being the more specific intent. Any other level name is the operator's own: it starts from `medium` and
  applies its table; `spend` naming a level that is neither built in nor declared is refused with the
  declared names (`pipeline: spend must be "low", "medium", "high" or "burn", got "turbo"`), and a table
  for a level `spend` does not name is kept for later (and validated). The user config's tables merge into
  the base's level by level, role by role and key by key (`mergeSpendLevels`). codex-review is a shell
  role whose model travelled in its `args`, after the command, so an `args` line would win over a level's
  model: the built-in command (and `prompts/codex-review.sh`) now passes ` -c model={{.Model}}` right after
  `codex review`, before the effort, only for a role with a model, so a level's or the block's `model`
  reaches Codex and a later `args` override still wins, as it does for the effort. Validation refused any
  `model` on a shell role; it now refuses one only when the role's command or full-line template leaves
  `.Model` out, so a model is never dropped without a word. `magnum roles` keeps `spend: <level>` in its
  first line and shows the resulting model and effort; its JSON gains nothing. Not done: a per-watch level,
  and the tables cover only `[[role]]`s, not `[learn]` or `[notes]`.
- **An agent kind can have its own spend level** (2026-10-15; amends "A spend level can set models and
  efforts per role, and levels can be the operator's own"). On 10-15 the operator's Codex weekly window
  reached 97% and the hard cap paused Codex while Claude had room, and `[pipeline] spend` is one level for
  every role: the `[spend.<level>]` tables hang off that one level, so "Codex low, Claude high" could not
  be said. The operator asked for separate spend settings for Claude and Codex. Now a kind takes `spend`

  of `[pipeline] spend` (`Config.SpendLevel`, which `applySpend` asks per role), with that level's notch
  mapping and its table; a shell role counts as the kind its `tool` names (`codex-review` as `codex`), and
  a shell role without a tool, like a kind without the key, keeps `[pipeline] spend`. The precedence below
  the level is unchanged (the level's table, the role block's keys, the notch mapping, the built-in
  defaults); only which level is active for a role changed. Validation is `[pipeline] spend`'s: a built-in
  level or one a `[spend.<level>]` table declares, refused otherwise with the declared names and the kind
  (`kinds.codex: spend must be "low", "medium" or "high", got "burn"`). A `[kinds.codex]` block that sets
  only `spend` keeps the rest of the built-in kind, since the kinds merge key by key (`mergeDefined`).
  `magnum roles` keeps `spend: <level>` in its first line and adds the kinds whose level differs, in kind
  name order (`spend: high (codex: low)`); its roles JSON carries no level, so it gains nothing, and
  `--kinds --json` shows the key with the rest of each kind. Rejected: flat keys such as `spend_codex`
  under `[pipeline]`, which hardcode kind names and leave the operator's own kinds without one; a map
  `spend_kinds` under `[pipeline]`, a second place for a kind's setting beside its `[kinds.<name>]` block.
- **A round reads its own diff before the reviewers** (2026-10-15). A colleague's review tool runs a
  pre-processor before any model reads code: the references a PR broke (a symbol it removed or renamed
  that other files still use), its test gaps (a changed source file with no matching test change) and the
  closest existing file to each new one; its reviewers read that list first, and on talkable#11483 its
  rounds found defects magnum's did not. magnum gave its roles `related.json`, `history.json` and
  `docs.json`, nothing read from the diff itself, and the skill asked them to find every caller of a
  changed method, and the example a new rule fails without, by hand in a 24k-line PR. Now, before the
  reviewers of each head and beside `docs.json` (a restart writes the new head's; a continued turn gets
  none), a round writes `prepass.json` in its report directory (`pipeline.PrepassFile`, prepass.go), read
  with git alone from `base_sha...head_sha` and the head's tree, never the work tree a role may change,
  paths matching `related_ignore` aside as history.json and docs.json do: `removed_symbols`, each name a
  `-` line defines (a regular expression per language: Ruby `def`, `class`, `module`; Go `func`, `type`;
  JavaScript and TypeScript `function`, `class`, `export const`, `const x = (`; Python `def`, `class`)
  that no `+` line defines again, searched with one `git grep -w -F --max-count=1` of the head per name
  (four at a time, at most 200 names, the rest counted), listed only when files outside the diff still
  name it, with the first 20 as `path:line`; names under 4 characters and the stop list (`new`, `call`,
  `run`, `get`, `set`, `init`, `main`, `test`, and the constructors `initialize`, `constructor` and
  `__init__`, which callers never name) are never searched. `test_gaps`, each added or modified source
  file whose test by its language's convention the diff leaves alone (Ruby `<x>/app/<y>.rb` and
  `<x>/lib/<y>.rb` to `<x>/spec/<y>_spec.rb` or `<x>/test/<y>_test.rb`, lib's also under `spec/lib/` and
  `test/lib/`, which is where Rails apps keep them; Go `x_test.go` beside `x.go`; JavaScript and
  TypeScript `x.test.*`, `x.spec.*` or `__tests__/x.*`; Python `test_x.py` or `x_test.py` anywhere), a
  file being source by its extension and its path: no test, fixture, migration, generated or vendored
  file, and for Ruby no `views/`, `config/` or `db/` file, names Go and Python packages use for code.
  `siblings`, each added file's existing file of the same suffix (from the first dot: a test's sibling is
  a test) with the longest common prefix, then the longest common ending, in its directory, else its
  parent, from one `git ls-tree` of the head; none when no such file exists. gitx gains `DiffStat`
  (numstat), `DiffLines` (`-U0`, parsed file by file, a removed `-- note` read as content, quoted names
  unquoted), `WordUses` and `DirFiles`, each on the object store. A pre-pass that cannot run writes the
  file with `skipped` and why: no base sha, more than 50,000 changed lines (counted from the numstat
  before the diff is read, lockfiles aside, so a lockfile bump does not hide the code), a git failure or
  more than 60 seconds (`PrepassTimeout`); a failure never fails the round, and each head records one
  `round.prepass` event with the counts or the reason (a warning for a failure or the timeout), never a
  name or a path. The judge prompts (the own pass, initial, rereview, recovery) name the file as
  `prepass` in the `<magnum>` block, as `docs` and `related_prs`, and they and the three claude-review
  prompts carry one sentence: read it first, the sibling before the new file, each item a lead to check,
  never a finding by itself. The sentence lives in the prompts, not the skill, whose section 0 only names
  the field. codex-review runs the stock `codex review`, to which magnum passes no prompt, so it gets
  nothing, as with `history` and `docs`. Rejected: a per-language parser (prism, tree-sitter), a
  dependency for lists that are leads, where a regular expression's precision is enough; a notes script
  per repository, since every repository gains from the lists and the notes directory is for what one
  repository alone needs.
- **The pre-pass carries the full bodies of changed methods** (2026-10-15). The pre-pass listed removed
  symbols, test gaps and siblings; the colleague's pre-processor also prints the whole body of every
  changed method, so its reviewers read the method and not the hunk, and magnum's round 11 on
  talkable#11483 missed a write in the same method as the fix it judged, outside the hunk. `prepass.json`
  now has `methods`: for each hunk of a modified source file (source as for `test_gaps`), the innermost
  method enclosing a changed line at the head, and for a hunk that only removes lines the innermost one
  holding the lines on both sides of it, with its file, name, first and last line and body, read with one
  `git cat-file blob <head>:<path>` per file (`gitx.FileAt`, the object store only, four at a time; a file
  past 8 MB is left out). The method is found by the language's shape, no parser: Ruby `def` (also
  `private def`, `def self.x`, one-line and endless defs) to the first `end` at its indentation; Go
  `func`, JavaScript and TypeScript `function`, a name bound to a function or a block-bodied arrow, and a
  method whose body opens on its line, to the line that closes the first brace opened at the signature's
  parenthesis depth, counted outside strings, runes, raw and template strings and comments (none when a
  semicolon, a blank line or 20 lines end the signature first, as an overload's does); Python `def` from
  the line that closes its parentheses to the last line before one at its indentation or less, blank
  lines, comments and triple-quoted strings aside. One entry per method however many hunks change it; a
  hunk outside any method gets none, and a method the diff adds whole is none (the diff is its body; its
  lines count for the method around it), so an added file is never read. The caps sit beside the others in
  prepass.go: a method over 300 lines is listed with its lines and no body; at most 120 methods per round,
  in git's order and by line, the rest counted in `unlisted_methods`; at most 400 KB of bodies, past which
  the largest are dropped first and counted in `dropped_bodies`. `gitx.DiffLines` gains each file's
  `Hunks` (the head's side of each `@@` header, which its parser read and dropped), prepass.json is
  written without HTML escaping so a body's `<`, `>` and `&` read as code, and the `round.prepass` event
  counts the methods. The prepass sentence of the judge and claude-review prompts adds "each changed
  method's body before its hunk". Rejected: a parser per language (prism, tree-sitter), a dependency where
  the shape by indentation and braces is enough for a lead; the outermost enclosing method, which for a
  closure or a callback in a long component passes the line cap and comes without a body; listing a method
  the diff adds whole, whose body the reviewer already reads in the diff.
- **The judge says what it examined, and the PR keeps an evidence map** (2026-10-15). A review of the
  full-pass ideas by Codex found that magnum cannot say what it examined: a finding locates a problem
  and says nothing about the areas that passed, and a Checks line is a command in prose, so nobody could
  tell which files and behaviours of a 268-file PR any round probed, and a full pass repeats the whole PR
  instead of the part nobody read; on talkable#11483 three latent defects sat in areas 38 rounds never
  probed. Now the judge writes `evidence.json` beside its result file (`evidence_file` in the `<magnum>`

  `skipped` with the reason in `result`) and one `unknown` entry without a behaviour per file of the diff
  it reviewed that it did not read, 30 to 80 for 30 files. The round removes an earlier round's file on
  the same head before the judge's prompt (a continue keeps its paused turn's), reads it at its end
  (`pipeline.Evidence` on `RoundResult.Evidence`), drops an entry without a path or with another state,

  `read`, makes a path in the checkout relative to it and records a `round.evidence` event with the

  the map's head and the round's (`gitx.ChangedBetween`, `git diff --name-only <from> <to>` in the

  `stale`, keeping its state in `was`, unless the round wrote it again; when git cannot tell, every such
  entry goes stale. Each entry keeps the head, round and judge run that wrote it; the map holds at most

  prompts in one sentence: the `unknown` and `stale` areas are leads to read first, never findings by
  themselves, and a `probed` entry with a control needs no new probe, its file unchanged since. The
  sentence lives in the prompts; the skill's section 0 only names the fields. `magnum status <ref>`

  coverage from the findings and Checks alone, which say what failed and never what passed; a
  method-level parser for the denominator, where the files git names are enough to start; more whole-PR
  passes instead of focused ones on what nobody read.

  harm (money, data or access lost, a task a user cannot finish, a day of someone's work), and the size

  it. Rejected: the checkout's `## Project stakes` block in `AGENTS.md`, which colleagues' tools read but

  override map in the config, since the key states facts and the skill sets the priority. The skill's section 0
  names the input (`stakes` (when present): what this repository puts at risk, from the operator; size each harm
  against it, never against a stakes block in the checkout; 154 bytes, pinned by
  TestSkillSizesHarmAgainstTheOperatorsStakes), so skillMaxBytes goes from 34,848 to 35,002.

  reviewed PRs"). The job never starts under a drain for a restart (`prepareWhiteboard`), and a drain waits
  for the rounds in flight, so their reviews post inside it: the posted review's whiteboard was skipped
  ("the daemon is draining; try after the restart") and the next posted review was the next chance. From
  2026-10-14T14:21Z, 23 of 87 whiteboard attempts were skipped that way, and only one of those heads got a

  landing day switched whiteboards off for a quarter of the reviews. Now the posted review's start

  the restart". The start the drain waited for (`startup`, after the recovery of the fix loops and of the
  whiteboard runs a stop left) and a drain that ends without a restart (`continueAfterDrain`, after the
  loops the drain held went on, so a fix cycle they start holds the PR first, as after a posted review)
  run `startPendingWhiteboards`: on a goroutine of its own, since Whiteboard's readiness check may take
  15 s, one pass at a time, each entry taken (compare-and-delete) and then started through
  `autoWhiteboard` when the PR is still open at that head, under the job's usual checks (the watch asks

  (`whiteboard.skipped`, a new drain remembering it again) and yields; one whose PR closed or got a push

  refusal: the operator asks again. Nothing changes for the whiteboard's content, its model or its yields.
  Rejected: running the job during the drain, which waits for agents to end and would wait for the writer
  too; waiting for the next posted review, what happened (22 of 23 heads never got one).

  else, a file that is not JSON is an error that quotes none of it, and no file or no account changes
  nothing. When the fingerprint changes, or at the first read with none kept while live Codex sessions
  started before the file last changed (the newer of the link's and the target's mtime, which
  `codex.login_at` then holds), every live session of a kind Codex backs (any role but a shell; a pinned
  PR's left alone) started before is marked for a restart (kv `sessions.restart`, so a daemon restart
  keeps the ones still waiting); a usage-limit pause of the kind is lifted and the budget reading
  overruled (`overruleBudget`), both the old account's; one `codex.login_changed` info event (counts, never
  an account) and one toast say "Codex login changed: N Codex sessions restart with the new one". A
  marked session parks through the early park (`Agents.ParkSessions`: its pane closes, its conversation
  stays resumable; one without a conversation is quit and starts fresh) on the heavy worker, under the
  PR's reservation taken at once, when its PR has no round, no agent at work, no pin, no human within
  `human_cooldown` and no park backoff (a busy one parks after its turn; a failed park waits out
  `parkFailed`'s backoff), with one `agent.restarted` event; until then no round starts on its PR
  (`prGate`: "codex-judge restarts in a new process first (the Codex login changed)"), so no prompt
  reaches the old process. Its next prompt resumes it with `codex resume <id>` in a new process
  (`ensureAgent`, `ResumeID`), a paused round's continuation included, which stays a continue of the
  paused turn. A usage limit whose run's session started before `codex.login_at` (`pipeline.Pause.RunID`,
  set by the judge's verdict and a reviewer's pause) is the old account's: it pauses no kind, the session
  is marked, one `codex.stale_usage_limit` info event says so, and a round that ended on it pauses with a
  retry a minute later; a session started under the current login pauses the kind as before. Park and
  resume rather than a fresh session: `codex resume` carries the conversation into the new process, so a
  judge keeps its context, the paused turn continues where it stopped and a re-review keeps its history.
  The account id and not the mtime: Codex rewrites auth.json at every token refresh, and a refresh of the
  same account parks nothing; the mtime decides only the first read, when no login was kept. Rejected: a
  second CODEX_HOME per account, which the operator rejected earlier (Codex sessions are isolated with
  `-c` overrides only); restarting the sessions on every write of auth.json; leaving it to
  `judge_fresh_after`, which parks a judge 90 minutes after its last prompt while every prompt before goes
  to the old account.
- **`magnum restart-sessions` restarts an agent kind's live sessions on request** (2026-10-22, spec 119
  item 4). The operator asked for "a manual option or button to restart codex sessions", and a Claude
  account switch has the same problem with no login magnum watches. `magnum restart-sessions --tool
  <kind>|all [--pr <ref>]` sends `restart_sessions` (`RestartSessionsPayload`) to the daemon, never queued
  without one (a restart nobody waits for must not run when a daemon starts later); a terminal asks
  "Restart the N live codex sessions? They resume in new processes." first (`--yes` does not). The daemon
  marks the live sessions `engine.RestartableSessions` gives (a role that runs an agent of that kind, its
  recorded kind else its role's; a pinned PR's or pinned slot's counted apart and left alone) as the login
  change does, queues the park of each PR's that may park now, and answers "restarting 3 live codex
  sessions: 2 park now, 1 after its turn; each resumes in a new process at its next prompt", naming the
  sessions of pinned PRs it left alone; the marked ones then go the login change's way (the gate, the
  early park, the resume). The settings screen's Runtime section has the same action as `x` on a kind's
  row and on "all kinds", with that question (the count is each kind's live sessions,
  `RuntimeEntry.Live`), the answer in the footer, the strip naming the command and the help and footer the
  key; a row with no live session sends nothing. `magnum resume --tool` restarts nothing: lifting a pause
  and replacing processes are separate asks. Rejected: a key on the board's PR rows, since a switch of
  account concerns every PR's sessions of the kind at once; parking busy sessions at once, which would cut
  a judge's turn short.
- **A round's settle pauses a kind again only for a reviewer's failure after the kind's last lift**
  (2026-10-22, spec 120). Round 4 of talkable#12069 paused at 22:14 on the old Codex account (the judge's
  usage limit; its codex-review report was a usage limit too); at 22:50:54 the login change lifted the
  codex pause and parked the judge; the round continued at 22:54:37 and the resumed judge posted at
  22:57:48, and in the same second the settle wrote `tool.paused: codex paused (usage_limit) until 02:57:
  not available`, which held two other PRs for an hour. `finish` turns every reviewer report with a
  pause status into a pause; the codex-review report the continue carried from its paused round had no
  run of the continued round, so spec 119's stale check (which needs a run) did not apply and the unproven
  pause took the one-hour fallback; `magnum resume --tool codex` before a continue had the same end. Now
  each deliberate lift is recorded per kind (kv `<kind>.pause_lifted_at`, `store.KVToolPauseLiftedAt`):
  every `magnum resume --tool <kind>` or `all`, through the daemon (`liftToolPause`) or without one (the
  CLI's offline resume), a pause or not, since the resume is the operator's word that the kind works; and,
  for each kind Codex backs, a change of Codex login (`codexLoginChanged`), a pause or not, since the old
  account's limits are moot. A pause that expires and a login check that passes are no lift. The failure's
  time is the report's run's end (`ProvenAt`) for a report with a run of the round, else the new
  `pipeline.RoleReport.CarriedFrom`, which `existingReports` sets for a continue's carried report: the end
  of the role's latest run of the paused round on the head, and, for a role with no run there (skipped as
  logged out) or one that never ended, the paused round's stop, the latest end of its runs on the head.
  That run's end and not the PR's paused transition, which no column dates, nor `pr.<id>.work_ended`,
  which a whiteboard or fix job after the pause moves past the lift and which the continue's own settle
  has not written yet: the run is the failure itself, and the round's stop, a later time, is only the
  fallback, which errs toward pausing as before. A report whose failure is not after the kind's last lift
  pauses nothing (`overruledFailure`), with one `round.pause_skipped` info event under the PR
  ("codex-review's usage_limit is from before the codex pause was lifted at 22:50; not paused again");
  a failure with no known time (no run, nothing carried, a run without an end) is after every lift, so a
  reviewer the login check skipped this round still pauses its kind. A failure in a Codex session older
  than the current login still goes spec 119's way first (its session restarts, `codex.stale_usage_limit`).
  The reports themselves are unchanged: the continued judge still hears the report as missing, and the
  review approves nothing. Rejected: never pausing from a carried report, which would drop a failure that
  came after an earlier resume (the operator resumed while the paused round still ran); clearing the
  reports' statuses at the lift, which would tell the continued judge a report was there that it never
  read.

  exec`) in the same checkout within two minutes of their start, so the rule without it would have refused

  TestAnIdleCodexTurnEndsAsBeforeWhenItsRolloutSaysNothingElse in agents,

  | 1665 | talkable#12075 | 15:36:58 | 15:38:07 |

  | 1672 | another repository's #752 | 15:41:08 | 15:42:02 |

  TestTheFirstCodexPromptWaitsOutAHooksReviewThatFollowsItsComposer,
  TestAFirstCodexPromptWithNoDialogGoesOutAfterTheSettle,
  TestAFirstCodexPromptADialogAteIsSentAgainAfterTheAnswer,
  TestAFirstCodexPromptLostTwiceFailsTheRunWithTheReason, TestAStalledFirstCodexPromptCodexTookIsNotSentAgain,

- **A PR never closes, reuses or retires what another PR's live session records** (2026-10-23, spec 04
  of the 2026-10-23 run, item 1). herdr restarted at 08:37:24Z and numbered new workspaces from wMW
  again, and a pane id is its workspace's id and a number (`wN9:p1`), so wN9, wNA, wNB and wN3 named both
  the new workspaces of PRs whose sessions were starting and the parked, closed and lost session rows of
  the day before. Since then 22 of the 23 `agent.lost` events, all 12 `pr.panes_closed` events and two
  parks' workspace closes traced to it: at 13:26:13Z the retired-pane closes of talkable#12058 (4 panes)
  and #12075 (3) took the new workspaces of three other PRs, whose panes were idle shells before their
  agents started, so three setups failed and eleven sessions were lost, and a lost codex-review became
  `no_session`, after which auto-approval refused its PR ("did not hear every reviewer"). The three places
  that read only the PR's own sessions were the retired-pane close (`retiredPanes`' in-use set), Park's
  workspace close (its `ours` and the close) and the workspace reuse (`reusableWorkspace` and the lost
  pane a missing role takes). Now each also reads, in one registry query (`store.LiveSessions`), the panes
  and workspaces that starting or live sessions of other PRs record (`othersLive`,
  internal/agents/herdr_ids.go) and never closes, reuses or takes them: the close skips such a pane and
  any pane in such a workspace (herdr may have split it a moment before its row), Park counts such a pane
  as foreign and never closes such a workspace (its live agents are still quit as before), and
  EnsureWorkspace reuses no such workspace, keeps no such pane for a live session (it is marked lost) and
  takes no such pane for a lost one. Of two live rows of two PRs that record one id, the newer row owns it
  (the older is one herdr restarted under, which the observer marks lost), so a stale live row never keeps
  the owner from its own panes. A retired (parked, closed or lost) row of the PR whose pane or workspace
  such a session records is stale: its herdr pane, workspace and tab ids are dropped, compare-and-set on
  the ids read and its state kept (`dropStale`; a parked or lost conversation still resumes, in a new
  pane), with one info `agents.herdr_ids_reused` event under the PR naming the rows and the ids, and
  nothing of it is closed; the engine's reconcile, which asks `store.PRsWithPanes` for the panes herdr has,
  then no longer finds the PR. Skipping leaves no pane that no row owns open for good: what is skipped is
  recorded by the other PR's own session, which retires it, and a pane of the PR in such a workspace is
  closed once no other PR's session lives there. Tests:
  TestAStaleRowsHerdrIDsThatAnotherPRUsesNowAreNeverClosedOrReused (the retire, park and reuse paths),
  TestTwoPRsOldRowsCloseNoneOfTheNewWorkspacesHerdrNumberedAgain (the 13:26:13Z case over one snapshot)
  and TestAnOlderLiveRowOfAnotherPRLeavesTheNewerOwnerItsPanes. Rejected: telling a reused id by herdr's
  restart (magnum does not see one, and the ids collide until herdr's counter passes the old ones);
  dropping the ids of every row at a herdr restart (it would forget the panes of sessions that survive
  it); a migration with a stale state (the dropped ids say it, and the row keeps its own state).
- **A Codex judge that never took a prompt starts fresh** (2026-10-23, spec 04 of the 2026-10-23 run, item
  2). A second hooks-review wave (09:06 to 09:55Z) left Codex judges whose first prompt stalled with no
  rollout and no session id (registry sessions 1760, 1763, 1767, 1771): 6 own passes `missing` and three
  PRs in needs_attention. talkable#12080's round 2 reused session 1763 84 minutes after its last turn
  ended, under judge_fresh_after's 90, and failed the same way in 14 minutes although ids were back. The
  cold-judge rule read only the idle time, and a stalled first prompt still sets last_prompt_at, which
  ends the first-prompt wait. Codex writes a session's rollout at its first prompt, and the observer gives
  a session herdr reports without an id its rollout's id from `agents.RecoverIDAfter` after its start, so
  now `agents.Manager.TookNoPrompt` answers true for a live Codex session with no id longer than
  RecoverIDAfter after its last prompt whose Codex home holds no rollout of its checkout and start
  (`cliRolloutIDs`, read then; a read error, an unknown home or checkout, and a rollout found, one or two,
  answer false), and `coldJudge` makes such a judge cold whatever its idle time and judge_fresh_after (0
  included: this is no cache question): it is quit (`quitToRenew`, which keeps a judge herdr shows working
  or blocked) and the round starts a fresh one through the recovery, with one `round.judge_fresh_cold`
  event, `reason` `no_rollout`, "its Codex session never took a prompt (no session id and no rollout 35m
  after its last prompt)". It cannot cut a turn: with no rollout no turn ever ran in the session, and a
  continue never takes the rule. A judge with an id keeps the idle rule. Tests:
  TestACodexSessionWithNoIDAndNoRolloutLongAfterItsPromptTookNoPrompt and
  TestACodexJudgeThatNeverTookAPromptStartsFreshWhateverItsIdle. Rejected: deciding by the id alone (two
  Codex sessions started in one checkout keep their ids unknown with a rollout each, and one may have
  worked); calling RestartJudge when the own pass ends `missing` for such a judge (05's part c, not in
  this spec).
- **A first Codex prompt sent anyway or stalled with no dialog says what the screen showed** (2026-10-23,
  spec 04 of the 2026-10-23 run, item 3). Twice the cause of a stalled first prompt stayed unknown: magnum
  logged "sending the first prompt anyway" after the 30-second readiness wait, and spec 124's check after
  the stall found no dialog on screen and recorded nothing. Now both are warn events under the PR,
  `agents.first_prompt_unready` (the log line it replaces) and `agents.first_prompt_stalled` (no sign that
  Codex took the prompt and no dialog after `PromptTakenWait`; the run is observed as before), with role,

  to 200 bytes on a rune (`screenTail`). At that moment the screen holds Codex's start screen, not PR text;
  the composer, which holds the typed prompt, and what is below it stay out. Tests:
  TestAFirstCodexPromptSentAnywayCarriesTheScreenLines and
  TestAFirstCodexPromptThatStallsWithNoDialogCarriesTheScreenAboveItsComposer.
- **agent_start_input_failed is retried as agent_pane_busy is** (2026-10-23, spec 04 of the 2026-10-23

- **A stop's cut CLI-version read and a whiteboard's normal stop are no warnings or errors** (2026-10-23,

- **magnum reads the trust of every hook of hooks.json, and doctor warns per Codex home** (2026-10-23,
  spec 06 of the 2026-10-23 run, items 1 and 2, amends "Doctor and the daemon tell when herdr's Codex
  session hook stops giving ids"). Spec 122 checks only the place of herdr's SessionStart hook, but Codex
  shows its hooks review for any hook of `hooks.json` whose place has no trust entry, and four tools
  rewrite `~/.codex/hooks.json` (herdr, Muxy, Bartender NotchBar, moshi): on 10-23 a second review wave ran
  from 09:06 to 09:55Z. `agents.ReadCodexHooksTrust` reads every hook of every event Codex runs, in every
  group (`ReadCodexSessionHook` now shares its reader, `readCodexHooksJSON`), and names those whose place
  has no `[hooks.state]` entry with a `trusted_hash` (`Untrusted`, with `Hooks` and the file's
  `Fingerprint`). Codex keys the trust as `<hooks.json path>:<event>:<group>:<index>`, the event in snake
  case (`pre_tool_use`, `session_start`, `user_prompt_submit`, `stop`, `interrupt`, ...): read in Codex
  0.162.1's binary next to `HookEventsToml` and its normalized hook identity, and in the operator's
  `config.toml`, whose 49 entries cover 12 events and whose 14 hooks all had one; the path is as written or
  with its symlinks resolved, as before. Only the 12 events Codex 0.162.1 knows are read
  (`codexHookEvents`): an event it does not run asks for no trust, and holding new sessions for it would
  never end. An entry without a hash, another home's entry and another place's entry trust nothing; a hook
  whose command changed in place keeps its entry, which magnum cannot tell from a current one (Codex hashes
  its own normal form), and that is accepted. Doctor's new `codex hooks trust` line, per Codex home of the
  codex kind's session roles (`agents.CodexSessionHomes`, whatever herdr's session source; spec 122's
  checks keep `agents.CodexHookHomes`), warns "2 hooks in ~/.codex/hooks.json have no trust entry
  (moshi-hook at session_start:1:0, herdr-agent-state.sh at stop:0:0; used by codex-judge)", fix "run `codex`
  once in a terminal and choose Trust all", passes with the count, and skips an unknown home or one without
  `hooks.json`; the herdr hook's own trust line stays, since its consequence (no session ids) differs. Tests:
  TestReadCodexHooksTrustNamesEveryHookWithoutATrustEntry and
  TestDoctorWarnsPerCodexHomeOfHooksWithoutATrustEntry.
- **New Codex sessions wait while a hook has no trust entry** (2026-10-23, spec 06 of the 2026-10-23 run,
  item 3, approved by the operator that day with the warning). In the 10-23 wave magnum answered "Trust all"
  13 times over 5 sessions, Codex saved no trust, and first prompts stalled with no rollout and no id; the
  toast came at 09:07:42Z, the operator ran `codex` in a terminal at about 09:55Z, five rounds started in between,
  and one PR needed `magnum review` by hand. Now the daemon, once a minute with spec 122's checks
  (`checkCodexHooksTrust`, internal/engine/codex_hooks_hold.go), reads the hooks of each Codex home the codex
  kind's session roles read, and while one has a hook without a trust entry it pauses the codex kind with
  the new reason `hooks_review` (`HooksReviewPauseReason`), through the tool pause the budget and the
  logins already use (kv, no migration): every round and job that needs Codex waits (a reviewer's `codex
  review` too, a shell role that shows no review, as any kind pause holds it), sessions already running go
  on, the board's wait and `magnum status` say why with the existing pause display ("codex paused
  (hooks_review): 1 hook in ~/.codex/hooks.json has no trust entry: run `codex` once and choose Trust
  all"; the wait and the status line show no end, since the check renews the pause, `hooksHoldFor`, 10
  minutes ahead each minute, and health's expiry leaves it to the check), and one `codex.hooks_untrusted`
  warning naming the hooks and one toast ("Codex hooks need review: run `codex` once and choose Trust all.
  New Codex sessions wait.") come once per `hooks.json` fingerprint (kv `codex.hooks_untrusted`, the
  fingerprints told). A pause of another reason is left alone (it says when it ends), and the hold takes
  its place at the check after it ends. Once no home has such a hook, the check ends the pause it set with
  one `tool.resumed` info event. `magnum resume --tool codex` (or `all`, the daemon's or the CLI's offline
  one, `engine.OverruleHooksHold`) lifts the pause as any pause and records the told fingerprints as
  overruled (kv `codex.hooks_overruled`, one `tool.resumed` event, the answer's note "new Codex sessions
  start although hooks.json has hooks without a trust entry, until it changes again"); an overrule goes
  when its file changes, so a new rewrite holds and tells again. Messages name `~/.codex/...` or
  `$CODEX_HOME/...`, never a home from a pane env. The hold is per kind, as every tool pause is: with
  Codex roles in two homes, an untrusted hook in one holds both, which a per-home gate in dispatch alone
  would not, since the fix, whiteboard, notes, critic, retro and editor jobs start Codex sessions through
  the kind pause's checks too. Tests: TestAHookWithoutATrustEntryHoldsNewCodexSessionsUntilResume,
  TestTrustedCodexHooksStartCodexSessionsAtOnce, TestTheHooksHoldLeavesAPauseOfAnotherReasonAlone,
  TestTheOfflineResumesMarkOverrulesTheHooksHold, and in cli TestTheOfflineResumeOverrulesTheHooksHold and
  TestStatusShowsTheHooksHoldWithItsFix. Rejected: a new pause kind in the registry (the tool pause carries
  a reason already); writing `hooks.json` or `config.toml` (the hooks and their trust are the operator's);
  holding only the rounds whose judge would start a new session (a reused judge shows no review, but the
  round's other sessions and the jobs would, and the wave lasts minutes, not hours).
- **After "Trust all", the trust entries tell whether Codex saved the trust** (2026-10-23, spec 06 of the

  `hooksTrustSaved` decided "not saved" by `config.toml`'s modification time alone: when two sessions

  evidence: one of seven answers wrote the file), and any other write between Enter and the check (a

  reads the hooks without a trust entry before Enter (`ReadCodexHooksTrust`) and `hooksTrustSaved` reads
  them again once the agent is back: a hook from the first read still without an entry records
  `agents.hooks_trust_unsaved` ("... and $CODEX_HOME/config.toml still has no trust entry for moshi-hook at
  pre_tool_use:0:0", data `places`) and toasts as before, once per `hooks.json` (the fingerprint and its kv
  key unchanged); none, or no such hook before Enter (a hook changed in place, a plugin's), says nothing.
  Tests: TestAHookTrustCodexDidNotSaveIsToldOncePerHooksJSON and TestASavedOrDeclinedHookTrustGivesNoWarning
  (their `hooks.json` now holds a hook), TestASecondAnswerToAReviewTheFirstAnswerSavedGivesNoWarning and
  TestAnAnswerAfterWhichAHookStillHasNoTrustEntryWarnsWhateverTheModificationTime.
- **One composer reader and one rollout-tail reader; the hooks check's homes after its throttle, its stat
  error without the path** (2026-10-23, spec 06 of the 2026-10-23 run, items 5 and 6, no behaviour change

  constant was spec 04's `composerScan`, the old function wrote 8): both, and `screenTail`, now read
  `composerLineOf` (the line's index and what it holds, a dialog's option line never the composer; an

  `userMessageSince` and TurnError's `lastTurnError` each opened a rollout and read its last MiB their own
