- **magnum closes or reuses a pane or a workspace by a recorded id only while herdr shows it is still the
  session's** (2026-10-23, spec 08 of the 2026-10-23 run). Spec 04's check sees only what the registry
  holds. At 15:10:53Z the live daemon, still on the code before spec 04, set up talkable#12069 and logged
  `closed 1 panes of retired sessions (codex-review)` (`pr.panes_closed`); herdr's server log shows request
  `magnum-2241-5125`, `pane.close`, pane 145, and one second later an eval replay reported `codex-review
  session lost (pane or agent gone)`. The replay ran in its own workspace ("eval talkable#11932", agents
  tagged eval-8cd077) and keeps its sessions in a scratch registry the live daemon cannot see, as it cannot
  see any pane the operator opens; herdr numbers workspaces and panes from the start again after every
  restart, so a stale row could still close such a pane after spec 04. Now a pane or a workspace a session
  recorded is closed, parked away or reused only while herdr's snapshot shows it is still the session's
  (`herdrView`, internal/agents/herdr_ids.go): a pane with an agent must carry the row's agent name
  (`another_agent` otherwise; a CLI herdr detected but names not, since herdr names only what agent.start or
  a rename named, is no agent magnum started, and is let through only for a row without an agent name, a
  shell role whose command runs a CLI such as `codex review`, by the directory); a pane without one must
  work in the session's checkout, the row's cwd, else the path of the PR's slot (`outside_checkout`, also
  when herdr or the row does not say where); a workspace must hold only panes that pass for a row of the PR
  that records them, and a pane no row records must carry one of the PR's agent names or work in the
  checkout of a row that records the workspace. The places: the retired-pane close, Park's workspace close
  and the workspace reuse (`inHerdr` before `retiredPanes`, Park's `closing` and `reusableWorkspace`; a live
  row's pane EnsureWorkspace's first pass keeps elsewhere is marked lost when it fails), the early park's
  close of the session's own pane (`closeOwnPane` leaves it, the session parked, the note saying it
  stays), and every key a park, a retire or a quit sends by a recorded id: the ctrl+c of Quit, Park,
  ParkHard and the early park (`ctrlC`, which no longer reads the session id from such a pane either:
  `RecordSessionID` ran before the ctrl+c and would have recorded the other agent's conversation) and the
  hard park's exit keys and close (`forceQuit`). Each looks at a fresh snapshot first (`beforeKeys`); a
  pane that fails gets nothing, with a warn log line naming the session and the ids: when herdr lists the
  session's agent nowhere, its agent is gone, which counts as quit (the session is retired, the pane left,
  and its ids dropped as a retired row's), and when herdr shows the agent in another pane the quit fails
  with ErrBusy and the session stays live (the observer moves the row to its agent's pane at its next
  tick, so the next park quits it there; Recover sends no key). The early park's exit keys were already
  held to the conversation the park found. A retired row whose pane, or its
  workspace when the pane is gone, fails is stale as spec 04's are: its herdr ids are dropped
  compare-and-set, state and session_id kept, with one info `agents.herdr_ids_reused` event per PR and
  reason (its data gains `reason`, `other_pr` for spec 04's), naming the ids, never a pane's screen or
  directory; a live row keeps its ids (Park retires it, and the next retired-pane close drops them). herdr's
  snapshot gives the agent's name and the pane's working directory (`agents[].name`, `panes[].cwd`, else
  `foreground_cwd`), which the eval's leftover close and the slot guard already read, and a session row
  records its checkout as its cwd (EnsureWorkspace's slot path). A shell the operator `cd`s elsewhere in a
  PR's workspace now keeps that workspace from reuse: the next round lays out its own. Tests:
  TestARetiredRowNeverClosesAPaneHerdrShowsAsSomeoneElses (an eval agent, the eval's codex-review shell, the
  operator's shell, the operator's CLI in the checkout and where a shell role's pane was),
  TestARetiredRowsPaneHerdrStillShowsAsTheSessionsCloses (a parked row's shell in the checkout, a lost
  row's agent anywhere, a shell role's detected CLI, a row without a cwd in the PR's slot),
  TestParkAndTheReuseRefuseAWorkspaceWithAPaneThatIsNotThePRs (both paths: both panes the replay's, one
  still the PR's, one the operator's shell, a row's pane gone),
  TestParkNeverClosesAWorkspaceItsLiveRowsRecordWhereHerdrShowsAReplay,
  TestAReusedWorkspaceKeepsNoLivePaneHerdrShowsAsSomeoneElses,
  TestAnEarlyParkLeavesARecordedPaneHerdrShowsAsSomeoneElses,
  TestAParkSendsNoKeyToARecordedPaneThatCarriesAnotherAgent (the plain and the hard park),
  TestAQuitSendsNoKeyToARecordedPaneHerdrGaveToSomeoneElse and
  TestAHardParkForcesNothingOnAPaneHerdrGaveAwayDuringItsQuit. Rejected: the workspace label as the
  identity (Park and the retired-pane close do not know it, a retro pane's workspace has its own, and it
  says nothing of the panes); the pane label "PR #N <role>" (it names no repository and stays whatever runs
  in the pane); taking a CLI herdr names not as the session's in any shell role's pane wherever it works
  (the operator's codex where a closed codex-review row's pane was); dropping a live row's ids (spec 04's
  rule stands); sending the ctrl+c to the agent by its name instead (the wait for an idle shell and the
  hard park's close would still go to the recorded pane); counting a quit as done while herdr shows the
  session's agent in another pane (it would park a session whose agent goes on under its name, which a
  fresh start then refuses).

- **Quit stops an agent with its kind's exit keys, as the early park does** (2026-10-27, amends "An early park
  quits an agent with its kind's exit keys, so Claude agents park" and "A Claude session is quit before the
  checkout moves only when the new head changes its project config, and a quit that fails is charged"). On
  2026-10-27 a PR got three new heads that changed its root `AGENTS.md`. Before each checkout, parkReloading quit
  the idle claude-review session with `Agents.Quit`: two ctrl+c 1 s apart, then a wait of up to 10 s for an idle
  shell. Claude 2.1.311 stayed in the foreground every time ("shell not idle after 10s (foreground: 2.1.311)").
  The round's setup failed six times from 09:32 to 09:58 UTC, and the PR needed attention twice. The idle park
  did not take the PR. It waited behind the 15-minute push quiet period, which is not longer than
  `park_idle_after`, and a PR that needs attention keeps its agents. Then `magnum restart-sessions --tool claude
  --pr` parked the PR's three Claude sessions through the early park, and each one quit with its exit keys in
  about 2 s. The 10-19 entry found this flaw and left `Quit` unchanged "for a follow-up with measurements". These
  are the measurements. The 10-07 entry blamed the MCP servers in the pane's foreground, which was probably the
  same flaw. Now `Quit` reads a fresh snapshot first. When the session records a pane, its kind has exit keys,
  herdr lists its agent and herdr or the row names its conversation, `Quit` uses `earlyQuit`: the look, one
  ctrl+c, 1 s, the look again, the exit keys and the wait. A composer that is not bare gets no key, and the quit
  fails with `ErrBusy` and no timeout. Any other session gets the two ctrl+c as before, so Codex keeps them. A
  session whose conversation nobody names keeps them too, because the look refuses every key without one. This
  reaches every caller of `Quit`: parkReloading, quitToRenew (the cold-judge rule and the rotation, for a Claude
  judge), `magnum restart-sessions` for a session without a session id, and the retro pane after a failed park.
  Nothing is forced. The 10-07 entry rejected a close of the pane, and that rule stands, and a quit that fails
  stays charged. Test: TestQuitQuitsClaudeWithItsExitKeys. An agent deaf to ctrl+c quits with one ctrl+c and the
  exit keys and parks, and nothing is closed. A draft gets no key, `ErrBusy` without a timeout, and stays live. A
  session with no conversation named gets two ctrl+c. The first two cases failed first with the production error,
  and the third fails when the conversation condition is dropped. Rejected: a hard quit at the round's last
  attempt (it closes the pane, which the 10-07 entry rejected, and the exit keys quit Claude every time so far);
  a change in parkReloading alone (the other callers of `Quit` have the same flaw).

## Screens and commands

- **Action keys ask y/N and only `y` confirms**; Enter cancels like any other key (a stray `R` followed
  by a habitual Enter must not start a 12-minute round). `ctrl+r`/F5 refresh. Keys mean the same on
  every screen (`r` review, `R` fresh, `i` simplify, `K` kill, `I` ignore, `x` release, `M`/`U` mute).
- **Frames are cached by a fingerprint of everything they show**, because a trackpad scroll in iTerm2
  arrives as hundreds of arrow keys per second and a 5 ms frame per key froze the board.
- **Mouse support is on by default** (`[terminal] mouse`, `m` toggles): wheel scrolls, header click
  sorts, drag resizes with widths kept per screen (`W` resets), right click opens the PR's action menu
  with the same y/N prompts (2026-10-04). Text selection then needs the terminal's override modifier.
  The dashboard's manual-worktrees toggle moved from `m` to `w` for this.
- **`daemon-stop`, `daemon-restart`, `install` and `uninstall` refuse while rounds are in flight**
  unless `--now`, because a restart abandons the rounds (their agents keep working, nobody collects
  the result). The dev loop passes `--now`.
- **`repo#N` resolves against every watched owner** when the default owner has no such repository;
  two matches are an error.
- **The PR board has views, and the filter has qualifiers** (2026-10-04). `v` cycles `all`, `magnum`
  (state not baseline or ineligible), `mine` (assigned to a self login or its review requested) and `ready`
  (open, not a draft, approved, no CHANGES_REQUESTED); the title bar names the view, `magnum prs --view`
  picks the one the board opens in and printed output, and tab keeps it. The filter adds `state:`,
  `assignee:`, `author:` (`@me`) and `review:requested` to the fuzzy words; a comma lists alternatives,
  qualifiers combine with AND, and an unknown `key:` stays free text because titles carry colons.
  Rejected: user-defined saved views (146 of 158 rows were baseline; three fixed views cover the hunts)
  and GitHub's search syntax (the board filters the registry, not GitHub).
- **`magnum init` writes `config.local.toml` from three questions** (2026-10-04): the gh login (default
  from `gh api user`), one repository, and who posts. The result is one gh identity, one watch with
  `include = [name]`, `daemon.default_repo`, no pool; posting as an App adds the App identity and keeps the
  gh login as `poll_identity`, because polling always needs a user. It is validated together with the
  committed `config.toml` before anything is written, refuses an existing file without `--force` (which
  keeps a `.bak`), and never asks for a private key: it prints the `.mise.local.toml` line instead.
  Rejected: a wizard for pools, roles and kinds (the second machine needs one review, not the whole setup)
  and storing the key (secrets stay in `.mise.local.toml`).
- **The PR card and `magnum status <ref>` show the last round's stage timings** (2026-10-04), computed from
  what the registry already holds: the slot's checkout step events before the round's first run, each
  role's runs from submitted to ended, the judge's end to its verification, and the total. A continue
  round has no checkout; a checkout that ended more than an hour before the round is an earlier round's.
  Rejected: a timings table or new events written by the pipeline (one more writer for data that exists).
- **`magnum resume --tool <kind>` also forgets the kind's per-model limits** (2026-10-04), through the
  daemon or directly in the registry when none runs, so a user who knows a limit is over does not wait for
  the cooldown. `magnum roles --kinds` prints each kind's `model switch:` line (switch command, fallbacks,
  default and reset model, or `-` when a model limit pauses the kind), and doctor suggests HTTPS clones
  (`git clone https://…` or `gh repo clone`) with the ssh-agent hint only for an SSH origin.
- **The screens ask only what `y` will do** (2026-10-05, after questions offered a `y` the daemon then
  refused or that did something else: `x` on a pinned PR, `A` after the head moved, `R` on a PR under review
  flashing a green "follow it with `magnum review --wait`", `I` on a merged PR promising to free a slot).
  The board, the dashboard and the picker share one row-action layer (`internal/tui/rowacts.go`): a table
  of the row actions (key, menu label, hint word, name), what each screen knows of its row (`actRow`; a
  fact a screen does not know stays unknown and is left to the daemon), one predicate `actionRefusal`
  checked before anything is asked, and the question built from the same facts. The right-click menus,
  the card's ACTIONS and the key hints are generated from the table, so the rules exist once instead of in
  six copies. Refused at the key with a red flash: `x` on a pinned PR ("unpin first (u)") or one with no
  slot; `A`/`C` after the head moved ("review again first (r)": a screen cannot pass `--force`); `r`, `R`,
  `i` on a round running (the daemon queues no second one: "round in progress; K kills it"); a review of a
  PR closed without merging or merged with its head reviewed, now on the dashboard too; `I` on a merged PR
  or an ignored one; `K` with no review running, paused or waiting; `U` on a merged or closed PR unless a
  mute dismissed its merged-unreviewed flag (then it asks to restore it), and on a PR that is not muted;
  `M` on a muted one; `p` on a pinned PR and `u` on one that is not. `I` names what it will do (kill or drop
  the review when one runs or waits, mute, free the slot only when the PR holds one; a closed PR is only
  muted, which keeps it ignored if reopened), the dashboard reads a PR `magnum ignore` muted as `ignored`,
  so its `U` asks to stop ignoring it, and the picker's review question says a pinned PR is unpinned, as
  the board's does. A refusal in the picker names its own key ("unpin first (ctrl+p)"). Rejected: asking
  and letting the daemon refuse (its answer came after the flash, or never, for a release), and a
  row-filtered key-hint line (it would change under the cursor and defeat the frame cache).
- **`magnum abort` takes back a review that waits in line** (2026-10-05). Before, only `magnum ignore`
  removed a forced review once queued, and that mutes the PR for good; `mute` does not stop one (a forced
  round runs muted). `abort` (and `K`) on a queued or rereview_pending PR, forced or automatic, now drops
  the review before it starts: the forced mark goes, so do the fresh-sessions, dry-run and on-request-role
  marks of the request, and the PR returns to reviewed, or baseline when never reviewed (a merged PR's
  post-merge review: closed, released after a fresh close grace); no agent is interrupted, no session
  parked, the slot is kept, since nothing started and a person may be working in its panes. A `--as`
  identity switch stays (it is documented as lasting). A round paused mid-way is stopped like a running
  one. The `pr.aborted` event carries `queued: true`. Rejected: restoring the exact state before the
  request (the registry keeps no such history; reviewed or baseline is what an abort of a running round
  gives too).
- **`Again` is gone; `ctrl+r` refreshes the picker** (2026-10-05). The hidden `magnum review --again`,
  `tui.ReviewOpts.Again`, the picker's `ctrl+r` and the numbered prompt's `a` duplicated a plain review (a
  forced round reviews a reviewed head anyway) and asked "Review X again" even of a PR never reviewed.
  `ctrl+r` and F5 now refresh the picker's list, as on every screen (the entry above on keys), keeping the
  filter and the highlighted PR. The daemon still accepts `again` in a review payload and ignores it:
  `decode` refuses unknown fields, so a request an older CLI queued with `--again` would fail otherwise.
- **Fix hints name what works for the verb, and no positional argument is a placebo** (2026-10-05). A PR
  the daemon has not recorded yet got "fix: `magnum review <ref>` adds it now" from mute, ignore, pin,
  abort and approve alike; following it started a forced round. Now mute, ignore and pin say to wait for
  the next poll (`magnum kick` polls now) and run the command again, unmute, unpin, release and abort that
  there is nothing to undo, approve, request-changes, open and watch that magnum has not reviewed it and
  that `magnum review` would start a forced round. `magnum pause 2h` paused for good with the reason
  "2h": a word that parses as a duration is refused ("use --for 2h"). `kick poll|reconcile|schedule`
  echoed its argument back (every tick does all three): it takes none now, and the three names are still
  accepted with a note, since an installed copy of the herdr plugin runs `kick reconcile` at startup.
  `magnum slots pin|unpin <slot>` runs `magnum pin|unpin <slot>`: one path through the daemon, which also
  writes the `pr.pinned` event a review's unpin reply reads; with no daemon running the request waits for
  its start, as `pin` always did (before, `slots pin` pinned in process then). Rejected: pinning in process
  from both (a second writer of pins and their events beside the daemon).
- **The herdr picker and status popups keep a failure on screen** (2026-10-05). `magnum-ctl.sh` ran them
  with `exec`, and `pick` skipped its press-any-key for open and browser, so the popup closed with the
  error. The script now runs them as children and, after a failing exit (ctrl+c's 130 aside), waits for a
  key; `pick` itself waits only after a review, pin or release that worked, so a failure needs one key, not
  two.
- **A pin is a wait, not an error** (2026-10-07). A round behind a slot `magnum open` pinned read "slot"
  with the error mark: dispatch wrote "slot review1 is pinned (magnum unpin)" into `last_error`, and the
  operator asked what "retry, then slot" meant; a forced re-review waited 3h50m on such a pin unseen. The
  pin is the operator's own choice, so it is its own wait (`WaitPinned`: who pinned it and since when, from
  the newest pin event), with no `last_error` (an older daemon's pin error is cleared at the next dispatch):
  the cell reads `re-review · pinned → u`, the card "pinned by magnum open (u unpins)", and once a round has
  waited 30 minutes on the pin one toast per PR and pin (its key names the pin's time) says
  "talkable#N waits for your pin (magnum unpin …)". A pin still never lapses by itself and the round never
  takes another slot. A guard's persisted hold (a person's changes) stays an error. Rejected: unpinning
  after a while (the pin protects a person's work in the checkout).
- **A retry names its attempt and its cause** (2026-10-07). A PR whose setup failed 9 times in 27 minutes
  read `retry` throughout; the attempt was only on the card. The wait now carries the attempt to come and
  the attempts allowed (`retry 2/3`) and a word for the cause read from the failed attempt's error
  (`setup`, `judge lost`, `timeout`, `error`, `stopped`, `human active`, `agent busy`, `infra`), and a
  narrow STATE column drops the cause before anything else (`Wait.Narrow`). Rejected: the error's first
  line in the cell (a chain of contexts; the card and `magnum status <ref>` keep the sentence).
- **A mute has a reason and leaves the queue at once** (2026-10-07). 6 of 8 mutes came before any round
  and none said why; a PR muted while queued stayed `queued` 28 hours, until a restart's reclassification.
  `magnum mute <ref> [reason…]` sends the words after the PR as the request's `reason`, which the answer and
  a new `pr.muted` event keep; a mute of a PR waiting for an automatic round (queued or rereview_pending, not
  forced) moves it to ineligible (`muted`, the filters' reason) in a compare-and-set from those states, and
  `unmute` decides its eligibility again. A forced round still passes the mute. Rejected: a `--reason`
  flag (the words after the ref read as the reason, like a commit message).
- **Board keys promise only what the daemon does** (2026-10-07). `A` and `C` asked "magnum found no
  findings" while the FINDINGS cell said "✗ 3 open"; `x` was offered on running, paused and close-grace rows
  that cleanup's plan skips, `I` promised to free a pinned PR's slot that abort keeps, and `D` was offered on
  merged and closed rows. The verdict question now names the earlier findings still open ("no new findings;
  3 earlier findings still open"), `x` refuses those rows with the reason (`K` kills a round; the grace says
  when the slot goes), `I` leaves the slot out for a pinned PR, and `D` refuses a merged or closed PR. The
  board row carries the close grace's end (`ReleaseAfter`, `prs.release_after`, no migration).
- **`magnum prs` and `magnum status` say what the board says** (2026-10-07). Neither showed a snooze nor
  the "3 open" of a review that posted no new finding. The printed STATE adds `snoozed→18:00` while no
  round runs and FINDINGS `blocking 3 open`; a `magnum status` queue line adds `· snoozed → 18:00 · 3
  open` (`snoozed_until`, `open` in the JSON) and a PR's card its snooze on the state line. The board's
  needs-you pill no longer hides a PR that waits for a round, is paused or needs attention: those keep their
  state's pill (the card shows both). Rejected: a new column (the board stays one line per PR).
- **A key queued behind a quit does nothing** (2026-10-09). Bubble Tea passes a model the keys it has
  already read before it handles `tea.Quit`, and the screens acted on those keys. On the cleanup screen,
  the model ignored `done`. A `y` typed after ctrl+c, esc or q applied the plan the user had cancelled. An
  enter typed after the enter that confirmed the last typed text read past the end of the texts and
  panicked. On the board and the dashboard, `leave` returned `tea.Quit` without marking the screen as
  leaving when no action ran. ctrl+c is handled before the y/N question, so a `y` typed after it answered
  the question still on screen. After q, esc or tab, a key that asks a question and its `y` started the
  action. That action then ran on the context that RunPRBoard and RunDashboard cancel as they return. The
  picker also kept acting after it finished: esc, enter, y gave back a review instead of the cancel. Now
  the cleanup model and the picker ignore every message once they are done. The cleanup confirm step
  checks its index before it reads the next text. `leave` drops the question and sets `leaving` before it
  returns `tea.Quit`, so `leavingKey` gets the queued keys, as it already did while an action finished (q,
  esc and tab still choose between quitting and switching). Two pipeline tests had the same kind of race
  and were also made deterministic. A fake refusal could win before claude-review's hung Submit marked its
  run working, so the round's cut saw a pending run and sent no esc. Now the refusing fake first waits for
  that run to be working (`e.waitRun`), as `pushAfterCodex` already does. Rejected: dropping only the
  question on ctrl+c (a queued key that asks and its `y` would still start an action after q, esc or tab);
  a separate guard in each screen's key handler (`leavingKey` already is that guard).
- **PR completion filters by the typed text before its limit** (2026-10-09). completePRsWhere took the 200
  newest PRs (completeLimit) and left the filtering to the shell. Once more than 200 PRs were recorded, an
  older PR never completed: with 205 merged PRs, `magnum misses talkable/talkable#1<TAB>` did not offer
  #1. The query now keeps a PR when its owner/repo#N starts with the typed text (a case-insensitive LIKE,
  with the text's wildcards escaped), or, for a typed number, when the PR is in daemon.default_repo and
  its N starts with that number. The limit applies after this filter.
- **A NeedDaemon request whose withdrawal fails is reported as still able to run** (2026-10-09, after an
  audit: when no daemon answered, the CLI treated any failure of CompleteRequest except a conflict as a
  successful withdrawal and printed "nothing was queued", but the request stayed pending, and a daemon
  started later would post the review or verdict). send now switches on the error. nil: withdrawn
  (errNoDaemon). store.ErrConflict: a daemon took the request, and its answer is reported. Any other
  error: `request <id> may still run when a daemon starts: withdrawing it failed: <err>`, without
  errNoDaemon, with the request pending in the outcome. The withdrawal runs on context.WithoutCancel, so a
  ctrl-c during the kick still withdraws. Rejected: retrying the withdrawal in a loop (the CLI cannot
  outwait a broken registry; it says what happened instead).
- **A reviewing pill's spinner redraws only the rows whose pill spins** (2026-10-09, amends "Finding
  priorities are colored icons; a reviewing pill spins": the spinner's frame was part of the rows' cache
  key). The frame was in prbRowsKey. So while any PR in scope was in review, each of the spinner's eight
  frames a second emptied the board's natural-width, layout, summary and row caches, and every frame
  measured and laid out all rows again. On 200 rows a frame cost 6.1 ms and 6.9 MB, as much as a cold
  first frame. Now the frame is in the frame's key (prbFrameKey.anim) and in the summary's key (one entry
  per frame: the nerd mode's reviewing count spins). It is also in prbRowKey, but only for a row whose
  pill spins (workingState of rowState), as the shimmer is keyed. It is never in prbRowsKey, so the
  widths, the layout and the other rows are reused. BenchmarkBoardSpinnerFrame (200 rows): -96% time, -99%
  bytes (6.9 MB to 64 KB) and -96% allocations (13,312 to 547). Rejected: keeping the frame in the rows'
  key and caching only the layout under a key without it (every row would still be drawn again on every
  frame).
- **A slow column-width save never freezes the screen** (2026-10-09). widthSaver.save numbered each save
  under the mutex that a running save command holds across its SaveWidths store write. A drag or W while
  the registry was slow therefore blocked Bubble Tea's event loop until the earlier write ended. Saves now
  take their number from an atomic counter when they are made. Only the commands take the mutex: to write
  one at a time and to skip a save older than the last one written. Rejected: dropping the mutex (two
  writes could land out of order and undo a reset).
- **The watch screen passes styling only** (2026-10-09). `magnum watch --ansi` forwarded every escape
  sequence a pane printed: a clipboard write (OSC 52), a link (OSC 8), screen erases, cursor moves, a full
  reset. The plain mode stripped the sequences but kept BEL, BS and C1 controls. The header drew the
  pane's title, role, status and herdr's fetch error raw. Now paneText walks the text with
  ansi.DecodeSequence. The ANSI mode keeps only 7-bit SGR (ESC [, digits, ';' or ':', then m) and drops
  every other sequence, including an unfinished one at the end. In both modes every control character but
  the newline becomes a space (a tab is four spaces; a carriage return is dropped). The header's fields
  and the fetch error are cleaned. Rejected: allowing OSC 8 links (a pane's link can point anywhere);
  passing SGR introduced by a C1 CSI byte (terminals read raw C1 bytes differently).
- **A picker reload stops when the picker closes** (2026-10-09). Unlike RunDashboard, RunPRBoard and
  RunWatch, RunPicker had no cancel scope. A ctrl+r reload still in flight when the picker closed ran on
  until its 30 s timeout. RunPicker now cancels the context it gives Reload when it returns.
- **Every row action has its own call; an action without one fails** (2026-10-09). actionRun had no case
  for U (unmute): its catch-all ran Unmute, so an action added later without a case would have unmuted the
  PR. The picker's pickRowAct fell back to release for any action it did not know. Now actionRun has an
  explicit case for every action, and its default returns a call that fails ("row action N has no call");
  an out-of-range action gets the same call. pickRowAct maps release explicitly and returns false for
  cancel and for an unknown action; the picker then refuses with a note. TestEveryRowActionRunsItsOwnCall
  walks every rowAct and checks its name and its DashboardActions call.
- **The tui tests fail on a command that does not answer** (2026-10-09). execCmd treated a command still
  running after 150 ms as a timer and dropped it. An action descheduled on a busy machine could then make
  a test pass vacuously. Now execCmd(tb, cmd) waits up to 5 s and fails the test.
- **Each slots subcommand prints its own usage line** (2026-10-09). `magnum slots list`, provision,
  remove, repair, adopt, pin and unpin printed the family's line with every form of `magnum slots`. Now
  each prints `usage: magnum slots <subcommand> ...` from its own Use string, and the usage-line test no
  longer accepts a family line.

- **The board is `magnum tui`, and `magnum` alone opens it** (2026-10-15; the operator asked). `prs` named
  the rows, not the screen, and a bare `magnum` printed the help on stderr with exit 2. The command is `tui`
  (newPRsCmd and the prs_*.go files keep their names in the code), `prs` stays as its alias so scripts and
  the gh shim's examples keep working (`gh magnum tui` in the install text, `Aliases: prs` in the help), the
  usage errors say `magnum tui`, and `execute` turns no arguments into `tui`: the live board on a terminal,
  the printed rows elsewhere, so `magnum | head` lists the PRs. `magnum help` and `--help` list the commands
  as before, `magnum <command> --help` explains one, and `magnum --config x` without a command still
  prints the help. Rejected: dropping the `prs` alias (a rename with no grace costs every alias and script
  the operator has); keeping `magnum` at the help (the help is one word away, the board is what the
  operator opens many times a day).
- **The card's "posted as" compares like with like, and a running round's kind waits for its own
  round_start** (2026-10-16). The registry records what a review was posted as in GitHub's state names
  (`COMMENTED`, `APPROVED`, `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, pipeline normalizeEvent), and findingsLines compared them
  with the decision's request event (`COMMENT`, `APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`), so every posted review's card
  read "Decision: approve; posted as approved (A approves, C requests changes)". Both sides now go through
  normVerdict, and a real override (a clean verdict posted as a comment) still says so. The engine stamps a
  round's start (`last_round_started_at`, enterReviewing) before it writes `engine.round_start`, so for one
  refresh a running round's RoundWhy is the previous round's: a round after a delta check read "delta
  check". runningRoundWhy trusts RoundWhy for a running round only with a start of its own at or after the
  round's (the rule the cli's listNamedRoles already follows); until then the state cell shows the stage and
  the time with no kind, and the card's LAST ROUND the timeline without the previous round's roles and
  kind. A delta check that waits keeps its words, which the daemon's wait decides. Rejected: a new row field
  for the running round's kind (both times already reach the row).
- **A running round's row marks its kind with one cell after the pill** (2026-10-16; the operator chose the
  mockup). A round is a first review, a re-review, a recovery, a delta check, a full pass, the full pass
  before approval or an audit pass, and only the card said which; the row showed the words "delta check"
  and "post-merge" and nothing for the rest, while a running first review and a re-review both show the
  spinner. One classifier, roundKindOf, serves the card's phrase and the row: a delta check, then the full
  pass before approval, a full pass, an audit pass and a reply round win over the engine's kind. Right after
  the reviewing pill the state cell draws the kind's mark from glyphs.roundMark in the configured icon mode
  (nerd: Octicons sparkle_fill, sync, issue_reopened, diff, checklist, shield_check, telescope; unicode: ✦ »
  ✚ ∆ ◉ ⚑ ☑, all East Asian width N; ascii: 1 r rc d F F+ a), in the reviewing pill's color, then a plain
  space and the stage and time: `⣷ reviewing  ∆ judge · 4m`, narrowing to `⣷ reviewing  ∆ 4m` and
  `⣷ reviewing  ∆`, the mark kept as "delta check" was (a column dragged narrower still keeps the pill
  alone, not a cut one). A continue, a nudge and a reply round (`replies` from engine.round_start, now
  RoundWhy.Replies and `round_why.replies` in `magnum tui --json`; the card says "reply round (2 replies):
  judge only") say `continue`, `nudge` and `replies` in its place; a post-merge round keeps its word before
  it (`post-merge » judge · 4m`); a delta check that waits keeps its words, and its line count stays on
  the card. The `?` legend gains the round marks of the mode in use. No cache key changes: the mark derives
  from the loaded row and the glyph set, and a refresh advances the rows' generation. Rejected: a text tag
  after the pill (the STATE cell grows by up to 9 cells and drops UPDATED at 140 columns); a mark column
  (3 cells on every row, and a new column was rejected on 2026-10-05); marking only the rare kinds (a
  running first review and a re-review both show the spinner, so the operator's question stays open).
- **The row says why a PR needs you, that a clean review is held, and that a thread is argued**
  (2026-10-16; the operator approved the plan on spec 48's mockup). Over 14 days 32 `pr.needs_attention`
  events on 18 PRs had six causes (failed attempts 15, a capped fix loop 5, a fix call 4, blocked 4, the
  judge stopping 2, identity 2), and each asks something else (`r` retries, a fix call means reading the
  report, blocked means the judge's pane), yet the row read `attention` alone; 27 of 341 posted reviews were
  clean verdicts posted as comments, and the held ones read `✔ clean` while a full pass still decided the
  approval; 6 stalemates on 4 PRs shared the title's `!` with a failed round. Now the attention pill names
  its cause after it, dimmed as the skip word is (`attention · failed`, `· blocked`, `· identity`, `· fix`,
  `· overload`, `· no review`), from the reason kind the row already builds (prAttention's
  attention.Reason.Kind: the kind the engine recorded, `engine.KVPRAttention`, else the one Explain infers
  from the stored error), never from the rendered sentence; an unknown kind keeps `attention`, `fix` covers
  a fix call and a capped loop (they share the kind), the cause wins over a snooze's time, and
  attention.Kinds lists every kind so a new one without a word fails a test. FINDINGS reads `✔ held`
  (`held` in yellow, before the counts, the open findings and the simplifications) only when the latest
  posted review is the one the approval hold record names (`engine.KVPRApprovalHold`, now exported with
  `engine.HeldReviewID`; the engine's heldReviewOf rule: a later review drops the record, and one left
  behind names an older review, so the later one reads clean); a clean verdict posted as a comment is not a
  hold by itself, since a
  comment-only identity posts every clean verdict so, and only a clean summary reads the record. A reviewed
  PR with stalemate threads reads `reviewed · argued`; a running round, a wait, a snooze and the cells that
  replace the pill (`✔ auto`, `✔ needs you`) keep precedence, and the title's `!` stays. `magnum tui
  --json` gains `attention_kind` and `findings.held`; argued derives from `stalemate_threads`. The legend
  gains the two state lines and the held item. No migration and no new query for the cause (prAttention
  already reads the kind); one kv read per row with a clean latest review for the hold. Neither word is
  wider than a wait (`attention · no review` is 22 cells, `re-review  quiet → 14:09` 25), so where a PR
  waits or a round runs no column moves, as the painter draws it (unicode; nerd and ascii keep the same
  columns):

  ```text
  100 columns
    REPO           #  TITLE                           STATE                       FINDINGS   REVIEWERS
  ▌ talkable  #12001  ! Speed up the referral grid…    attention · failed         ✗ P1 P2×2  rev-ann✔
    talkable  #12002  ! Add the coupon list importer   attention · fix            ● P2×2     rev-ann✔

    talkable  #12002  ! Add the coupon list importer        alice   —               40m  —           attention · fix            ★ 💬 commented 1h  ● P2×2     ✓ 65/65  1c +12 −3     rev-ann✔

    talkable  #12004  ! Retry the webhook delivery on 5xx   alice   —               40m  —           reviewed · argued          ★ 💬 commented 1h  ● P2       ✓ 65/65  1c +12 −3     rev-ann✔

    talkable  #12006  Bump rails to 7.2.1                   alice   —               40m  —           re-review  quiet → 14:09   ★ 💬 commented 1h  ● P3×2     ✓ 65/65  1c +12 −3     rev-ann✔
    talkable  #12007  Split the payouts job                 alice   —               40m  —           ⣷ reviewing  ∆ judge · 4m  ★ 💬 commented 1h  ● P2       ✓ 65/65  1c +12 −3     rev-ann✔
  ```

  On a board where nothing waits or runs, STATE grows by up to 11 cells, as a wait's text grows it: at 100
  columns LAST REVIEW gives way, at 140 AUTHOR. Rejected: a `no auto` title tag for a stopped
  auto-approval (the stop can be the operator's own doing, the card explains it, and a tag shortens every
  title); a whiteboard mark and a trivial-push mark (rarely acted on); agent time on the row (cost only, and
  cost-only items were dropped on 2026-10-12); `fix call` for the fix kind (a failed fixer run shares it,
  so the word would overpromise); the cause inside the red pill (it grows the pill, and every other word
  after a pill is dimmed text); a narrower form that drops the cause with a running round's stage (the cause
  is what decides the operator's next key, as a wait's text is, which keeps its words too).
- **Starred PRs lead the board** (2026-10-16, the operator approved spec 55's mockup). The operator must
  deliver some PRs, usually their own and sometimes a colleague's. They want these PRs always at the top,
  newest update first, whatever sort the other rows use. Before this change, nothing moved a row up. The
  pin is a slot mark and a title tag. A badge never reorders, because "the sort is the reviewer's choice".
  The ★ mark means yours.

  Now the board's `*` and `magnum star <ref> [--off] [--json]` star a PR. The kv key `pr.<id>.star`
  (`store.KVPRStar`) holds `{"at": <RFC 3339>, "by": "the board" | "magnum star"}`. No key means not
  starred, and an unstar deletes the key. One setter writes the registry directly: setPRStar in the CLI,
  which both paths reach through starMain. There is no daemon request and no migration. A second star keeps
  the first record. `magnum star` sets the state and never toggles it. It resolves the reference as `magnum
  snooze` does, refuses a PR that the registry does not know, and prints the result.

  The board's source reads every star in one query: the new `store.KVValues` returns the keys of `pr.*.star`
  with their values. The source sets PRBoardRow.Starred and StarredAt before the board filters and sorts.
  Thus the live board, the printed rows and `tui --json` agree. The printed rows get a `starred` flag in
  STATE. The JSON gets `starred` on every row and `starred_at` while it is set.

  SortPRBoard keeps the open block and the recently closed block. In each block, starred rows come first.
  Two starred rows compare by ActivityAt, newest first, then by reference. This comparison comes before
  the Recent order, the needs-you rule and the chosen sort and direction. A starred merged PR thus leads the
  Recent block. It leaves with its window like any closed PR, and a reopened PR returns starred. A star
  never shows a row that the owner scope, a view, the filter or `h` hides. Other people set labels, and so
  a badge does not change the order. The operator sets each star, and so a star does.

  The mark is the first tag of the title, before the pin. It is yellow and a space follows it. The nerd mode
  draws nf-oct-feed_star U+F4CD, the Unicode mode ✪ U+272A (East Asian width N, one cell) and the ASCII
  mode the word `star`. The ★ mark stays yours. The summary line adds `✪ N starred` after the pins. The
  card adds the line `✪ starred 2h ago (* unstars)`. The `?` legend adds
  `✪ starred: floats to the top, * toggles; ★ is still yours`, and its keys add `* star or unstar`.

  The `*` key toggles at once, without a y/N question. The table's hints label it star or unstar where a
  set has room for it. The card and the menu label it too. It starts and stops no work, only the board reads
  the star, and the same key undoes it. The keys `p`, `u`, `o`, `b` and `t` also run at once. The y/N rule
  above stays for every action that starts or stops work. Only the board has the key. The dashboard's
  queue is the daemon's queue. The queue, eligibility, throttling and `magnum pick` ignore stars.

  The live board's `--limit` capped the registry query, which orders by the last update, before the board's
  own sort. An old starred PR fell off before it moved up. Now the source reads every matching row, and the
  board caps the rows after its view, filter and sort (PRBoardOptions.Limit), as the printed rows did. The
  summary line counts every row in scope. The README and `magnum tui --help` said "starred" for yours. They
  now say "marked ★".

  The real painter draws these rows in TestTheStarredBoardMockup, the mockup test. Three PRs are starred:
  the operator's own PR with a failed round (updated 50h ago), a colleague's PR (updated 90m ago) and a
  merged PR. The cursor is on the first row. The summary line ends with `📌 1 pinned   ✪ 3 starred`, or
  `pin 1 pinned   star 3 starred` in ASCII.

  Rejected alternatives:
  - A `prs.starred` column. It needs a migration and a drained restart for a field that only the screens
    read.
  - A mark in the cell after the cursor. That cell is one cell wide, the queued mark ◷ shares it, and the
    mark touches REPO.
  - ⭐ as the mark. It is two cells wide, and the nerd mode has an icon.
  - The chosen sort inside the starred group. The operator asked for the newest update first.
  - A star as a queue priority. A star is what the operator tracks, not a request for review capacity. A
    board key that changes usage and scheduling is a risk.
- **A held review's card, the printed table's `held`, and a dead attention branch** (2026-10-17, spec 70).
  Three leftovers of the held-review, printed-board and fix-loop work. (1) A clean review that held its
  approval (`approve_after_full_pass`) posts COMMENTED by design, and the card compared the posted event
  with the verdict only, so its decision read "posted as commented (A approves, C requests changes)" and
  invited the A that the hold postpones, although `FindingsInfo.Held` reached the card. Now `findingsLines`
  reads it first: the line is "Decision: approve; held: posted as a comment, the approval waits for the full
  pass", with no key hint; a clean comment with no hold (a comment-only repository) keeps its "posted as"
  words and its hint, and the card's ACTIONS footer, which lists A for every PR, is unchanged (A still
  approves by hand, which the operator may choose). (2) The printed `magnum tui` STATE listed the other
  board flags but not the hold, which the live board shows as `✔ held`; `prsStateCell` now adds `held`
  after `stalemate` when the row's findings are held (`tui --json` already had `findings.held`), so the
  three readings agree. (3) `attention.Explain` carried a reading for the end the pre-87fa4f0 fix hook
  wrote ("fix loop ended: the re-review did not post (replied)"): a re-review the loop forces never ends
  replied since the loop decides only on the round it forced, no row carries the text (0 rows) and the
  code cannot write it again, so the regexp, its branch and its test are gone and every other fix reading
  stays. Tests: TestAHeldReviewsCardOffersNoApproveHint (tui, with the card at 100 and 140 columns),
  TestThePrintedStateFlagsAHeldReview and the printed line in TestFindingsReadHeldOnlyForTheHeldReview
  (cli). Rejected: keeping the dead branch for rows an older daemon wrote (none exist, and a row that did
  would read as the loop's own end, which says what happened); hiding A on a held card (the operator may
  approve by hand, so the key stays and only the line stops inviting it).
- **The settings screen: `magnum settings`, and `,` on the dashboard and the PR board** (2026-10-20, spec 95,
  asked for by the operator: "make me form with settings, like other TUIs have, so I can change spend and other
  stuff without editing config toml", using huh, lipgloss and Bubble Tea "with all magic"; the layout was
  mocked up through the real styles and approved with six changes). The screen is internal/tui's
  settings*.go over two small interfaces, `tui.SettingsSource` (the file, the resolved roles, the plan and
  the commit, which the cli adapts from internal/settings, spec 94) and `tui.SettingsRuntime` (the pauses);
  the screen never parses TOML and never writes a byte itself. Layout: the title (`magnum · settings`, the
  scope, the file, `N unsaved`, and `restart pending` on the right while the daemon runs an older file than
  the saved one, from spec 94's `daemon.config_sha256`), a rail of sections (Runtime, then the source's
  sections in its order, Spend & models first) with a yellow ● on each holding unsaved edits, one line per
  setting (label, value, state: `default` dim, `set`, `● unsaved` yellow, `✗ invalid` red; a list shows its
  items under its first one, up to five lines), a three-line detail strip (the TOML key and "applies after
  restart" or "applies now"; the description, or the loader's words for an invalid value; "was", the
  default and where the value comes from), and the footer through fitHints. The six approved changes:
  (1) Spend & models lists only the spend level and each kind's spend; the roles grid (role, model, first
  and re-review effort, as magnum's own loader resolves the draft, `Preview`) is the editable part: enter
  on a role opens its popup, which edits the role's cells in its level's `[spend.<level>]` table or its
  base `[[role]]` model, one field a page; (2) save is two steps: `s` shows the diff of the exact lines
  (each hunk's table heading and line; `n` turns the dated notes off and on), and only its own `s` asks
  "Save N changes to ~/.config/magnum/config.toml? y/N" on magnum's confirmLine, where only `y` writes;
  (3) at 125 columns or more the grid stands beside the list, and below it the roles become list rows
  (`opus* high/-`) and the grid under the list lists only the roles whose model or effort changes (a level
  that resolves the same changes nothing a role runs): the literal reading of the change, which keeps the
  roles editable on a narrow screen without repeating the unchanged ones; (4) the Runtime rows have short
  action labels (`p pause`, `r resume codex`, `R resume all`) and the strip's last line gives the full
  command and what it does; (5) the grid's `*` and yellow mark what differs from the saved file, not from
  the running daemon, and the title says `restart pending` for the daemon; (6) the dated note's rule is
  spec 94's. After a save that changes what the daemon reads at start the screen asks "Restart the daemon
  when it is idle to apply? y/N": `y` writes spec 94's restart mark (`RequestRestart`), anything else
  leaves `restart pending`. huh is a field editor, not the frame: each edit is a small huh form in a box
  over the list (a Select for an enum, a bool, an effort or a model, whose "other…" opens an Input; an Input
  with the setting's check for a duration, a number, a percent or a 300-character text, empty putting the
  default back; a MultiSelect for a watch's roles with its one-judge check; a list editor of its own for
  logins, repositories and checks, which stages each add, edit or remove at once, so `u` takes each back and
  esc only closes it), themed from magnum's 16-colour styles, with huh's quit key (ctrl+c, which aborted
  silently) disabled so the screen asks before discarding, a Select's filter and a Text's external editor
  off, and a WindowSizeMsg sent after the form is built and after every message (an embedded form sizes
  itself only from one, and a description evaluated late or a page shown or hidden changes its height).
  A Select writes its bound value on every cursor move, so the spend popup's candidate is resolved as the
  cursor moves and the grid previews it ("preview: burn") without staging; esc cancels and the grid goes
  back to the draft. No huh Confirm is used anywhere (its enter submits whichever side is toggled, and y or
  n answers and moves on). A Select's first choice is always the default, which an unset key starts on, so
  enter keeps what applies (the review found an unset bool staging its opposite). While the draft is
  checked or saved the keys that change it wait, a plan answers only the draft it was made of, and every
  command's answer names the screen that asked, so a screen opened again with `,` drops the answers of the
  one before. Runtime is not config: its rows (automation, each agent kind, all kinds, each
  watch's identity-leak pause) read what `magnum status` reads and act through the same code `magnum pause`
  and `magnum resume` run (a pause form of how long, for or until, and a reason; `r` on the selected row;
  `R` for every kind), each after its own y/N, and they say "applies now · not saved to the config file";
  a plain resume's answer names the agent-kind and watch pauses it leaves, which the CLI's answer does not.
  `,` (free on both screens) opens the screen inside the same program: a host model keeps the dashboard or
  the board, routes the keys to settings while it shows and every other message to both, so the screen
  that opened it keeps its timers, its data and an action in flight, and esc brings it back with the same
  cursor, filter and scroll without rebuilding anything. The screen runs without mouse mode (a click
  reaches nothing and the terminal keeps its own selection), its frames are cached by a generation bumped
  only by messages it shows, it starts dark and follows tea.BackgroundColorMsg, every state is spelled out
  in words for a colorless terminal, and every text a load hands it is cleaned of terminal controls. Other
  keys: `/` searches labels and keys across every section and scope (a leading `*` keeps what the file sets
  or the draft changes), `c` picks the scope (Global, each watch by position with its owner and first
  repositories, each repository, a watched one without a block saying a save creates it), `[` and `]` move
  between watches or repositories, `d` stages the default (the key goes, its comment stays), `u` undoes
  the last staged edit, `?` lists the keys, and esc, q or ctrl+c ask "Discard N unsaved changes? y/N" when
  the draft holds any. The cli adapts spec 94's internal/settings (settings_source.go): one row per
  [[watch]] and per repository from the templates, each value checked by Snapshot.Check before it is
  staged, the loader's refusal shown without its "config <the layers read>: " prefix (its paths pushed the
  reason off the line), a restart the daemon refused on the file as it is shown as a warning, and
  `--history` listing the kept versions numbered as `--restore` takes them; tui.NewSettings exports the
  model so a program of the caller's embeds it, which the end-to-end test does over a synthetic config.
  Two reviews of the screen hardened it. Every popup has an id that tags its form's commands (their
  batches and sequences too), so what a cancelled popup's form answers late never reaches the next one;
  a cursor's blink stays untagged, since it names its cursor. huh's g and G move a Select without
  writing its value, so the screen reads each Select's hovered option after every message and sets its
  description itself (no huh evaluation runs on another goroutine reading the bound value); huh keeps
  the first theme a field gets, so the popup's theme reads the screen's styles through a pointer, and a
  background answer redraws it; a resize sizes it again. The grid takes a role's level from the roles
  of the draft alone, never a popup's candidate, and a role popup waits while the draft's roles are on
  their way; a cancelled picker shows the draft's roles at once. Values stay as the file has them (an
  untouched list entry is staged back byte for byte) and are cleaned only where shown; an empty list
  shows what it stands for ("every author"); a row that inherits follows a staged edit of what it
  inherits ("inherit (burn)"); duplicates in a list follow the setting's matching (logins and
  repositories whatever their case, check names as written); a Select offers a saved value off its
  list as "(saved)" rather than start on another; emptying a list the file never set stages nothing; a
  runtime answer older than the latest read is dropped; a paste reaches the open Input or the search; a
  loader refusal marks only a setting whose whole key path it names; the Runtime section numbers the
  watches as the scopes do; each item a list editor types has a form of its own generation, so an earlier
  item's late answer never submits the next; `d` on a role waits for the draft's roles as its popup does; and
  a kind's spend inherits [pipeline] spend on the screen only when no layer sets it (a base config's
  `[kinds.codex] spend = "low"` stays low when another level is staged). A save refused because the file
  changed on disk (tui.ErrSettingsChanged, which the adapter wraps around settings.ErrChanged) asks "Read it
  again and keep the N staged edits? y/N"; every reload that meets staged edits drops an edit of a watch whose
  position another watch now holds (another owner, or the same owner with other repositories, as when two of
  one owner's watches swap), and after a save the keys that change the draft wait until the saved file's rows
  are read. `--history` and a restore work over a file that no longer loads, through settings.History and
  settings.RestoreFile (a small addition to spec 94's package, its own commit); the restart answer says when
  launchd does not run the daemon (as `magnum status` tells it: launchd's pid is the daemon's) and names
  `magnum daemon-restart --when-idle`. The colorless golden frame, identical to the plain one, became a test
  that every state reads without color. Not taken: refusing an uppercase Y (every magnum screen confirms with
  y or Y).
  Rejected: huh as the whole screen (a form is a line of fields with no rail, search,
  per-section marker or jump, dead after completion, and its errors block leaving a group); `,` as a screen
  switch through runScreens (leaving the board cancels its context and with it an action in flight, and its
  cursor, filter and scroll would have to be carried over by hand); applying edits live as some TUIs do
  (the daemon reads the config only at start, and a spend change must not happen on a stray key); a stage
  key in the list editor (esc would have had two meanings); teatest (one more dependency for what driving
  Update with key messages already tests).
- **`magnum open` holds what it restores for a while and asks first** (2026-10-22, spec 121, approved by the
  operator). At 02:51 local the operator ran `magnum open` on talkable#12048 to look at its panes. Its judge
  had been parked an hour earlier by spec 119's login change, so open restored the PR: it claimed review8,
  checked out the reviewed SHA, resumed the judge and pinned the PR and the slot ("magnum open: restored in
  review8 at 7469270, pinned"), with no question first (rowacts listed open among the keys that run at
  once). The operator: "why does open pin stuff without confirmation? I expected to open herdr panes, not pin
  something". The pin lasted until `magnum unpin`, so the paused round of 12048 could not continue; the
  `magnum fix` unpins entry above records the same cost (the board's `f` failed twice on a PR open had pinned
  30 hours earlier). Now the restore is a hold: the same pin, so every guard that leaves a pinned PR or slot
  alone (dispatch's slotGate, the idle park, the release and cleanup plans, eviction, the session restart,
  the fix and whiteboard jobs) applies unchanged, plus a record (engine.KVPROpenHold, `pr.<id>.open_hold`:
  until = the open plus the new `[daemon] open_hold`, default `30m`) that a restart keeps. The hold ends at
  the later of that and `human_cooldown` after the PR's human_active_at (the last input in its panes), when
  the tick, before dispatch, unpins the PR and its slot with one `pr.open_hold_ended` event, so a paused or
  queued round goes on in the same tick. It clears the slot's pin as a review's unpin does (ClearPin), not
  as `magnum unpin` (Unpin also acknowledges a head_drift or unpushed_commits hold by taking the folder's
  HEAD as the checkout): an automatic end must never hand a person's commits to the next release. `magnum
  pin` drops the record (a lasting pin, which the answer says), every unpin drops it too (`magnum unpin`, a
  review's or a fix's), a record whose PR is no longer pinned goes at the next tick, `open_hold = "0"`
  writes none (today's lasting pin), and an open of a PR a lasting pin already keeps leaves that pin as it
  is. A wait on the hold carries its end (`re-review · held → 03:21`, "slot review8 is held by magnum open
  until 03:21; `magnum unpin` lets it run now (the hold ends by itself)") and toasts nothing; the board's
  state cell says `held → 03:21` where nothing else waits, the card "held by open until 03:21 (u hands it
  back, p keeps it)" and the summary pill counts holds apart from pins; `magnum status` says "held by open
  until 03:21" on the pins line and the card, with `held_until` in the JSON. Open asks only when it would
  restore: the board's row knows it (PRBoardRow.OpenRestores, from the sessions of the role o opens, the
  judge or the fixer at work: none live and one parked, as openRestore decides), and `o` there asks
  "Restore talkable#12048 in a slot to read it? It holds the PR until 30 minutes after your last input."
  (the duration from open_hold; "until you unpin it" for 0); `magnum open` asks the same on a terminal
  before it sends the request, `--yes` skips it, and `--json` and a script never ask, as the herdr plugin
  and scripts call open. A focus of a live pane asks nothing and holds nothing. Existing pins: the newest pin
  event of a PR is what pinOrigin reads, and `pr.opened` says open made the pin, so at the start a pinned PR
  without a hold whose newest pin event is the open's gets a hold ending open_hold after the start (one
  `pr.open_hold_set` event); a `magnum pin` or `magnum slots pin` pin stays lasting, as does one the pruned
  events no longer remember; `pr.open_hold_ended` counts as an unpin for pinOrigin and PinnedSince. The
  picker's open runs `magnum open`'s code on its terminal once the picker closes, so it asks there; the
  dashboard's `o` does not know the PR's sessions, so it still restores without asking (with the hold,
  which ends by itself). Rejected: asking on every `o` (a focus of a live pane is the common case
  and changes nothing); no hold at all (the restored judge would be parked again by the idle park, which the
  two-step park makes quick, and the panes the operator is reading would close under them); keeping the
  lasting pin with a reminder toast (the round still waits until the operator acts, which is what the
  evidence shows they forget).
- **`magnum open` restores through any parked session when the judge's is gone** (2026-10-27, wave 1 of the
  fix loop's design, section 5.5, approved by the operator). A plain `magnum open` of a PR refused: "the
  codex-judge session is closed: `magnum review` starts a new round with fresh sessions", while its
  claude-review session was parked, and `magnum open --role claude-review` restored the PR at once. The
  refusal knew only the role it opened, the judge's, and the parked conversation of another role was one flag
  away. Now, without `--role`, when the role open would open has nothing to open (its newest session is
  lost or closed, none of its sessions is parked or up) and no session of the PR is starting or live,
  the newest parked session of any role by `started_at` (the later one of two that started together) takes
  its place: `openMain` asks for that role's restore, so the request, the question on a terminal, the hold
  and the wait are those of `--role <that role>`, and the answer line names the role it focused. The rule is
  one function over the PR's sessions (openRestoreRole), and the board's `o` asks the same question:
  openRoleOf names that role (the fixer's while its loop works, else the judge's, then the stand-in) and
  openWouldRestore applies the rule to the role it is given, so the board says "restores" for exactly the
  rows open restores, and `o` asks y/N first. A lost judge session counts as the closed one: openRestore's
  refusal already treats both alike (the role's pane is gone with its session), and a lost session has no
  conversation to restore either. Unchanged: a role named with `--role` is never replaced (its own refusal
  stands, with a parked session of another role beside it); a live or starting session of the PR, of any
  role, keeps today's focus of a live pane (the restore replaces the refusal, not the focus: `o` would
  otherwise ask to claim a slot for a PR whose panes are up); a judge that never had a session still says
  "has no session yet"; with no parked session the refusal is the same text. A parked role the watch no
  longer runs keeps the judge's refusal in `magnum open` (the board's row may ask first and then refuse: a
  config edit between two sessions, not worth a config read in the row's query). Rejected: restoring
  through the judge's own parked session only (the case here has none); asking the operator which parked
  role to restore (the newest is the one the PR was last worked in, and `--role` remains for another); the
  daemon choosing the role (its open request already takes any role, and the CLI is the one that reads
  the sessions to ask y/N). Tests, failing first: TestOpenWithoutARoleRestoresThroughAParkedSessionWhenTheJudgesIsClosed
  (closed and lost judge, a newer claude-review and an older claude-simplify parked: one open request for
  claude-review, no refusal), TestOpenOfAClosedJudgeRefusesWhenNoSessionIsParkedOrARoleIsNamed,
  TestOpenOfAClosedJudgeFocusesALivePaneBeforeItRestoresAParkedOne and
  TestTheBoardsOpenFollowsTheParkedSessionWhenTheJudgesIsGone.
- **`magnum open` stands in only with a role the daemon restores** (2026-10-27, the wave 1 review; amends
  "`magnum open` restores through any parked session when the judge's is gone"). Park parks every session
  with a session id, the fixer's (claude-fix), the whiteboard writer's and a judge's in reserve too, and
  the daemon's open takes only the roles the watch runs (`RolesFor`): the newest parked session of any role
  could be claude-fix, which the CLI accepted (its fix-role fallback), asked y/N for and sent, and the
  daemon refused with `unknown role "claude-fix"`; a parked whiteboard or reserve judge session kept the
  judge's refusal beside an older parked claude-review, while the board's `o` said "restores". The stand-in
  is now the newest parked session of a role the daemon's open restores (`openRestorable`, over
  `cfg.RolesFor(cfg.WatchFor(repo))`), in `openMain`, `openRoleOf` and `openWouldRestore` alike; without a
  config any role may, as before. Test, failing first: TestOpenStandsInOnlyWithARoleTheDaemonRestores (a
  newer parked claude-fix, claude-whiteboard and claude-judge beside an older parked claude-review: the
  open, and the board, pick claude-review; with only the fixer's and the writer's parked, the judge's
  refusal and no request).

## Operations

- **The daemon exits when the schema was migrated under it** (another binary ran a newer migration);
  launchd restarts it on the new build. Rebuild and restart together.
- **Events and requests are pruned** (`keep_events` 30 d, `keep_requests` 7 d), keeping the rows the
  crash-resume logic still reads.
- **In-process slot work takes `state/ops.lock`**; a daemon that finds its own lock held and
  `ops.lock` held exits non-zero so launchd retries.
- **This repository is public.** Nothing private appears in tracked files or history; `make test` runs
  `check-private` with patterns kept only in the gitignored `.mise.local.toml`. Personal identities,
  watches and pools live in `config.local.toml`; `config.toml.example` is a complete worked setup.
- **Linux is a todo** (launchd, AppleScript reveal, `open`, `osascript` are the macOS-only parts); the
  code cross-compiles.
- **Subprocess transcripts log at debug, failures at warn** (2026-10-04). 87% of daemon log lines were
  `exec` lines of successful commands; execx now logs them at debug and a non-zero exit, failed start or
  timeout at warn, always with the redacted command line, when its logger takes levels
  (`execx.LevelLogger`). Rejected: dropping the transcript (it is what explains a failed git or gh call).
- **Doctor checks only what the configuration uses** (2026-10-04). MySQL is checked only when a `[[pool]]`
  declares databases; `mise exec` only with a pool; the login-shell shims only when mise is on PATH, a
  pool exists or the LaunchAgent starts the daemon through mise; otherwise they report SKIP. A new
  `launchd mise` check fails when the installed LaunchAgent's mise does not exist, because launchd then
  cannot start magnum at all. Rejected: unconditional checks (a second machine without DBngin or mise saw
  failures with fixes it did not need).
- **An infrastructure failure pauses dispatch once and is never charged to a PR** (2026-10-04, after every
  fetch failed with `Permission denied (publickey)` for ten hours and five PRs went to needs_attention with
  an error that read like theirs). A checkout whose error names a refused SSH key, DNS, a network timeout or
  refusal or TLS, or a dependency step failing with the same exit status and last stderr line on two PRs
  within ten minutes, sets `daemon.infra_paused_until`: no round starts, one urgent toast (key `infra`), the
  PR goes back in line without an attempt. When the wait ends a probe runs `git ls-remote origin HEAD` in the
  failing clone (else any watched clone) with gitx's environment; success lifts the pause, failure doubles
  the wait (2 to 30 minutes). `magnum resume` lifts it at once. Rejected: per-PR retries (they spent the
  attempts of every PR on the same outage) and a per-repository pause (an SSH agent or DNS failure is
  global).
- **The build that will run checks the configuration and the prompts first** (2026-10-04, after 138
  crash-loop restarts on an unknown config key and 14 runs that failed on template fields the running daemon
  lacked). `magnum config` validates and renders every prompt file the roles name with this binary's
  template data (twice: every field set, optional fields empty, so both sides of an `{{if}}` run);
  `daemon-restart` and `install` run `bin/magnum config` and refuse with its error; the daemon checks the
  same before it starts and writes the refusal to stderr (launchd.log) and daemon.log. Rejected: checking
  with the CLI that runs the command (it need not be the binary launchd starts) and parsing templates only
  (a parse cannot know which fields the data has).
- **Restarts can drain** (2026-10-04; 12 of 42 rounds were killed by restarts). `daemon-restart --drain`
  and `install --drain` set `daemon.draining` straight in the registry (no migration: the running daemon's
  schema may be older), so the daemon starts no round, wait until none is in flight (a line every 15 s, at
  most `--timeout`, 2 h), restart, and lift the flag; the new daemon lifts it too when it starts, and giving
  up or ctrl+c lifts it without restarting. `--now` still restarts at once (the dev loop). Rejected: a
  daemon that waits for its rounds on SIGTERM (launchd and the CLI would wait without a word).
- **Urgent toasts never block the loop; informational ones are batched** (2026-10-04, the engine half of
  the notifier change). Needs-you, attention, tool and budget pauses, identity health, token refresh, the
  identity leak, low disk and the infrastructure pause go through `ToastUrgent` in goroutines that shutdown
  waits for (10 s) and then cancels, releasing their dedupe keys. Posted reviews and new repositories share
  one batcher, so 14 repositories found at once are one toast. The tab-bar file starts with when it was
  written and its max age (three poll intervals); the command `magnum install` prints shows "magnum down"
  when it is older, while a plain `cat` still shows the status line. Rejected: the file's mtime (unchanged
  content is not rewritten, and `stat` flags differ between macOS and Linux).
- **Re-reviews honour a reply contract** (2026-10-04, after magnum left all 23 author replies unread and one
  "moot" answer stayed "still open" through two re-reviews without a reason). Before a re-review the pipeline
  reads the PR's review threads over GraphQL (`github.ReviewThreads`), keeps those the posting login started,
  classifies every other reply by its first words (`fixed`/`done`/`addressed`, `not a bug`/`by design`/
  `intended`, `won't fix`/`out of scope`/`follow-up`, a leading `(Claude)` skipped) and writes them to
  `review-threads.json` next to the reports; the prompt names the file and the counts, never the reply text,
  because replies are PR content. The skill accepts `fixed` only when the code at the head shows it, honours
  `not a bug` and `won't fix` with a reason unless the judge proves the reason wrong (then one sentence in that
  thread, posted after the review is read back), sends standing decisions to the repository notes, and lists
  each old finding as fixed, answered or still open with a one-line reason. A failed read leaves the judge to
  read the replies itself. Rejected: replies inside the prompt (PR text in a prompt), trusting resolved
  threads (the authors' tools resolve every thread they answer) and a model classifier (the judge checks every
  claim anyway; a deterministic parser only sorts them).
- **Finding provenance, then `magnum stats`** (2026-10-04; raw acceptance misled: Claude's 28% hid that it
  was the only source of 9 of 24 posted findings). The result file lists every finding the judge weighed under
  `provenance` with its sources (roles, `judge` for its own pass), its verdict and, for a rejection, one of
  seven reason codes. A posted round stores them in the `findings` table (migration 0005), replacing the
  run's rows; a result without provenance stores none. `magnum stats` reads only the registry: rounds by
  start day and repository with their outcome (the latest `round.end`, else the judge run's), finding counts
  from each posted result's `findings` (so older rounds count too), median and p90 per role over finished
  spans, per-source judged, posted, unique and rejected counts with reasons, and model switches, denies and
  round restarts from events. Rejected: acceptance from the `candidates` counts (they cannot show unique
  contributions) and a separate metrics store (the registry already holds every input).
- **Prompts are loaded once, at startup** (2026-10-04; supersedes "Prompts are files under `prompts/`, read
  at prompt time"). Reading them at prompt time let an edit reach the running daemon mid-round, and an edit
  meant for the next build failed renders until the restart. The daemon now loads every prompt its roles
  name, `model-fallback.md` and each judge's skill once, right after the start check rendered them, and
  renders that snapshot once more before the first tick (an edit landing in between makes it exit; the next
  start refuses with the check's error). Rounds render from the snapshot. The skill is a file the judge reads
  itself, so judges get a copy, `state/skill/<first 12 hex of its SHA-256>/SKILL.md` (copies no judge uses
  are pruned after a week). Every reconcile compares the files with the snapshot (size and mtime, then
  SHA-256) and records the changed ones (`daemon.prompts_changed`, an event when the set changes) for
  `magnum status`: "prompts: loaded <time>, N files changed on disk since". The CLI (`magnum config`,
  `magnum roles`, doctor) still reads the files on disk. A prompt edit therefore takes `daemon-restart`, as a
  new template field did already. Rejected: watching the files and reloading in place (a reload needs the
  same render check, and a half-written file would reach a round).
- **An App approval follows the head** (2026-10-04; in one repository that needs one approval and keeps
  approvals across pushes, 24 of 50 approved merges in 30 days landed commits newer than the approval). When
  a PR's last magnum review by an App identity (the configured App whose login posted it) approved it and
  the poller sees a head with commits that approval did not see (GitHub's compare of the approved commit and
  the head; a failed compare counts as new commits), magnum dismisses the approval as that App with
  "magnum: new commits since this approval; a re-review follows" before the re-review is queued, records
  `review.approval_dismissed` and the review's event as DISMISSED. A head without new commits keeps it
  (`review.approval_kept`); `keep_approvals = true` on the `[[repo]]` (or the `[[watch]]`) keeps them all;
  other logins' reviews are never touched; a 403 is reported once (`review.approval_dismiss_refused`) and not
  retried, other failures every poll. An approval posted on a head that moved during its round goes at the
  next poll. Rejected: relying on the re-review (a merge during the quiet period carries the stale approval,
  and a later COMMENT review does not withdraw an approval on GitHub).
- **Verification readiness runs before the reviewers** (2026-10-04; in 9 of 18 posted rounds the judge
  skipped or failed a check it wanted, and four Ruby-blocked rounds burned about 160 reviewer agent-minutes
  before the judge found the cause). `[[repo]]` and `[[pool]]` take `prepare` (commands such as
  `bin/rails db:test:prepare`), `ready` (probes, exit 0 = ready) and `ready_timeout` (5m, for all of them
  together); a `[[repo]]` key replaces the pool's. Before the reviewers of an initial, re-review or recovery
  round the pipeline runs them in the checkout as `zsh -lc <command>` with the slot's env (the login shell
  the agents' tools use), then checks that `ruby -v` there runs the Ruby the checkout pins (`.mise.toml`
  `[tools] ruby`, else `.ruby-version`, read through `os.Root`). A failure never stops the round. The results
  go to `readiness.json` next to the result file (with each command's last output line), to the judge
  prompt's `readiness` list (status and magnum's own reason only, because output is PR text) and to a
  `round.readiness` event; the skill has the judge read the list before any check and record failures under
  `environment_failures`. A restart on a newer head keeps the round's first result. Rejected: stopping the
  round on a failed prepare (most findings need no test run), and probes taken from the repository notes
  (the judge writes them from PR-influenced experience; magnum runs only configured commands).
- **A push of comments, whitespace or docs is not re-reviewed** (2026-10-04; one PR got a 16-minute re-review
  by three agents for a commit that only reworded YAML comments, and its judge said so). Before a re-review is
  queued, and when a review posts while its head moved during the judge's turn, the poller asks GitHub for the
  delta's patches in one compare call (`github.CompareFiles`) and `engine.TrivialDelta` classifies them: every
  file modified (not added, removed or renamed) with a complete patch, and every added or removed line blank,
  a whitespace-only change of its counterpart in the same run of lines (indentation counts in Python, YAML and
  Makefiles), or a comment of the file's type, or the file is documentation (`.md`, `.txt`, `.rst`, `.adoc`,
  `docs/`). Comments that change behaviour (a shebang, magic and build-directive comments) and code commented
  out or back in are not trivial; any doubt (a truncated patch, a failed call, an unknown file type) means a
  re-review. A trivial delta moves `reviewed_sha` to the new head with the last verdict, queues nothing, keeps
  an App's approval (it runs before the approval check) and records `pr.trivial_delta`; during a review the
  appended note reads "_Reviewed a7b3f8c; 1 commit arrived during the review (comments only), no re-review
  needed._". `[daemon] skip_trivial_deltas` (default comments, whitespace, docs; `[]` turns it off) and its
  `[[watch]]` override choose the classes; a forced `magnum review` always runs. Rejected: asking the judge to
  decide (it costs the round the check saves) and docs that drive behaviour (prompts written as Markdown) as a
  built-in exception (drop "docs" for such a watch instead).
- **Rounds magnum cut short are refunded** (2026-10-04; one PR reached its daily cap of six with a round that
  failed to render a prompt and one stopped by a restart, then sat seven hours through six pushes). The cap
  still counts rounds at their start, but `finish` takes one back (rounds_today down, last_round_started_at back
  to the round before, `round.refunded` with the reason) when it was stopped (shutdown, restart, drain, abort),
  failed before any of its runs was prompted, failed on a prompt that did not render, or ended because the
  judge's model and every fallback model were limited; an infrastructure failure after the count is refunded
  too. Posted, needs-attention, blocked, timed-out and other failed rounds count. Rejected: counting rounds at
  their end (a crash would then never count, and the interval needs the start).
- **Every waiting PR says why and until when** (2026-10-04; the PR above waited seven hours with no word
  anywhere). After each dispatch the engine writes `pr.<id>.wait` for every queued or re-review-pending PR: the
  retry backoff, else the timing rule that clears last (quiet period, burst quiet period, re-review interval,
  draft interval, daily cap with its count), else a mute, quiet hours, what holds every PR (a pause, a drain, an
  infrastructure pause, herdr down), else the reason the dispatcher gave (a paused kind, the budget's soft cap,
  the identity, the slot, capacity), else "next dispatch". The dashboard's queue, the board's state cell and the
  card's "Next review" show the compact form (`re-review · cap 6/6 → 00:00`); the card and `magnum status <ref>`
  show the sentence with what lifts it (`magnum review <ref>` for what a forced review overrides, `magnum
  resume` for pauses). Rejected: computing it in each screen (the screens do not know the throttle's push
  history or the dispatcher's last reason).

- **magnum fetches over HTTPS through gh, whatever the clone's origin** (2026-10-04). A clone whose
  origin is a github.com SSH URL is fetched from the HTTPS URL with gh as the only credential helper;
