  says "magnum: talkable#11999 closed | its slot review16 stays pinned (magnum unpin)" (the key
  `closed-pinned:<pr id>` for 24 hours; the close is one compare-and-set transition, so it fires once, and
  the key keeps a restart from repeating it); a PR without a pin keeps the old wording and no toast.
  `magnum status` gets a `pinned:` line per pin ("review16 (talkable#11999, closed 5h ago, pinned 5d)"; the
  PR's state from the registry, the age from the newest `pr.opened`/`pr.pinned` or `slot.pinned` event
  that no unpin follows, `engine.PinnedSince`; none when the events were pruned; `pins` in the JSON), and
  the PR board's summary pill appends "· 2 on closed PRs" to "📌 4 pinned" when a pinned row's PR is merged or
  closed (words in the pill, no new line; it counts the rows the board lists, so a pin on a PR closed longer
  ago than `[board] recent_closed` is in `magnum status` only). The pin itself does not change: nothing
  releases it, and a closed PR's pinned slot is kept as before. Rejected: listing pinned closed PRs on the
  board past the recent window (a change of what the board shows, for a pill that already says the number),
  and a pin that lapses after a time (decided against on 10-07).
- **Thirteen review rules from the 2026-10-12 run** (2026-10-12, amends "A cleanup migration's finding shows
  its row count query", "Security findings are written in plain words" and "Two review rules borrowed from a
  public code-review skill"). The operator approved them on 2026-10-12, after the run's analysts read 109
  posted reviews, 283 answered threads and 15 real misses since 10-08. Each rule has a test of its own in
  `internal/agents/review_format_test.go`. Ten are in `skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md`. (a) Section 6: when
  fixes of two or more of the judge's findings patched one mechanism (a word list, a pattern set, a list of
  cases) and a new case still gets through, it posts one finding that the mechanism cannot be completed, with
  the structural fix and the rounds, even against a standing decision whose reason this answers; one PR got a
  new hole in the same word lists in three rounds (P1, P3, P1) until a person asked for the structural change.
  (b) Section 3: a merged finding's **Fix** names every other `path:line` of the same defect; a candidate named
  two sites, the posted P2 one, and the second came back "(missed earlier)" a round later. (c) Sections 2 and
  6 and `judge-own-pass.md`: a missing guard in a list, registry, validator or call-site set gets the set
  listed once, every gap proved with the same probe and posted, a Checks line `swept N <things>: M gaps` and
  `unproven: <what is missing>` for a member it cannot prove, and a re-review sweeps the set again before it
  calls such a finding fixed; 26 of 32 "(missed earlier)" findings since 10-01 sat in a directory an earlier
  finding of the same PR already hit. (d) Section 4: the trigger names its in-app producer (a route, a UI
  action, a job); one that needs an operator-typed setting, a non-default local environment, a console or
  stored rows no code path writes is P3 (P2 at most) with one command that checks it, and a P1 needs a trigger
  reached with the defaults ("non-default" keeps a change that breaks developers' normal local work P1); all 3
  P1 declines of the window were over-ranked, and 17 of 74 P3 threads were declined as console-, staging- or
  preview-only. (e) Section 2's structure sentence: a delete or reuse of records thought unsaved or free that
  another path creates in that state, and a remote change that cannot be undone (a rotated token, a charge)
  before a local save that validations can refuse; two P2 misses on one head. (f) Section 2's claims sentence
  and the three claude-review prompts: a documentation change's statements about data (who can read it, how
  long it is kept, when it is deleted) are claims checked against the code, the infrastructure files and the
  PR's other pages; a decision record said logs go after 30 days while another page of the PR said their copy
  in object storage never expires, a P2 miss (codex-review runs the stock `codex review` and takes no prompt).
  (g) Section 3: an example that passes only values no production caller sends pins nothing; specs passed
  Integer ids while requests send Strings, and the judge had rejected that gap as `style_only`. (h) Section 6:
  before the judge calls a finding fixed, it checks what the fix costs at real sizes; a fix to magnum's own P2
  paged through every code of every discount on every launch, and a throttled page refused the launch. (i)
  Section 4: any harm that needs stored rows of a shape (a stricter parser or validation on existing data)
  carries the query that counts them, as a cleanup migration's finding does (whose priority rule stays); a P2
  declined "after checking production" had no query to offer. (j) Section 7's machine paragraph: database
  specs on a merged tree whose base added migrations are a limit (the slot's schema is the head's), not run,
  and read `skipped (machine)`; one PR's merged-tree specs failed 12 times on a table the base had added. The
  same paragraph now names the network and Redis as codex-review's limits by design: from this run on its
  command runs under the checkout's `db_lock`, so its database runs take their turn. Two are reply wording in
  `judge-rereview.md` and `judge-recovery.md` (`judge-continue.md` resumes a turn and holds none). (k) A second
  rebuttal in a thread that holds one of the judge's names, in the same sentence, what both counterexamples
  share and the change that closes the class, never a third instance; 4 of 10 rebutted threads needed three
  fixes. (l) A new P3 whose consequence the reason of an answered thread already covers, with no larger harm,
  is not posted (`duplicate`), and that answer's body line says `(also covers <title>)`; 5 of 9 P3 declines
  under the current skill repeated an earlier answer on the same PR. One is in the claude-review prompts only.
  (m) When the PR closes an access hole, the report lists each request entry point that reached it with its
  access check, and a `Description: ✗` line when the description names fewer; a person found that a closed
  hole had reached more pages, exports and workers than the description said. A test keeps "entry point" out
  of the skill: the Codex judge reads it, and text that enumerates the reach of an injection fix drew Codex
  cybersecurity flags on judge turns. The skill grew by 2,211 bytes (the ten rules 2,158, codex-review's
  limits 53) and won 126 back (the readiness field's shell and Ruby notes, the local paths `post_review`
  refuses, `delta_check`'s "only when true"), so `skillMaxBytes` rose from 30,436 to 32,511; every earlier pin
  holds. Rejected: k and l in the skill (it was 10 bytes under its cap, and the rounds that post rebuttals
  carry their reply wording in those prompts), and rewording the migration sentence (its pin is the 2026-10-08
  rule, which keeps the priority).

- **The fixer signs its replies, and the retro learns only from people** (2026-10-12, amends "The retro
  classifies the replies to magnum's own findings" and "A missing-context decline is a repo miss for the
  notes"). The fixer posts as the PR's author. With a gh identity, the watch posts as the same login. Thus
  the replies of the fixer had no mark of their own, and `learn.OwnThreads` counted them as answers of the
  author. The fixer answered 85 of the 88 threads that got an answer under the current skill. The notes of
  one repository recorded ten choices of the fixer as what "the authors accept". After the merges, about 19
  of its declines were about to become learned "absent" cases. Now each reply of the fix skill ends with
  `<!-- magnum:fix -->` (`postreview.FixReplyMarker`, next to the reply marker of the judge, read by
  `IsFixReply`). A reply with this marker, by the PR's author or by one of magnum's logins, is the fixer's.
  `OwnThreads` shows its author as `(magnum fix)` (`learn.FixerAuthor`). The reply still answers the
  finding. When nobody else answered, the thread is `fixer` in `candidates.json`. The classifier gives such
  a thread its outcome, and a verdict for a declined or argued finding, but no lesson (`prompts/retro.md`).
  `checkThread` accepts the item without a lesson, and it removes any lesson, scope or patterns. Thus the
  `declines` row keeps the outcome and the verdict. It makes no learned eval case and no input for the
  skill editor, because both need scope general. A missing-context decline of the fixer is no repository
  miss, and it withdraws a miss that an earlier retro routed. A person's reply next to the fixer's makes
  the thread a person's. `routeDecline` then names that person as the reviewer of the miss, never magnum or
  its fixer (`learn.IsMagnum`). The marker in the reply of any other person makes no fixer of them. The
  replies table of `evidence.sh` in the improvement loop gets a `by` column: fixer, own, person, or
  `person?`. The last one is a reply that the threads file cut at 600 characters, before the marker. The
  table also counts the threads by who replied last. Limits: the threads file of the re-review and the
  judge still read the replies of the fixer as the author's (`ownThreads` in the pipeline). A reply from
  before this change has no marker. Rejected: a `declines` column for who answered. That needs a
  migration, and `scope` already keeps these rows out of each learner. Also rejected: removing the threads
  of the fixer from the retro. Their outcomes still show which findings got a fix.

- **A restart on a new build, config or prompts retries the PRs a failed round parked** (2026-10-12). A round
  that fails `maxAttempts` (3) times on one head parks its PR in needs_attention as `failed`, and nothing
  took it out but a push or the operator: of the operator's 24 forced reviews in four days, 7 took a PR out
  of needs_attention after a restart had fixed the failure's cause and two more belong to the same incidents
  (on 10-10 an unknown-role bug parked PRs at 13:27:02, the daemon restarted on the fix at 13:27:39 and the
  forces came at 13:32; on 10-12 a launch-line bug parked 6 PRs over 19 failed rounds, the restart on the fix
  came at 13:39:33 and five forces at 13:42:40-49), and meanwhile two PRs merged unreviewed. Now
  `needsAttentionKeyed` records with the attention's kind what the daemon runs (`pr.<id>.attention_run`, a
  `runFingerprint`: the build as its revision, or its version without one, and the binary's mtime, so a
  rebuild of one commit from a changed tree is another build; the SHA-256 of the loaded config as JSON,
  defaults included; and `config.PromptSnapshot.Sum`, over every prompt's text and every skill's content the
  start loaded), taken once per daemon. `retryParked` runs at the start after `recoverRows` and
  `recoverFixes` and before the first tick: an open PR in needs_attention whose kind is `failed` and whose
  record differs (or is missing: a build before the record parked it) moves back to its claimable state
  (queued, or rereview_pending with a reviewed SHA) with attempts 0, no next attempt, the throttle's
  next_eligible_at and no last error, not forced, so it waits its quiet period, interval and cap like any
  PR; one `pr.retried_after_restart` event per PR names the part that differs ("retried after the restart
  on e7ad419: the failure's build differs", or config, or prompts), and one batched toast lists them
  ("magnum: retrying 2 PRs parked by failed rounds before this build"). A PR that fails again under the same
  run is parked with that run and stays, as the operator approved; the other kinds stay too (a fix loop's
  cap or call, a blocked judge, a judge that posted nothing, an identity check or leak, an API that stayed
  overloaded), and so do a PR with a Codex flag (with or without a fallback judge) and one its watch no
  longer accepts. A dry run retries nothing, as it recovers nothing. The attention toast's and reveal's
  dedupe key (`attentionKey`) now names the run as well, so a retried PR that fails again within the
  30-minute window of its first toast is toasted again instead of going quiet after the retry toast said it
  was being retried. Rejected: retrying on every restart (a restart on the same build only fails again),
  and forcing the retried PRs (a forced round skips the timing rules and goes first, while the cause may be
  the PR's own).
- **A confirmed close stops a round nobody asked for** (2026-10-12, amends "`magnum abort` takes back a
  review that waits in line", whose stop machinery this uses). Before, the poll confirmed a close (`pr.closed`
  after two CLOSED/MERGED answers a minute apart) but left the PR's round running. The round ran until the
  judge found the PR closed and posted nothing. In the window three rounds ran on PRs already merged. One
  started 71 s after the merge and ran 16.7 minutes. One ran 9 minutes after `pr.closed`. One posted a review
  11 minutes after the merge. That is 34 role-minutes of three or four roles each, and a review nobody reads.
  Such a round also held the close grace of every closed PR, because `closeGrace` waits while a round of a
  closed PR runs. Now `confirmMissing` calls `stopClosedRound` after it moves a PR with a round in flight to
  closed. That call gives the round a close stop (`roundStop.closed`: GitHub's state and the count of
  confirmations). After it records `pr.closed`, it cancels the round. The `pr.closed` event of a PR with a
  pool slot says `merged on GitHub (confirmed 3×); stopping its round; slot handed back when it stops`. Then
  `afterRound` serves the stop as an abort without a request, through `stopPR`. It interrupts the working
  agents and parks the sessions. It abandons the active runs with `stopped: the PR merged on GitHub`, not
  `aborted by user`. It ends a fix loop "by the PR's merge on GitHub". It hands the slot back. A pool slot is
  released as `merged` or `closed` (the reasons cleanup gives). A per-PR worktree and a pinned slot stay for
  cleanup, as before. The PR stays closed and is released after the close grace. One `round.stopped` event
  says `round 1 stopped: the PR merged on GitHub (confirmed 3×)`, then what the stop did (`1 agent
  interrupted, 1 run abandoned, sessions parked, slot review1 released`). Its data holds `outcome: closed`, the
  round, `gh_state` and `confirmed`. A round that did not reach the pipeline yet has no active run, so its
  event gives no number. The event is not `pr.aborted`, so `magnum fix --wait` does not read it as an abort.
  Three kinds of round run on as before. The first is a forced round (`magnum review`, the board's `r`, the
  fix loop's re-review). The second is a round that a review request started (`roundJob.requested`). The
  third is a post-merge review (the poll never confirms its merged PR again). The dispatcher records this on
  the reservation (`roundHandle.asked`). An open's restore, a fix job and an abort that already stops the PR
  are not rounds to stop. If an abort also comes, it is served as an abort. The refund rule does not change.
  The round's result is the pipeline's `stopped`. If its judge was not prompted yet, the round is refunded, as
  for a round that a shutdown stopped. Otherwise it counts. Recovery needs nothing new. The stop runs in the
  daemon on a context of its own, as an abort's does. If the daemon dies during the stop, a closed PR stays,
  and cleanup owns it, as after a shutdown during such a round before. A forced round keeps its slot until it
  ends, as before (`TestCloseGraceWaitsForARoundInItsCheckout` now forces its round). Rejected: stopping a
  round someone asked for (the operator asked for a review of this PR, merged or not). Also rejected: leaving
  the slot to the close grace (an abort hands it back at once, also for an aborted post-merge round on a
  merged PR).

- **Every re-review's start event records the size of its delta, and the loop's evidence counts a reviewer's own rejections apart** (2026-10-12).
  `engine.round_start` recorded `delta_lines` and `delta_files` for delta checks only, so nothing in the
  registry told a full re-review of a 17-line fixer push from one of a 2,000-line rewrite, and the cost
  lens could not set a round's minutes against the change it reviewed. Now every re-review and recovery
  round that has a reviewed commit to measure from (not a first review, an eval's replay, a continue or a
  round on the reviewed commit itself) records the size of the commits since it: `delta_lines` and
  `delta_files`, measured as a delta check measures them (`roundDelta` asks `measureRange` as the watch's
  poll identity, so a push that merged the base branch counts the PR's own change, not the base branch's
  lines), and `delta_partial: true` when a file had no patch GitHub sends in full, which makes the lines a
  lower bound. `delta_check` stays true for checks only, so the screens that read it
  (`magnum prs --json`, the PR board) show what they showed. The comparison is the one `baseMerged` made a
  moment earlier in `roundInput`, so it costs a GitHub call only for a range that merged or diverged (the
  PR's own diff before and after it); a failed comparison or a watch without a client records no size
  and the round starts as before. Rejected: `git diff --numstat` in the slot (gitx has no diff stat, and
  after a merge of the base branch it counts the base branch's lines). The improvement loop's `evidence.sh`
  changed with it. A `claude-review.md` report ends with a "Rejected" list of candidates the reviewer
  dropped itself, and the judge ledgers each as a rejected finding with the reviewer as the only source
  (46e6383): of the 1,079 rejected rows of claude-review alone since 10-08 15:13, 843 match a bullet of
  that list, so the findings tables read as 119 P1 rejected against 6 posted for claude-review alone, when
  the judge rejected 4 of the P1 findings it reported. Neither the ledger nor the registry marks them, so the script matches each
  row's title against the report (the cosine of word stems, a bullet's claim before its first colon or a
  finding's heading; 0.2 for a bullet that no finding beats, 0.3 for a finding), writes every row with its
  class (self, reported, unmatched or no report) and the text it matched to `claude-review-origin.txt`,
  gives the findings table a `self` column and adds a table of the claude-review-alone findings by
  priority, with the reviewer's precision between posted / (posted + reported + unmatched) and posted /
  (posted + reported). A posted finding is not classified (its title matches a bullet about the same code as
  often as not). The posted-reviews table drops a nudge run whose review id another listed run carries
  (3 nudges, 112 rows for 109 reviews). `selftest.sh` covers the matching and the nudge on a small registry.
  Rejected: counting the Rejected list's bullets from the reports alone (the judge splits and merges them,
  so the count is not the ledger's) and a mark in the ledger (the judge's output format is pinned).
- **The judge and the claude reviewers check a changed flow against the platform's published rules**
  (2026-10-13). On talkable#11932 a colleague's review found that the new signup page asks the merchant
  for a myshopify.com domain and starts the Platform app's install outside Shopify, which App Store rule
  2.3.1 forbids ("Apps must be installed and initiated only on Shopify services. Your app must not request
  the manual entry of a myshopify.com URL or a shop's domain during the installation or configuration
  flow"); four days earlier the same review had found the form shown before OAuth (rule 2.3.2). Magnum
  reviewed the page in 28 rounds; one judge (round 15) opened the requirements page, applied the OAuth
  clause alone, and rejected claude-review's candidate about the retry form as speculative ("The
  still-supported Talkable-origin signup form is intentional"). The 2026-10-12 improve run's lens 0 called
  the first miss out of reach (a platform policy) and proposed only a repository note, which never landed.
  Now the review skill's section 2 says: a flow the PR adds or changes that a third party governs with
  published requirements (an app store listing, a platform app's install, OAuth, billing or webhook flow,
  an API's terms) is checked against the whole section of those requirements that covers it, read on that
  party's own site by web search, sentence by sentence, not only the one a report quotes; a flow they
  forbid is a finding that cites the rule's number and quotes its sentence, P1 when the default path
  reaches it, and a reason that calls it deliberate covers only the rule it names. The three claude-review
  prompts say the same with WebFetch; `codex review` takes no prompt. The skill was at its cap, so
  fourteen parenthetical examples went (the readiness and machine-failure examples, the related-PR kinds,
  the second P1, P2 and P3 examples, "idioms, pleasantries", two quoted asides, "Node or Python"); no
  pinned sentence changed. The improve skill's lens 0 no longer counts a published rule as out of reach,
  and the local eval corpus gets `install-outside-shopify` (talkable#11932 at 0950625) to measure the
  change. Rejected: a notes line alone (it reaches one repository, and the judge had the page open and
  still missed the sentence), and a generic web fetch for the judge (section 1 keeps `gh` for GitHub
  data; Codex's `--search` is the parity for a documentation lookup, as the plugin entry of 2026-10-12
  says).
- **A head whose CI turns red after the review gets a judge check** (2026-10-13, extends "The judge sees
  the head's failing checks"). On talkable#11483 the head e2777d0 was pushed at 07:41:54Z; magnum's round
  38 (a recovery round) prompted its judge at about 07:44Z and posted at 08:11:53Z "No new problems since
  9e80a11; CI is red: Dependency Audit failed, unrelated". The head's RSpec run started at 08:12:39Z and
  finished red at 08:26-08:31Z with two failing examples the PR causes (the eval lock spec, `Expected 216000
  to be > 222315`, the PR's six new eval cases pushing a full run past the 60-hour lock, and a controller
  spec that expects one `mark_pending` call where the PR now makes two). Round 39 at 08:15Z only answered
  threads, and nothing looked at the reviewed head's CI again: the poll stored the checks and compared
  nothing. A colleague's review at 09:47Z reported both failures as blocking, an hour after CI finished,
  while magnum's last word on the head called it unrelated. The skill already knows what a failed check
  means (`failing_checks`, section 7: a P1 broken build the PR causes, a red head never reads LGTM); the
  judge is only told when its prompt goes out. Now a check of the head magnum reviewed (no push since, the
  stored checks that head's, the PR open, not merged, not muted) that failed, with a known time, after the
  judge prompt behind the latest review posted on that head queues a judge check of the same head: the
  prompt time is `runs.submitted_at` of that round's first posted run (`store.PostedPromptAt`; in a
  two-prompt round the candidates prompt, the one `failing-checks.json` was written for), not
  `reviewed_at`, since a check that completed between the prompt and the post was not seen either, and a
  check that failed before the prompt was in the file and is answered. The PR goes to `rereview_pending`
  as for replies (`pr.ci_red`: "CI finished red on <sha> after the review (1 failed check, at 08:31); a
  judge check follows"), and `pr.<id>.ci_followup` records the head and each failed check it covers by
  workflow, name and failure time. `eligibility.PRFacts.CIRedAt` makes the throttle hold it only for a
  snooze (no quiet period, interval, cap or reply debounce; a request still wins), quiet hours let it run
  as the judge alone, it counts against no cap, and dispatch starts it as a same-head round of the judge
  alone (`ci_red: true` and "(CI red after the review)" in `engine.round_start`), which is no reply round
  (its judge reads the replies all the same). Its prompt (`judge-rereview.md`, `judge-recovery.md`, only
  under `.CIRed`) says CI finished red after the review: decide each failed check from its log, a P1
  with the failing example quoted when the PR causes it, else an unrelated Checks line, and post exactly
  one review with the section 7 verdict. The board and `magnum prs --json` show the wait as a CI check
  (`CI check · CI red`, "CI turned red after the review; judge check pending"). One judge check per
  failing check and head: a rerun of the same workflow and check that fails again after the check posted
  is covered by the review that stands, while another check failing later gets its own. While it waits, CI
  that no longer shows its checks failed (a rerun runs, or passed) takes the PR back to `reviewed` and
  the checks out of the record (`pr.ci_red_dropped`), so a rerun that fails again queues it again; a push
  supersedes it (the record goes, `pr.ci_red_dropped`, and the push's round reads the new head's CI). A
  round in flight, a fix loop, a forced or requested round take precedence (their judge reads the
  failing checks too). The event names no check: the PR's workflows name them, so they stay in the
  registry. GitHub's rollup stays FAILURE while a check that failed before is still red (talkable#11483's
  case: Dependency Audit had failed already), so the poll's cheap rollup read also takes the rollup's
  counts by state (`checkRunCountsByState`, `statusContextCountsByState` through `contexts(first: 0)`, the
  same request with more fields and no node listed), and Details stores the same counts with the checks
  (`ci_json`'s `rollup`): a failed or pending count that differs reads the checks again, a superseded run
  counting in both (the stored checks' own tally drops superseded runs, so comparing with it would read
  the checks of every head with a passed re-run on every poll); when either side has no counts, the
  rollup state's comparison is all, as before.
  Rejected: a notification instead of a round (the author gets no finding, and the
  LGTM or "unrelated" stands), a new run kind (`runs.kind` has a SQL CHECK, `0025_fix_runs.sql`, so a
  flag on rereview and recovery rounds is the cheap path), and a skill change (the skill is at its byte
  cap and already says what a failed check means; no new `<magnum>` field either).
- **A check that fails on the base too does not hold an auto-approval** (2026-10-13, amends "Auto-approval
  waits for the head's checks"). On talkable#11483 the Dependency Audit check had been red for days on the
  PR's heads and on master alike (the same package versions: `ruby_llm` 1.16.0 and `source-map-js` 1.2.1).
  Magnum's reviews said so in prose ("CI is red: Dependency Audit failed, unrelated (same package versions
  on master)"), and the gate still refused every approval of the PR with "its head's checks fail (magnum
  approves it once they pass)". The operator's rule: a red check does not block the approval when it fails
  the same way on master. "The same way" is the same check (the same workflow and name, as
  `store.CheckResult` identifies one) failed on the base branch's tip too; conclusions are not compared.
  On a rollup `FAILURE` or `ERROR` the gate reads the head's stored checks (`ci_json`, only when they are
  the head's and list every one) and the checks of the tip the last Details fetch read (`prs.base_sha`:
  magnum's posted review, a CI change of the head and any activity on the PR read it again, so it is the
  tip at or after the head's checks finished) through the new `github.Client.CommitChecks`
  (`repository.object(oid:)` as a Commit, with the contexts and the normalization Details reads of a head:
  the latest run of each workflow and name). When every failed check of the head failed there, the head
  goes through once its other checks finished: a check that still runs answers "its head's checks have not
  finished", which a standing approval waits out, since GitHub's rollup fails as soon as one check fails.
  The base comparison comes first, so a head with a failure of its own and a check still running is
  refused, and a standing approval withdrawn, as before. A head that goes through records
  `review.auto_approve_ci_base` ("its head's 1 failing check fails on master's tip <sha7> too; the
  approval goes ahead") once per head and round (kv `pr.<id>.auto_approve_ci_base`, `<head>|<run id>`: the
  gates run on every tick until the approval posts); like `pr.ci_red` it names no check, since the
  repository's workflows name them. Anything else refuses as before: a failed check the tip passes, lacks
  or fails under another workflow only, a failing rollup with no failed check stored, a head of more
  checks than GitHub lists (100: "have not finished" would never end there), no known tip, a read that
  fails (logged at info; the reason never carries an error's text). A tip's checks are kept in memory for
  10 minutes per repository and commit, a failed read too (one point per tip, not per PR or tick; a
  restart reads them again), so a tip whose checks still ran is read again after that. A standing approval
  held to the gates after a later round follows the same rule; the approval's body, the card's refusal
  text and `auto_approve_refused` do not change. Rejected: parsing the review's Checks lines (prose, not a
  contract); comparing conclusions (a check cancelled on the tip and failed on the head is red on both); a
  per-repository allowlist of check names (the operator would have to maintain it, and it would pass a
  check the PR itself breaks); reading the base ref's tip by name (`base_sha` is the tip of the head's
  last read, the one its checks ran against).
- **The judge is told the notes' line limit** (2026-10-14, amends "The notes limits are curation triggers,
  measured in code"). Five of the eleven notes proposals of the improvement window (30, 31, 33, 35 and 37)
  had `max_line` as their only trigger: notes of 2 to 7 KB with one to four lines past 300 characters, which
  a judge had written because nothing told it the limit (neither the judge prompts nor the skill named
  `max_line`). Each curation only reflowed those lines, and every result was larger than the notes it
  started from (4786 to 4970, 3230 to 3827, 5494 to 5703, 2243 to 3019 and 6964 to 7216 bytes), at a Claude
  session of about three minutes and an operator review each. Now `agents.JudgeData.NotesMaxLine` carries
  `[notes] max_line`, set by the pipeline from the runner's config (`Runner.Config.Notes.MaxLine`) when the
  round has notes, and the judge-initial, judge-rereview, judge-recovery and judge-continue prompts render
  it as `notes_max_line: 300` in the `<magnum>` block with one sentence before it: "Keep each line of the
  `notes` file at most `notes_max_line` characters long: a longer line triggers a curation." Both are left
  out without notes and without a known limit (0), and the own-pass prompt, which writes no notes, does not
  carry them. The sentence says "at most" because the measure is `n > max_line` in characters
  (`notes.MeasureText`). The skill stands unchanged (it is at its byte cap, and the limit is a fact of the
  configuration, which the prompt already carries for every other notes field). Rejected: magnum reflowing
  or truncating the judge's lines after the round (the notes are the judge's text, and a cut line loses its
  meaning); blocking a rewrite that holds a long line (the limits are triggers, not caps, and a curated
  proposal may keep a line a reader needs whole); the value in the skill's text (it would drift from the
  config).
- **An own PR merged by hand raises no merged-unreviewed toast** (2026-10-14, amends "merged before
  magnum reviewed its last push is flagged"). Two of the seven `pr.merged_unreviewed` events of a week
  were the operator's own PRs, merged seconds after they went ready (3 and 30 seconds); each raised an
  urgent toast and a red attention row for 24 hours, for a merge the operator did on purpose. The four
  colleague cases were right to flag. Now `mergedUnreviewed` skips the toast for a PR whose author is one
  of the operator's logins (`ownPR`, the board's "mine"); the `pr.merged_unreviewed` warning and the flag
  (the red pill, the card's sentence, `M` to dismiss it) stay as they are, so a merge that was an accident
  still shows on the board. A PR whose author is not known yet keeps its toast. Rejected: no flag at all
  for an own PR (an own PR merged while a round was due is still unreviewed; the board should say so);
  skipping the toast by how soon after ready it merged (a threshold to tune, and a person's own PR is
  theirs whatever the delay).
- **`magnum retro` queues behind a running learn job** (2026-10-14, amends "Learn jobs run one at a time").
  A curation asked for while another learn job ran was queued, and a retro was refused ("no retro now: the
  notes curation of talkable/talkable runs (started 17:17), and learn jobs run one at a time"). On
  2026-10-14 the operator met that twice, once right after their own curations and once when the improve
  loop's step 2 began with the retro while a curation a proposal review had started ran, and polled by hand.
  Now a retro asked for while another learn job runs is queued (kv `learn.retro_queued`: the PRs it named,
  `again`, the lookback it resolved and when it was asked; the settle delay is `[learn] settle`'s when it
  starts) with a `retro.queued` event, and answered as a queued curation is ("queued: starts when <job>
  (started HH:MM) ends; `magnum logs` follows it"). The request completes with that answer at once, as a
  queued curation's does (a request held in flight until the retro ends would outlast the CLI's 30 s wait);
  the queue is the registry's, so a restart keeps it, as it keeps the curations' queue. The tick tries the
  queued retro first in `maybeRetro`, which runs before `maybeCurate`, so once the job ended it starts
  before any curation queued meanwhile: the retro feeds the curations with misses. A curation asked for
  while the queued retro waits for its turn (the job ended, the next tick has not come) is queued behind
  it too, unless the retro's CLI is paused. A drain, a stop or an infrastructure pause (`holdReason`) and a
  pause of the retro's CLI (`retroToolPause`) still refuse a request, since a queue cannot wait them out;
  when they come after the retro was queued it stays queued, and every tick tries it again. One retro
  waits at a time: a second request answers "a retro is queued already (asked HH:MM) and starts when ...
  ends" and changes nothing; a retro running answers "already running" as before, and a queued retro holds
  the day's, which follows it. A queued value that does not read is dropped with `retro.queue_dropped`.
  Rejected: a queue of retros (two retros of the same lookback find the same PRs; the second has nothing to
  do), merging a second request into the first (its lookback and PRs would change what the first answer
  promised), and keeping the request pending until the retro ends.
- **The claude reviewers take the database lock per command, and the platform-rules paragraph is pinned**
  (2026-10-14, amends "The roles of a round take turns on the slot's databases"). Four checks of one
  improvement window ended in exit 75, the lock's 20-minute timeout (talkable#11483 once, #11932 three times),
  and one codex-review report was lost: #11932 round 44 waited 20 minutes and the judge had no codex-review
  candidates. The reports name claude-review as the holder, running a multi-file spec batch or a whole mutation
  loop (`REVIEW_MUTATIONS=...`) under one lock call, while codex-review holds the lock for its whole `codex
  review` by design, so it is the role that starves. The sentence of the four claude prompts (claude-review,
  claude-rereview, claude-restart, claude-simplify) said to run every database command as `<db_lock> <command>`
  and nothing about the size of a command. It now says the lock covers one command: one spec command per call,
  never a batch or a loop of them, and each mutant or overlay run takes the lock on its own, so the other roles
  get their turn between commands (`TestClaudePromptsTakeTheLockPerCommand`). SKILL.md is unchanged (it is at
  its byte cap, and its line about `db_lock` stays); `fix.md` and the judge prompts are not part of this. The
  "Platform rules:" paragraph of the skill (de84b79, 551 bytes) was in none of the 205 pins of
  `skill_pins.txt`, so the landing's "no pinned sentence changed" said nothing about it and the skill editor's
  only proposal collided with it. Its first clause and the words "cites the rule's number and quotes its
  sentence" are pinned now (`TestSkillPinsThePlatformRulesParagraph`), so an edit of them fails the pin test
  and the editor sees them. Rejected: a shorter `--timeout` for the claude roles (it only turns the starved
  role's wait into the holder's failure), splitting the lock by role (the roles share one database, which is
  why the lock exists), and making codex-review lock per command (it runs one `codex review` whose spec runs
  it cannot split).
- **A comment the judge read and rejected as a duplicate is caught, not a miss** (2026-10-14, amends "Learning loop:
  daily retro" and "The retro's classifier names the rejected finding a miss matches"). On a PR of the 2026-10-14
  window a colleague posted two inline comments about a minute before round 1 started. The round's judge read
  both, confirmed them, and rejected its own candidates F1 (P1) and F2 (P3) as `duplicate`, citing those very
  threads (the review skill's rule: an existing thread already covers it). The retro still made the two comments
  misses with `raised: rejected`, because `learn.Build` linked every comment near a rejected finding to it,
  whatever the reason and whenever the comment was posted; both rows went to the skill editor and into the
  learned eval corpus, where the gate replays them. Now the nearest rejected finding of a comment (the one
  Build already linked) whose reason is `duplicate` makes the comment caught (`Result.Caught`, no candidate, as
  for a posted finding) when the comment was created strictly before the review that rejected the finding;
  the same second keeps today's reading. **A `duplicate` of another thread is the only reason treated so**: for
  `not_reproducible`, `speculative` and the rest the judge read the problem and disagreed or dismissed it, which
  is exactly what the retro measures, so the comment stays a candidate, `raised: rejected` with the reason
  (`pre_existing` and `outside_diff` as well: the judge said the problem is not this PR's, where a duplicate
  says someone already reported it). A comment made after the review was never read by that judge and stays
  raised whatever the reason. The skill's `duplicate` also covers an earlier review of magnum's own; the comment
  is near that review's posted finding then, and was caught already. **The review's time** is the `SubmittedAt` of the GitHub review
  that `Input.ReviewRuns` binds (runs.review_id) to the finding's run, looked up in `Input.Reviews`; the engine
  needed no change. `Input.Reviewed` is not used: it is keyed by commit, not by run, and in the engine its time
  is the run's last stamp (verified or ended), later than the posting, and a head reviewed twice
  (`--again`) has one row for two reviews. When the link is missing (no review bound to the run, the review not
  listed, a pending one without a time) nothing proves the judge read the comment, and the comment stays a
  candidate as before. Rejected: comparing with the finding's `CreatedAt` (when the round's result was
  recorded, after the posting and the verification) or with the round's start (not in `Input`), which would
  need an engine change for a window of minutes; and counting any near duplicate rejection, not only the
  nearest, which would catch a comment whose own nearest finding the judge disagreed with. The cost: a comment
  made after the judge read the threads and before it posted counts as caught, a lost candidate rather than
  noise. The two rows already in the registry stay as they are (`magnum retro --again` rebuilds them); no
  migration. Tests: `TestACommentTheJudgeReadAndRejectedAsADuplicateIsCaught`,
  `TestACommentAfterTheReviewNearADuplicateRejectionStaysRaised`,
  `TestADuplicateIsTheOnlyRejectionReasonThatCountsAsCaught`,
  `TestADuplicateRejectionCountsOnlyWhenTheReviewIsKnown` and
  `TestTheNearestRejectedFindingDecidesWhetherADuplicateCatchesTheComment`. No new dependencies.
- **A judge that never comes up is started once more, and no start adopts the agent of a session magnum
  ended** (2026-10-14, amends "A cold judge is not lost to the agent it quit"). Three rounds ended in error
  from 2026-10-12 to 10-14 because a fresh Codex judge never came up. In talkable#11359 round 2 herdr's
  agent.start answered ok in 11 ms, but herdr never registered the agent (its log has no "agent changed"
  line for the pane until the next round's start, which registered in 0.4 s); the own pass's prompt failed
  with `agent_not_ready` after Submit's 60 s wait for the agent, which `judgeGone` did not count (only no
  session, `agent_not_found` and `pane_not_found`), and the candidates prompt 13 minutes later failed with
  `agent_not_found` and had no restart of its own, so 20 minutes of reviewer work were lost and the head got
  no review. In another PR's round 6 the start adopted round 5's judge, which had never come up (status
  unknown, no conversation) and whose session magnum had closed 90 s before: the prompt found it gone 13 s
  later. Now `judgeGone` also counts `agent_not_ready` (`herdr.CodeAgentNotReady`, which Submit returns only
  after that wait), and the candidates prompt gets the own pass's single restart (`judgeAgain`): the judge
  run that never reached the judge is abandoned unsent, as a push's restart replaces it, so the engine's
  crash recovery and the unverified-review search both take the new run for the review's marker; the judge
  starts again through `RoundInput.RestartJudge` (`round.judge_restarted`); and the prompt is rendered
  again for the new run with the reports and files as they were. A second refusal, or a start that fails,
  ends the round as before. `adoptable` refuses an agent herdr lists under the role's name when a session of
  that name was closed by magnum within the last 10 minutes (`endedAgentMemory`: how long magnum remembers
  a closed session), and, when the agent never came up (status unknown) and carries no conversation id,
  while any session of that name exists that magnum closed or marked lost (the engine's restart marks the
  gone judge lost). Such an agent in the start's own pane is launched anew there (the idle-shell wait and
  agent.start, as in a fresh pane); one in another pane makes the start busy (`ErrBusy`: the setup is
  retried in a minute, uncharged); the sessions not read make it busy too. Beyond the spec: the second rule
  needs the agent not up, and counts lost sessions with closed ones. An agent the daemon launched but never
  recorded (a crash between agent.start and markStarted) is up, and refusing it would make every later
  start wait for an idle shell that agent occupies; without lost sessions the round's own restart would
  adopt the agent it restarts for. Not known: whether herdr's agent.start takes the name while it still
  lists the never-registered agent in that pane; if it refuses, the start fails as the adopted agent's
  prompt did.
- **A round never takes another run's review for its own** (2026-10-14). talkable#12009's round 10 was
  prompted 33 s after round 9 posted its review, and its judge's result file named that review. The REST
  fallback of verification (the review the result names, by the reviewer, on the target, submitted after
  the prompt less `clockSkew`'s 2 minutes) accepted it, reading its marker, round 9's run's, as no marker,
  and the round counted as posted with a review it did not write. Now the fallback refuses a review whose
  body carries a `magnum:run` marker of none of the round's markers (`otherRunMarker`), with a warning that
  names the run, and so does verification's marker-less last resort; a review with no marker at all is
  accepted as before. Such a round then ends as one whose result names a review GitHub does not show for
  its marker (needs attention), or is nudged when the result names none.
- **An empty GraphQL answer is asked again at half the page** (2026-10-14, amends "The radar reads no CI; a
  read by node id does, and a page GitHub cannot answer in time is asked again smaller"). 75 of the 89
  failed `gh api graphql` calls from 2026-10-12 to 10-14 took 11 to 13 s, past GitHub's 10 s limit, and
  answered "unexpected end of JSON input" (an empty body) or REFUSED_STREAM; `overloaded` counted a 5xx, a
  GraphQL error naming a timeout and the stream the peer cancelled, so talkable's radar failed 5 polls
  without the half-size retry a 502 gets. Now `overloaded` also counts an error whose text, or the gh
  exit's whole stderr, holds "unexpected end of JSON input" or "REFUSED_STREAM".
- **The docs say what the code does: the fix role's identity, seven built-in roles, the help texts**
  (2026-10-14, after the docs-accuracy read of 3e09420). The read compared README.md, prompts/README.md, the
  three config files and the cobra help texts with the code and found these statements false. The README gave
  the built-in claude-fix the identity `me` and said the loader refuses a fix role without an identity, where
  the role names none, acts as the watch's poll identity and the loader refuses only a declared identity that
  is not a gh one. "Four built-in roles" stood in seven places where the code has seven (the round's four, the
  reserve judge, the fix role and the whiteboard role), and "omitted `roles` = every role" was loose, since a
  watch without `roles` runs the roles of a round and its first judge only. prompts/README.md lacked the
  roles' `fix`, `whiteboard` and `rerun_min_lines` and the kinds' `login_file`, `plugin_allow` and
  `plugin_disable`, and its `wrapper` row the value `bypass`. The help texts of `magnum fix` (a review that
  found nothing and left nothing open, a snooze), `prs` and `status` (the keys f, F and w), daemon-restart,
  daemon-stop, install and uninstall (a skill edit or gate, a fix job and a whiteboard job also hold a stop),
  `abort` and `ignore` (a whiteboard job is stopped too) and `whiteboard` (a slot not at the head, a pinned PR)
  lagged the code, and so did the README on the board's `f` (a head that kept its verdict and a review that
  keeps an earlier finding open are let through), the Claude sessions' MCP flags (the whiteboard writer's
  `args` add an `--mcp-config`), Whiteboard's prerequisites (`magnum whiteboard` by hand needs it too) and
  `cleanup` (a review screen on a terminal). "See Re-reviews" pointed at no heading: the re-review prose is
  under `### Re-reviews` now, and the paragraphs after it under `### Review requests, caps and pauses`, with
  no text moved. The footer fields `.QuietHours`, `.DraftsSkipped` and `.RequestLogin` are in
  config.full.example.toml, and the behaviour only the cobra help or a config comment named (`[terminal] app`
  for any app name, `resume --tool` and `--watch`, the flags of review, open, attention, logs, watch, pick,
  daemon and cleanup, the daemon's `agent_start_stagger`, `max_total_working_codex` and `min_warm`,
  `[github] transport`, a repository's `wt_hooks`, a watch's `clone_root` and `skip_cross_repository`, the
  learn editor's `editor_effort`, `editor_args` and `editor_prompt`) has a line in the README. Two tests keep
  the count and the keys: `TestEveryTomlBlockInTheDocsDecodesWithoutUnknownKeys` decodes every toml block of
  both READMEs through the loader's decoder, and `TestTheDocsCountTheBuiltInRoles` fails when a doc writes
  another number of built-in roles than `len(DefaultRoles())`. Left as written: the Go comment of
  `Role.Timeout` (config/roles.go) that still says "the four roles config.defaults.toml writes out", since
  a comment of an exported field is in docs/API.md and the change belongs with a code change, and the value
  `generic` of `[terminal] app`, which names no application to bring to the front (any other name is
  brought to it with `open -a`).
- **The atomic file write skips its disk syncs in a test binary** (2026-10-14, amends "One atomic file
  write"). The gate was slow because it waited on the disk, not because it computed. At 3e09420 `go test
  ./...` took 106 to 112 s (217 s with `-race`), and the engine package, the critical path at 105 s, used
  1.1 cores on average for 16 parallel tests. `fsx.WriteFileAtomic` syncs the file and then the directory,
  and Go's `File.Sync` is F_FULLFSYNC on macOS: about 9 ms a call against 0.05 to 0.2 ms for a plain write,
  and a flush queues on the whole device, so the tests of one package slowed the others. The tab-bar
  heartbeat alone made 8,537 atomic writes in six packages' tests. Now `WriteFileAtomic` and
  `WriteFileAtomicIn` skip both syncs when `testing.Testing()` is true (the style of the five sites in
  `internal/agents`); production is unchanged, and no test can observe a sync, so none pins one. Measured on
  this machine with `go test -count=1 ./...` back to back, master against the change: 118 s and 115 s
  against 44 s and 39 s (load 15 to 32), and 254 s and 281 s against 82 s and 42 s earlier in the day at
  load 22 to 57. Under `-race` the suite takes about 190 s now and the engine package about 180 s of it,
  which is the race detector's cost, not the disk's. `TestFromAppDryRunOnce` left `Usage.CodexHome` empty,
  so its tick read `$CODEX_HOME` or `~/.codex/sessions` of the machine it ran on: it points the Codex home
  at a temporary directory with one rollout (37% used) and asserts that the budget the tick read is that
  rollout's, so the budget gate it exercises is the same everywhere. Tried and left out: a scratch registry
  for `storetest.Open` (`store.Options.Scratch`: `journal_mode=MEMORY`, `synchronous=OFF`,
  `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE`). 22 tests of the cli and evalrun packages open the file a second time (the
  command under test opens the registry of the fixture that `storetest.Open` holds), which the exclusive
  lock locks out; and with the syncs gone the four settings (as it is, all three pragmas, without the
  exclusive lock, WAL with `synchronous=OFF`) ran the engine package in 25.1 to 25.9 s and the slots package
  in 11.6 to 12.4 s, back to back twice, so no setting had anything left to save. Rejected: skipping the
  syncs through an environment variable or a package variable a test sets (a test that forgets it syncs
  again, and the binary keeps a switch that production could flip), and a file system the writers take as
  a parameter (about 40 call sites for one decision `testing.Testing()` already makes).
- **The tab-bar heartbeat is written without disk syncs** (2026-10-14, amends "One atomic file write").
  `WriteTabBarFile` writes the file at the start and the end of every tick. It went through
  `WriteFileAtomic`, so each of the two writes paid two full disk flushes (about 9 ms each, queued behind
  every other write to the device) for a file that is worth nothing after a crash: the tab-bar command
  prints "magnum down" for a file that is missing, empty or has no fresh timestamp, which is what a lost
  heartbeat is. Now `fsx.ReplaceFile(path, data, perm)` writes a temporary file with a unique name in the
  directory and renames it over the target, with no file sync and no directory sync: a reader still sees the
  old content or the new, never part of a file, the mode is exact whatever the umask, a symlink at the path
  is replaced and a failed write leaves no temporary file (`TestReplaceFileWritesReplacesAndLeavesNoTempFiles`,
  `TestReplaceFileReplacesASymlinkInsteadOfFollowingIt`, `TestReplaceFileFailureLeavesNoTempFile`). Only
  `WriteTabBarFile` uses it, and its doc comment says why a caller picks it. Rejected: keeping
  `WriteFileAtomic` for the heartbeat in production (the flush buys nothing there and holds up the daemon's
  other writes), and skipping the syncs for every caller (the state files, notes, skill copies and reports
  must survive a crash).
- **A status comment on the PR says where its review stands** (2026-10-14). Colleagues could not see that
  magnum was about to review a PR: the window had 7 `pr.merged_unreviewed` events, four of them 4 to 58
  minutes after the last push, inside or near the quiet period, and the operator was asked in Slack for
  reviews that waited out a quiet period, an interval or a slot. `[pipeline] status_comment` (default
  `false`, so the distributable defaults post nothing new; a `[[watch]] status_comment` overrides it as
  `whiteboard` does) gives each PR magnum means to review one comment on its conversation, posted as the
  PR's posting identity (`github.Client.CreateIssueComment`, `EditIssueComment`; the JSON body on gh's
  stdin), edited in place, its first line the marker `<!-- magnum:status -->`, its id, identity and last
  text's fingerprint in kv `pr.<id>.status_comment`. A checklist ticks down Scheduled (the head, "re-review
  of" after a review, and why it waits, with the end in UTC), In progress (since the round's start) and
  Posted (the review's link), with one fixed sentence ("A merge before the review posts skips it.") and
  `[pipeline] status_comment_note`, a line of the operator's; one line replaces it when magnum will not
  review the head (muted, ignored, Codex-flagged and held, needs_attention: "magnum will not review this
  head. The operator was told.", no cause) or GitHub merged it before the review posted. A closed PR is not
  edited again; drafts, post-merge reviews, dry runs and scratch registries (eval replays) get none.
  One place drives it: the tick reconciles every comment with the registry after `noteWaits`
  (`noteStatusComments`, engine/status_comment.go), the stage following from the PR's state, its recorded
  wait (`KVPRWait`) and its last review. The spec named the hooks a wait, a round start, a posted review, a
  mute, an ignore, a Codex flag, a park and a merge pass through; they lie in six files (wait.go, round.go,
  round_settle.go, abort.go and requests.go, codex_flag.go, poll.go) and run on the round goroutines as
  well as the tick, so they would need a lock per PR and a retry of their own for a write GitHub refused.
  From the tick, a refused or rate-held write is simply written by a later tick, a restart goes on from the
  registry, and only one goroutine ever writes a comment; the price is that In progress and Posted follow
  the round by a tick (30 s) or two. Rate: only a changed text is written (the header's time left out of the
  comparison), at most once per PR every 2 minutes (a failed attempt counts) and 10 writes a tick, which
  applies to every stage change too, not only to the waits. The words: the timing rules' waits (quiet,
  burst, the intervals, the cap, the delta, a snooze, a request's debounce) keep their own `Wait.Detail`,
  which holds only the config's durations and counts; every other wait gets a fixed phrase ("the end of
  quiet hours", "a retry after a failed attempt", "a free review slot", "is held on magnum's side"),
  because a retry's Detail quotes the failed attempt's error (a fetch's error names the PR's branch, which
  is PR text), a gate's names a pool, an identity or its error, and quiet hours are written in the
  operator's zone. A round on the reviewed head (a reply round, a CI check, a re-decision) leaves the
  comment at Posted. Failures never touch a round: `pr.status_comment_failed` (warn) at most once per PR an
  hour, `pr.status_comment` (info) for each write with its stage. A comment gone at an edit (404, a person
  deleted it) is posted once more; gone a second time, the PR gets none until its next head. Rejected: a
  comment per round (noise on every PR), a check run or a commit status (an App token on every repository,
  and no words: a status cannot say why it waits), a label (no progress, no time), hooks at each event
  (above), quoting every wait's Detail (PR and error text on a public conversation), and finding a lost
  comment again by its marker (a read of every PR's comments for a kv row the registry keeps; the marker
  is there for a person or a later tool).
- **The status comment ends truthfully, leads with the state in plain words and shows the earlier
  review** (2026-10-14). The first live comment showed three gaps. A PR closed without a merge was never
  edited again, so its comment stayed at Scheduled or In progress for good. A merged PR got its line only
  while closed or releasing, so a release before the tick left a stale one. A `magnum review` of the
  reviewed head stayed at Posted, because the reviewed-head check came before the queued and running
  states. The wording also misled: "updated HH:MM" moved only with the text, so it read as a heartbeat it
  is not; "a free review slot" is magnum's jargon; "until HH:MM" promised a start that capacity can delay.
  Now every comment ends on a true line, written at once (past the 2-minute spacing, unless its last
  attempt failed) and once: "Closed before the review of `<sha7>` posted.", "Merged before the review of
  `<sha7>` posted.", the posted line for a PR closed or merged after its review, the not-reviewing line
  kept for a muted one, and "Not reviewing: the PR is a draft." for a PR that turned into a draft (with
  `include_drafts = false`, so it left review) while the comment promised a review. The kv row records the
  end (its head, time and whether the PR was forced), and nothing is written after it until a new head, a
  review request newer than the end, a `magnum review`, a reopen, or the draft's ready for review. Released
  PRs are read too, but only those whose row changed in the last 24 hours (`store.PRFilter.UpdatedSince`):
  the last edit normally goes out while the PR is closed (the close grace), so the read only catches one
  GitHub refused, and reading every released PR at every tick would cost a kv read each for good. On the
  reviewed head, a round someone asked for restarts the list as "Another review requested for
  `<sha7>`": forced (`magnum review`, unless it asks to re-decide the replies, `kvPRRedecide`), a pending
  review request, the running round's `roundHandle.asked`, or a list the comment already shows for that
  head (a restart lost the handle); a reply round, a judge check of red CI and a re-decision leave the
  posted line, as before. The header reads "status changed 14 Oct, 18:43 UTC" and moves only with the
  stage, the review or the wait (kv `state` and `changed`); the first line leads with the state ("Review
  queued for", "Re-review queued for", "Another review requested for") and fixed words for every wait:
  "other reviews are running" for the slots and the capacity, "not before HH:MM UTC (<rule>)" for the
  timing rules, which now use a fixed name instead of their Detail (the spec's example drops the
  durations, and the nested parentheses would read badly), "a retry after a failed attempt", "starts
  shortly" or "held on magnum's side"; "This comment updates by itself." precedes the merge sentence. A
  posted review collapses the comment to one line ("Review of `<sha7>` posted 18:52 UTC: <link>") without
  the sentences or the operator's note, which is kept only while a review is to come or held. A re-review's
  list is followed by "Earlier review of `<sha7>`: <link>" (the latest one only) and, from the last
  review's `ReviewSummary.Open` when its record is that review's, "The last review recorded N earlier
  findings still open." (left out at 0 or unknown). A fix loop shows from its row alone: "Applying
  automatic fixes, cycle N of M" under the posted line in phase fixing, and "Reviewing the fixes in
  `<sha7>`" leading its re-review in phase reviewing. Left out: the usual duration of a round ("Reviews
  like this usually take 12 to 25 minutes"), since an honest figure runs from the round's start, which
  the In progress line shows and which includes the checkout and the sessions' start, while the runs table
  only has the first prompt's time; the round start of past rounds lives in the `engine.round_start`
  events, the spec's stop condition, and a runs-only figure would understate a pool repository's rounds by
  their checkout, inviting the merge the comment tries to prevent.
- **The daemon can take its PATH from the operator's login shell** (2026-10-14). launchd gives the daemon
  a fixed PATH (`launchdPATH`: `~/.local/bin`, mise's shims, Homebrew's and the system directories),
  which every command it runs inherits, while DBngin's MySQL, PostgreSQL and Redis directories, with the
  version in each name, are on the PATH only the operator's zsh plugin exports build. When talkable's test
  boot started to spawn `redis-server`, every test schema load the daemon ran failed (talkable#12025 four
  times, #12026, #12028), and two failed resets broke slots review11 and review18. Now `[daemon]
  shell_path` (default `false`) has the daemon command ask `$SHELL -ilc` (`zsh` when SHELL is unset) for
  its PATH once, in runDaemonEngine before app.New, so before anything the daemon runs (config loading
  and the prompt check run no command), detached from any terminal (NoTTY), without stdin and for 20 s
  at most, and append the entries its own PATH lacks, in the shell's order, with os.Setenv: launchd's
  PATH stays first and in order, so mise's shims still win, and the commands it starts inherit the rest
  (exec resolves names through the process's PATH). The script is `printf '%s\n' "$PATH"`, not the
  spec's `print -r -- $PATH`, which bash lacks. The last non-empty line that reads as a PATH (colon-
  separated absolute directories) counts, so banners and hook output around it are skipped. The engine
  records it at startup (engine.Options.ShellPATH): one `daemon.shell_path` event, info "PATH from zsh: 4
  directories added", or warn "the login shell (zsh) answered nothing in 20s. The launchd PATH stays"
  (fixed words for an exit, no PATH line or a shell that does not start, never the shell's output), and
  kv `daemon.shell_path` with the count for `magnum status`'s daemon line; the directories go to the
  debug log only, since a directory's name can carry a secret's path. A change of the shell's PATH takes
  effect at the next restart, as a config change does; the CLI keeps its terminal's environment and
  doctor gains nothing. daemonSys.RunEngine nil now means runDaemonEngine (which reads daemonSys for the
  capture: an initialization cycle otherwise). Rejected: the directories in a magnum key or in the
  LaunchAgent plist's PATH, which an upgrade of MySQL or Redis misses (the version is in the directory
  name, and the one file the operator maintains is the shell's exports file), and sourcing a named file,
  which depends on the shell's variables and plugins that only the shell's own startup sets.
- **Nine review rules from the 2026-10-14 run, and the room they need** (2026-10-14, amends "Thirteen review
  rules from the 2026-10-12 run" and the claude-review prompts' list of rejected candidates). The operator
  approved them on 2026-10-14, after the run's analysts read 57 posted reviews, 307 answered threads and the
  retro's misses. Each has a test in `internal/agents/review_format_test.go`. Eight change
  `skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md`. (1) Section 4, after the size, count or timing trigger: a race names the
  window's length and how often the competing writer runs; when a rerun or retry recovers, seconds against a
  daily or rarer writer is P3, a loss that stays and matters beyond one record is P2, and a failure that a
  plain rerun clears is not a broken migration or deploy. Five race findings on three PRs were posted as P1
  or P2 and declined: one a P1 about a row created after a daily ranking job had read the table, a
  sub-second gap a rerun healed, the others the same PR's next round and three findings on talkable#11958;
  no comment stated the window or the writer's rate. (2) Section 4's test-double clause: a double that
  allows an ordering, timing, limit or value the real component never produces proves nothing, and, in a
  sentence of its own after the order-of-calls clause (whose pin holds), for what an external system sends a
  recorded payload (the PR's QA evidence, fixtures, logs) outranks its docs; a Shopify app PR's P2 rested on
  a probe that set a field by hand and on Shopify's docs, while the author's real orders carried the product
  title. (4) Section 3's `duplicate` bullet: another reviewer's open P0–P2 the judge decided gets a body
  line, `Confirmed <link> (counted in N)` or `Considered <link>: <why not>`; talkable#11483 round 40 proved
  a colleague's P1 with a spec, rejected it as a duplicate of her thread and posted "Fix 1 problem", round
  41 said LGTM, and another Shopify app PR's first round did the same with a P1 from Shopify's changelog.
  (5) Section 2's authorization list: no caller refused that passes on the base, a key acting as a user
  included; talkable#12019 was approved, then a colleague found its new write gate refusing an API key whose
  acting first admin has no role on the key's site (the local eval case `key-write-gate-first-admin`). (6)
  Section 7: a probe only this machine has gets a Checks line that says what it exercised and its result,
  not its file name, and codex-review's unrun checks get no Checks line; 333 of 939 Checks lines in 45 of 55
  reviews named files only this machine has (`REVIEW_MUTATIONS=own-email-kind-scope.json bin/rspec`), and
  four reviews noted a role's sandbox, against the rule of no notes on the process. (7) Section 2, right
  after the sweep sentence (whose pin holds): the sinks of a value in a URL or header are such a set,
  analytics, error trackers, app logs, parameter filters, access logs, log shippers; talkable#11932's P1
  about status credentials in analytics and server logs stayed blocking for nine reviews while its sinks
  were found one at a time (analytics, two error trackers, two server filters, request parameters, access
  logs shipped to storage). (8) Section 7's merged-tree sentence: such specs get no `environment_failures`
  entry; talkable#12009 filed them as an environment failure three times. (9) Section 3 reads a report's
  list of what it rejected as context, not as claims to judge, and the three claude-review prompts no longer
  ask for that list, nor for a `Description: ✗` line beside a closed access hole's entry points (the
  entry-point list stays): 485 of 543 rejected ledger rows came from claude-review alone, 339 of them its
  own Rejected bullets that the judge re-judged, none became a posted finding, and the Description clause
  gave 8 candidates, all on talkable#11483, all rejected as P3 (7 `style_only`).
  `.claude/skills/magnum-improve/scripts/evidence.sh` still runs on a report without a Rejected list (its
  `self` column reads 0), so it stays as it is. One is in `judge-rereview.md` and `judge-recovery.md`, the
  prompts of the rounds that have earlier findings: (3) a verdict that blocks only on earlier findings names
  each of them in the body with its thread link, not only their count and the previous review's link;
  talkable#11932 rounds 45 and 46 posted "Blocking: 2 problems" with no new finding and one link to the
  previous review, while magnum's rebuttals sat in threads the author had resolved. The rules add 908 bytes
  (the rejected-list clause's change counted, -12). The room came from lens 11's trims: 240 bytes of
  unpinned wording (`run_id` folded into the next field line, the readiness kinds, "or to stop and ask",
  which the unattended rule at the top covers, "wrong behaviour" and the missing tests in section 2's
  checklist, which section 3 and the P2 definition hold, the Plain English guard, with 0 hits in 101
  comments, "when code names permit" and three words of section 5's word rules), the P1 OAuth callback, P2
  retried email and P3 wrong-field examples (217), and two merges (121): the two clauses on records thought
  unsaved or free became "a delete or reuse of records thought unsaved or free (uploads, drafts, unowned
  rows) that a save path leaves on a stale list or flag, or that another path creates in that state (trace
  every writer)", and the input no caller produces joined the operator-only trigger's sentence as "an input
  no caller, documented API or user sends is P3 at most", each ceiling as it was. SKILL.md went from 32,509
  to 32,839 bytes and `skillMaxBytes` from 32,511 to 32,839 (+328). Pins edited on purpose: the
  operator-only trigger sentence and the input sentence (TestSkillRanksTriggersOutsideTheAppsPathsLow,
  TestSkillCarriesTheRulesFromMisses), the unsaved-records clause and the opening of the
  records-thought-free pin (TestSkillCarriesTheRulesFromMisses,
  TestSkillChecksRowsThoughtFreeAndARemoteChangeBeforeALocalSave), the by-design limit sentence, rule 6's
  one (TestSkillKeepsByDesignLimitsOutOfMachineFailures), the merged-tree sentence
  (TestSkillSkipsDatabaseSpecsOnAMergedTreeWhoseBaseAddedMigrations), and the rejected-list clause, now a
  phrase the skill must not say (TestSkillDigsIntoChangedBehaviourAndReplacedMechanisms,
  TestSkillReadsAReportsRejectedListAsContext). Rejected: the skill editor's proposal 1, six one-off
  simplify rules in the judge prompts (the operator declined it on 2026-10-14; a general rule may still
  come), and moving the notes procedure to a NOTES.md read after posting for room (1,385 bytes, but it saves
  no tokens, since judges update the notes in 52 of about 60 rounds, it sidesteps the cap instead of keeping
  the rules tight, and the daemon would copy and pin a second file).
- **The login shell's PATH may hold a tilde or a relative entry** (2026-10-14, amends "The daemon can take its
  PATH from the operator's login shell"). The first capture on the operator's machine answered "printed no PATH":
  their zsh exports `~/.dotnet/tools` unexpanded, and `looksLikePATH` refused the whole line for one entry that
  was not absolute. The second capture failed on `/Applications/Little Snitch.app/Contents/Components`, an entry with a space. A line
  counts as a PATH when more than half of its entries are absolute; a `~` entry is expanded to HOME when appended,
  a relative one (`.`, `bin`) is left out, since the daemon's PATH holds directories, and a space is kept. Rejected: appending the entry as written (the daemon would search a literal `~`); refusing
  the line (one odd entry would cost every other directory).
- **Magnum's own mise files are undotted, and launchd goes through mise for either spelling** (2026-10-15).
  The repository's `.mise.toml` is now `mise.toml`, and the docs keep the private patterns and logins in
  `mise.local.toml`, as the repositories it reviews do; `.gitignore` names both local spellings, so an older
  `.mise.local.toml` stays ignored (mise still loads it). launchPrefix sent launchd and the gh shim through
  `mise exec` only when the checkout held `.mise.toml` or `.mise.local.toml`, so a checkout with only the
  undotted files would start the daemon without the variable an App's private_key_env reads. Now any of
  `mise.toml`, `.mise.toml`, `mise.local.toml` and `.mise.local.toml` counts, since mise reads each (the
  dotted file overrides the undotted one, https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html). The placeholder-key
  error names `mise.toml` and `mise.local.toml`. A reviewed repository's mise files already worked under
  either name ("The rendered local mise file keeps the main clone's spelling").
- **CI takes Go and golangci-lint from mise.toml** (2026-10-15, amends "A lint and CI gate"). Each job set up
  Go with actions/setup-go from go.mod, and golangci-lint-action installed its own pinned binary, so the
  workflow repeated the versions `mise.toml` pins. Now every job runs `.github/actions/setup-environment`:
  jdx/mise-action installs the `mise.toml` tools and exports its `[env]`, then actions/cache restores the
  module and build caches keyed on the job, the platform, the Go version mise reports, and the hash of
  `go.sum` and the workflow (a change of test flags still saves a new build cache), and `go mod download`
  runs. The weekly run on the newest Go sets MISE_GO_VERSION=latest, with mise's install cache under its own
  key, and its matrix leg is named `stable` beside `mise.toml` (was `go.mod`). golangci-lint-action keeps
  only-new-issues and runs the binary from PATH (install-mode none). govulncheck installs into
  `$RUNNER_TEMP/bin`, since mise sets GOBIN to its Go's directory. The exported `[env]` holds only
  MAGNUM_PRIVATE_PATTERNS = "", which `make check-private` treats as unset, and the workflow uses no secret it
  could shadow. Dependabot also watches `.github/actions/*`. Rejected: running golangci-lint by hand with
  `--new-from-rev` (the action already finds a push's and a PR's base).

- **A fix of an end state is judged against every write that reaches it** (2026-10-15, amends "Nine review
  rules from the 2026-10-14 run"). On a 24k-line PR the judge called a kept-tiers defect fixed, with a
  mutation that proved the new regression test and its own pass recording the fix as "limits writes to
  inserted actions", and approved; a colleague's next round found a second path to the same failure in the
  same restore: another write copied the tier flag onto a live action, which then paid nothing, and the
  fix had not touched it. The notes line the judge had written in that very round said to probe every
  later step that writes records depending on the kept thing, and the judge did not apply it to the fix
  before it. Section 6's `fixed` bullet now says that a defect that is an end state (a record left as the
  code cannot serve it, a value a reader cannot use) is fixed only when every write of the same flow that
  reaches that state is covered: list them, and probe one the fix leaves untouched. The rule adds 238 bytes;
  121 came from section 6's threads-file fallback (`gh api … --paginate` is in the prompt's `threads_file`
  anyway) and a shorter magnum's-own-line sentence, both unpinned, and the cap goes from 32,839 to 32,956.
  New test TestAFixOfAnEndStateIsJudgedAgainstEveryWriteThatReachesIt. The eval case
  `restore-turns-action-tier-based` holds the miss; it replays a first review, not a fix verification, so
  the next run reads the live re-reviews under the rule instead. Rejected: a judge prompt clause instead of a
  skill rule (the same discipline applies to the own pass and to recovery rounds); undoing the fix and
  watching the new test fail as the rule (magnum's mutation runs do that already, and they proved the test,
  not the fix's reach).
- **A fix's write set, a feature's optional branches and the notes applied are on the record** (2026-10-15,
  amends "A fix of an end state is judged against every write that reaches it"). A Codex read of the
  talkable#11483 misses named three habits the judge lacks. A fix was called fixed with no record of what
  it covered: the end-state rule says to list every write and probe one, and nothing made the list
  visible, so nobody could see a narrow verification. The three defects a colleague's round found share
  one shape: a feature that offers an optional or keep-current branch (skip these blockers, keep the live
  rewards, keep the current tiers) composed with a later step that assumes the skipped thing was created
  or replaced; the skill asked for callers and data flow, not for that composition. And the judge wrote
  that round's lesson into the repository notes in the same round in which it verified the fix, and did
  not apply it: the notes are read at the start and rewritten at the end, and writing a lesson is not
  applying it. Three rules in SKILL.md: (1) section 6's `fixed` bullet, after the end-state sentence: record
  each such fix in the own pass under `## Fix evidence` (the invariant, the writes that reach the state,
  those probed and those unproven); an unproven write the fix left untouched keeps the finding open. (2)
  Section 2, after the structure sentence and its "Report one only with the input that goes wrong.": for
  each optional or keep-current branch the PR adds (a skip, a retain, a force flag), name the state it
  keeps and every later step of the flow that assumes the skipped thing was created or replaced, and probe
  the reachable combinations end to end; not "through the real entry point", as the spec had it, since the
  skill must not say "entry point" (TestClaudeReviewersListTheEntryPointsOfAClosedAccessHole: such text
  drew Codex cybersecurity flags on judge turns). (3) Section 2's notes paragraph: before the verdict, the
  own pass lists under `## Notes applied` each notes line that applies, with the probe or argument that
  discharged it, or `unknown`; a lesson written this round applies to this round first. Each rule names
  its heading itself, shorter than a line about it in section 0 or 8. The rules add 675 bytes (212, 245
  and 218); 102 came from unpinned wording: the readiness statuses, now "each with its status and reason"
  (28), "edit files" in section 1, which "Do not change the code" at the top says (12), a stacked PR's
  lower layer "only as context" (24), an answered thread's "a reply, never a new comment" (14), and "A
  report's priority is a claim like any other", now "whatever a report says" (24). No pin was edited.
  SKILL.md went from 33,119 to 33,692 bytes and `skillMaxBytes` from 33,119 to 33,692 (+573). New tests
  TestSkillRecordsAFixesWriteSetAndUnprovenWrites, TestSkillProbesOptionalBranchesAgainstLaterSteps and
  TestSkillAppliesTheNotesBeforeTheVerdict, with the regenerated skill_pins.txt. Rejected: a judge prompt
  clause instead of skill rules (the own pass and the recovery round need them too).

- **The product is Magnum in everything it posts** (2026-10-15; the operator found "Magnum" and "magnum"
  mixed in GitHub comments). The review footer said "About Magnum" and "Automated review by Magnum" while
  the status comment was headed "magnum review status", said "held on magnum's side" and "magnum will not
  review this head", the operator's verdicts read "after magnum's review of", the withdrawn auto-approval
  "magnum: this automatic approval is withdrawn" and the default `auto_approve_body` "Approved after
  magnum's review of". Every text a person reads on GitHub now says Magnum; `magnum` stays the command
  (`magnum review`, `magnum unapprove`) and the markers (`<!-- magnum:… -->`), and the skill's section 5
  says so for the judge's own prose. The CLI, the logs and the events keep the lower-case name: they are
  the program, not the product. Rejected: lower case everywhere (the footer and the README's product
  name are capitalized already, and a sentence that starts with the name reads as a typo in lower case).

- **A fresh start heals an agent that will not quit** (2026-10-15, amends "A park that fails backs off, and
  its cause is recorded once"). The operator asked for fresh sessions on talkable#11932 twice (`magnum review
  --fresh`), and the round parks every agent of the PR first. The fixer's Claude Code stayed its pane's
  foreground process through two ctrl+c, so the quit's wait for an idle shell timed out (`agents: quit
  session 535: agent busy: herdr pane w9J:p1: shell not idle after 10s (foreground: 2.1.296)`). A busy agent
  is a wait, not a failure, so no attempt was charged: the board said "retry 1/3, agent busy" for 40 minutes
