  while the setup failed every 90 seconds, 26 times, and no round started. The park went through `Quit` at
  all because the PR's workspace held a fifth pane, a plain shell no session owns, and the park closes a
  workspace only when it holds the PR's panes alone. Now `agents.Manager.ParkHard` is `Park` whose quits go
  on where `Quit` waits. It sends the kind's `exit_keys` (a new `[kinds.<name>]` key, keys as herdr's
  send-keys takes them; claude: `/exit` then enter, one key each; the other built-in kinds: none) and waits
  `QuitIdleTimeout` again. A pane still not an idle shell is closed alone through herdr's `pane.close`
  (`herdr.Client.PaneClose`; herdr 0.9.3 has it, and `magnum doctor` now requires it), never its
  workspace, whose other panes may be anyone's. The session becomes closed with `closed_at`, never parked,
  and `pr.park_forced` (info) records the role, the pane and the cause (`no idle shell after ctrl+c and the
  exit keys; pane closed`), never the pane's text. An agent the exit keys quit is parked as by a plain quit,
  a pane herdr refuses to close fails as before (`agents.ErrBusy` with herdr's timeout), and every refusal
  of `Park` (a run in flight, an agent working or blocked, a busy pane of a workspace it closes) stands. The
  fresh start's park (`startSessions`, engine `parkFresh`) counts the tries an agent did not quit for (the
  `quit_timeout` class) in kv `pr.<id>.fresh_park_busy`: the first waits as today, the second and later ones
  park hard. A refusal because a run of the PR is in flight (a fixer or another round at work) counts
  nothing and is never forced, since that agent works and is not stuck. A round's start, a park that works,
  `magnum abort` and the PR leaving the round states delete the count. `magnum abort`'s park
  (`parkForStop`) is hard on its last of three tries. The retry label on the board and the card counts
  these tries too (`retry 2/3 agent busy` after the second, at most 3/3), since they charge no attempt; the
  status comment is unchanged. The idle park and the Codex-flag release keep the plain park and their
  backoff. Rejected: closing the pane on the first timeout, since a slow exit would lose a conversation
  that a second try keeps; a retry budget alone, since the third failure would leave the PR in
  needs_attention with the same stuck pane; closing the workspace, which on this machine holds a shell no
  session owns; typing `/exit` as one word, since herdr validates every key before it writes any and takes
  key combos only.
- **A finding names its harm, its size and the fix's cost in words, and P2 means the 10 anchor**
  (2026-10-15). Since 2026-10-13 the colleagues' reply skill scores every comment's suggestion: pros minus
  cons on an open scale with anchors (1 nobody notices, 3 the next person to touch the code feels it, 10
  real money, real user harm or a day of work, 30 not safe to ship), `Low priority` below a net of +5, and
  four kinds exempt whatever their net (a defect the diff introduced, a broken reference, a failing test, a
  crash). On talkable#12032 two of magnum's P3s got `Low priority, net 0` and `net +2.2`, and a Codex
  connector P2 got `net -6`. The operator asked whether magnum should post the same pros, cons and net; the
  evidence says no, as "No score before posting" (2026-10-05) did. Two blind scorers put the colleague's
  scale on 106 posted findings whose outcome the retro knows: they agreed (rank correlation 0.89), yet the
  chance that a fixed finding outscores a declined one was only 0.51 to 0.59, the median net of a fixed P2
  was 1.7 to 2.0, a +5 bar would have dropped 54 of the 79 findings the authors fixed, and a P-level derived
  from the net gives no P1 and at most three P2s. The colleague's tool itself scores magnum's fixed P2s at
  +3 to +4.5, and people fix them anyway; it adopts a posted net 11 times of 13. What carries across the
  two tools is a named consequence with its size (the tool weighs a pro above 3 only when the comment names
  one, and quotes the deciding pro), a stated regression (never dropped), and the fix's cost. The retro's
  13 over-ranked P2 declines all said the finding was right and the consequence small: a self-healing
  millisecond race, a hand-made request that fails only itself, a product choice, a risk the diff cannot
  fix, a throwaway test rig. P2's definition named reach and "harm beyond the triggering request", not the
  size of the harm. Four rules in `skills/magnum-review/SKILL.md`: section 4's P2 bullet adds that the
  comment names and sizes the harm (money, data or access lost, a task a user cannot finish, or a day of
  someone's work), and a harm that heals itself or ends with the request is P3; section 5's comment form
  gives the consequence its size (who loses what, how many, how often) and **Fix** what it costs (the lines
  it touches, what it could break), the cost never lowering the priority (2026-10-05 kept cost out of
  "is this real"); when the reproduction also ran at the base, one line before **Fix** states the
  regression, `This PR introduced it: on <base_ref>, <result>; with this PR, <result>.`, `base_ref` being
  the `<magnum>` block's name for the base branch (a finding in a feature the PR adds has no base result,
  which the rule's condition already covers, so the skill does not say it); and section 6 decides a reply
  that scores the fix (`Low priority, net -6. <reason>`) by its reason, never by the number: the judge
  rebuts only a fact it disproves at `head_sha`, or a consequence its comment sized that the reply leaves
  out, with the evidence and no score of its own, and honours a product decision, data only the author
  holds and every decline of a P3. That sentence follows "Then the finding stays open: …", not the
  "Honour it unless…" sentence before it, so that "Then" still follows a reason proved wrong. The rules
  add 838 bytes (175, 147, 165 and 351); three unpinned trims win back 114: section 4's two sentences after
  the P-list become one (41), section 5's "the author cannot see your machine" goes (36), and so does
  section 7's "Finish all analysis before you post." (37). SKILL.md goes from 34,124 to 34,848 bytes and
  `skillMaxBytes` from 34,124 to 34,848. New tests TestSkillP2NamesAndSizesItsHarm,
  TestSkillCommentsSizeTheConsequenceAndCostTheFix, TestSkillStatesARegressionAgainstTheBase and
  TestSkillDecidesAScoredDeclineByItsReason pin the four rules, and the two pins of the Fix sentence read
  "one smallest safe change, what it must keep" for "and what it must keep", the rule they protect kept;
  `skill_pins.txt` is regenerated. `skills/magnum-fix/SKILL.md` keeps its own scoring (the fixer fixes at a
  net of 3 on the same anchors). Rejected: posting `Pros:`, `Cons:` and `Net:` lines, since a posted net
  of +2 under a P2 hands the author's tool a number below its own bar and the nets did not predict fixes;
  deriving the P-level from a net, which on real data gives no P1 and at most three P2s; an internal net in
  the result file as a measurement, since the blind experiment already measured it; and leaving P3s out,
  since colleagues fixed 27 of 33 answered P3s.
- **Auto-approval leaves the PRs of listed authors to a person** (2026-10-16, spec 50). With `auto_approve`
  and `auto_approve_as` magnum posts the operator's own approval on a head its review found nothing
  blocking on, and the operator wants some authors kept out of that: a colleague whose PRs must get an
  explicit human review before they merge, whatever magnum's review says. The only way was to stop
  auto-approval per PR after the fact (`review.auto_approve_stopped`). A `[[watch]]` key
  `auto_approve_skip_authors` lists GitHub logins, matched as `skip_authors` matches them (any case, with or
  without `[bot]`; an empty entry or one with whitespace in it is refused, naming the block, and a duplicate
  matches as one), and the same key on a `[[repo]]` block adds logins for that repository alone
  (`Config.AutoApproveSkipsAuthor`; a field, two lines of matching and one of validation). On such a PR
  the automatic approval never posts: `authorRefusal` refuses before the gates (`autoGateRefusal`) with
  "the author is in auto_approve_skip_authors", recorded for the card and in one
  `review.auto_approve_refused` event per head (its record names no round, `run_id` "", so a second clean
  round of the head writes nothing; a round that finds something to fix clears it, as it clears the other
  reasons). A standing approval is not held to it: `standingGateRefusal` runs `autoGateRefusal` alone, so
  an approval posted before the author was listed, and the operator's own `A` (recorded like an automatic
  approval), stand, and a later review that finds something to fix withdraws either as before. `A` and
  `magnum approve --as` still approve (`OperatorApprovalRefusal` never asks the gates): the point is a
  person's decision, and the operator is that person. The card says "auto-approval: off for this author (auto_approve_skip_authors)", dim, in place
  of the refusal's yellow sentence (the board reads the key in the reason, as `skipWord` reads
  `skip_authors`), `auto_approve_refused` in `magnum tui --json` carries the reason, and the row shows no
  `✔ auto`. Nothing on GitHub names the author or the list: the status comment never spoke of
  auto-approval and reads as on a watch without it. Rejected: a label on the PR (the author can remove it);
  a `[[repo]]`-only key (the rule is about a person across repositories); posting a GitHub comment that
  names the exclusion (author-visible and needless); refusing inside `autoGateRefusal`, which a standing
  approval's later round runs too, so the next clean round of the head would withdraw the operator's own
  `A` approval.
- **An author's own inline threads are not replies, and a reply round with nothing to answer ends
  replied** (2026-10-16, spec 51, amends "Replies on magnum's threads get an answer without a push").
  On 2026-10-15 the author of a PR posted eight inline comments
  on it, the findings of their own review tool, each a review that started a new thread, and pushed their
  fixes a minute later. `repliesOf` counted every review or comment by the PR author as a reply to
  magnum's review, so the eight read as "8 replies to the review" and started a reply round of the judge
  alone on the old head; post-review refused each of its replies ("comment N does not start a thread of
  …", the right guard), the judge wrote `blocked`, the PR went to needs_attention and the re-review of the
  new head waited 15 hours for the operator's retry. An author's review now counts as a reply when it
  answers in one of magnum's threads (`Remark.Answers` names an own login) or has no inline comments (a
  body alone answers the review as a whole), and an issue comment counts as before; a review whose inline
  comments start threads of the author's own or answer another reviewer's (`AnswersKnown`, `Comments` > 0,
  no own login in `Answers`) is the author's own finding. `github.Remark.Comments` is new: how many inline
  comments the review has (of its first ten), read from the replies connection the poll already fetches
  (no query change, no cost), since `Answers` alone holds nothing both for a review whose comments start
  threads and for one with a body alone. That connection resolves the timeline's last two reviews only,
  which on the 12031 shape left six of the eight unresolved, still counting under the old rule. So the
  poll now asks GitHub what the inline comments of every other review newer than magnum's latest review
  of the PR (`reviewed_at`, the review a reply round would answer) answer, up to ten per PR, the newest
  (`resolveAnswers`, `github.Client.ReviewAnswers`: `nodes(ids:)` with each review's first ten comments
  and their `replyTo` author, keyed by the review's node id, the new `Remark.ID`): one call for the poll's
  batch, none when no PR needs it. GitHub's dry run (2026-10-16, against a public repository) priced it at
  1 point for 1, 10, 40 and 100 reviews (a call asks about at most 100), while the Details query stays at
  1, 1, 3 and 5 points for 1, 10, 20 and 40 PRs (1, 1, 2 and 4 without its replies connection). An older
  review beyond the cap, or one a failed call (`poll.answers_error`, warn) left unresolved, keeps the old
  rule (`AnswersKnown` false); trusted repliers (owner, member, collaborator) count only in magnum's
  threads, as before. post-review's replies mode no longer refuses
  the whole file for a reply to a thread the reviewer login (or a former one) did not start: it skips
  that reply, lists it under `skipped` with the reason (who started the thread, no text), posts the rest
  and exits 0 with `replied` even when it posted nothing ("nothing posted; skipped 3 replies to threads
  someone else started"); a comment that is no thread's first comment on the PR (another PR's, a reply
  inside a thread), a malformed reply, a duplicate and a third rebuttal still exit 2 with `invalid`. The
  JSON gains `skipped` beside `replies`, which the prompts' "the `replies` it printed" reads unchanged.
  SKILL.md section 8 and the reply-round clause of `judge-rereview.md` and `judge-recovery.md` say in one
  sentence: "A thread another reviewer or the author started is theirs, never answered inline; a reply
  round with nothing of yours to answer ends `replied` with no replies, never `blocked`." (177 bytes; the
  skill's cap goes from 35,002 to 35,179.) A reply round whose judge result is `replied` with no replies
  already ended `replied` (the pipeline's `repliedVerdict`) and left the PR reviewed with its replies read
  (`replies_read_at`, so the same replies start no new round; `pr.<id>.reply_round` names the head); it
  now also records `round.replies_none` (info: how many replies started it, how many of them are in
  magnum's threads, and so why none was magnum's to answer: "none of them is in one of magnum's threads",
  or "the 1 reply in magnum's threads needed no answer"). For one release, a `blocked` result in a reply
  round whose blocker names post-review's refusal of replies to threads magnum did not start ("does not
  start a thread", "reply validation", a foreign thread: `foreignThreadBlock`) ends the round `replied`
  with nothing answered and a `round.warning` (warn), so a judge on the old skill during an upgrade does
  not park the PR; any other blocker, and the same one in a round that asked for a review, stay blocked.
  The shim sits in the pipeline's verdict, where a result file becomes an outcome, rather than in the
  engine after it: the judge run is then verified `replied` and `engine.round_result` says `replied`, as for
  a judge on the new skill, instead of a failed blocked run the engine overrides. Rejected: counting no
  author review at all (a review body "fixed, see the commit" is a reply); treating a refused reply as a
  judge failure (the guard is right, and the round is not wrong: it had nothing of its own to answer).
- **A start clears a dead launch that holds its agent name, and a fresh start closes the panes it
  replaces** (2026-10-16, amends "A judge that never comes up is started once more, and no start adopts
  the agent of a session magnum ended", "A cold judge is not lost to the agent it quit" and "A fresh start
  heals an agent that will not quit"). On talkable#11932 codex-cli 0.163.0 died at its TUI bootstrap in
  every judge pane, and herdr kept each failed launch listed as an agent with `launch_pending: true` and
  `agent_status: unknown` on a pane that showed only a shell prompt (`mg-11932-codex-judge-5d01cf` on
  w9J:p2). Every later start of the judge under that name
  failed with herdr's `agent_name_taken`, and the cold judge's quit refused the round because herdr still
  listed the agent it quit: three attempts, needs_attention, a retry after a restart, three more, and the
  board read "retry 3/3 setup" for hours until the operator closed the pane by hand. A launch that never
  came up is now cleared (`agents` `clearDeadLaunch`): when herdr lists the role's name on an agent that is
  `launch_pending` or at status `unknown` (never one working or blocked) and the pane's foreground process
  is its shell (`pane.process_info`, `herdr.IdleShell`; a pane that runs anything is left alone, as is one
  herdr cannot answer for), magnum closes that pane (`pane.close`, as the hard park does) and records
  `pr.launch_cleared` (warn: the role, the agent, the pane, its replacement, whether the launch was
  pending, and the CLI's own last error line there as `paneError` reads it, never the TUI's text, which a
  PR can steer). `StartAgent` does it before anything else. When the launch held the very pane the role
  was given, a replacement is split from it first (down, so it takes the closed pane's place), with the cwd
  and pane environment the PR's newest session that recorded that pane has (else the role's newest), and
  named like it; the starting and live sessions that pointed at the closed pane point at the replacement,
  and the closed pane's id forwards to it for the daemon's life (`Manager.replacement`), so a caller still
  holding the old id (the round's judge restart, the resume after a checkout, a later role's split anchor)
  lands in the new pane. With no environment recorded there is no replacement, since a pane without the
  role's identity env would act as the wrong account: the pane is closed all the same, its sessions become
  lost and the start fails busy, so the next attempt's workspace lays a pane out. The cold judge's quit
  (and the session rotation's, both `quitToRenew`) keeps its ten-second wait for herdr to drop the quit
  agent; a name still listed then goes through `agents.Manager.ClearDeadLaunch` with the session's pane as
  the one to replace, and the judge starts fresh in this round when it was cleared, busy as before when it
  was not. An agent at status unknown in the start's pane used to be launched anew there (herdr answered
  `agent_name_taken` while the launch was pending) and one in another pane made the start busy; both are
  now cleared when their pane is an idle shell. herdr 0.9.5 offers no cheaper drop: `agent.rename` would
  keep the launch listed under another name, and `pane.release_agent` releases the lifecycle authority an
  integration's hooks report (it takes their source and agent label), not a launch `agent.start`
  registered, and its effect on one cannot be checked without the live socket. The same PR's workspace
  held 17 panes (one claude-fix, two claude-whiteboard, two codex-judge, six claude-review, six
  codex-review): a fresh start parks the PR's sessions, which leaves their panes as idle shells while the
  operator's shell keeps the workspace open (and a session the PR lost there keeps the next start in it),
  `EnsureWorkspace` reuses a pane only for a lost session, and nothing closed the old ones but the hard
  park's close of a stuck agent. Now a fresh start's park that worked (engine `parkFresh`, plain or hard)
  and the hard park of `magnum abort`'s last try (`parkForStop`) close the panes of the sessions the park
  retired (engine `closeRetiredPanes`, `agents.Manager.CloseRetiredPanes`): every pane of the PR's parked
  and closed sessions that herdr still has, when its foreground process is the shell and no agent listed
  there works or is blocked, and never one a starting, live or lost session of the PR records (a lost
  session's pane is the one the next workspace reuses) nor one no session records (the operator's shell).
  One `pr.panes_closed` (info) gives the count, the roles and the panes; a pane herdr refuses to close is
  logged, and the park still holds. So the workspace keeps one pane per role of the round plus the panes
  magnum does not own. A parked session whose pane is closed keeps its conversation: `ResumeID` never
  looked at a pane, `Recover` leaves a parked session herdr shows nowhere alone, and the role's next start
  resumes it (`resume {session}`) in the pane the workspace lays out, as for a lost session. The idle park
  and the Codex-flag release keep their panes as before. The retry loop says what blocked it: the stored
  error keeps the start's own words, and `attention.Explain` (the card's line, `magnum attention`, `magnum
  status`) reads a launch that never came up in them (herdr's `agent_name_taken` after the start's "start
  <agent> in <pane>", or the start finding the name in another pane, "herdr still lists in pane <pane> …;
  the agent never came up"): the cause becomes "a dead launch holds the codex-judge's pane w9J:p2 (agent
  mg-11932-codex-judge-5d01cf): closed on the next retry", so the summary of a PR that spent its attempts
  reads "agents failed 3× on <head>: a dead launch holds …" (one that still retries reads it too, kind
  failed whatever herdr's message says), and the next step says the retry closes the pane when it shows
  only a shell, `magnum review` retries now and `magnum open` shows a pane that runs something. Any other
  chain reads as before. Rejected: a new agent name per attempt (herdr would list the dead one for as long
  as its pane lives, and the workspace would still grow by a pane per attempt); closing the whole workspace
  (it can hold the operator's own shell); leaving the panes (17 slivers after a day of retries, and `o`
  opened a workspace of them).
- **A fix is probed on the shapes its writers leave, and a reviewer reads the writer before it drops a
  candidate** (2026-10-16, amends "A fix of an end state is judged against every write that reaches it").
  On talkable#11483 a colleague's whole-branch review found, for the third time, a defect in the restore's
  tier handling right after a magnum round said the fix was fine. The round-11 fix rested on a premise its
  commit message and a code comment state: the action editor saves a flat action with only disabled tier
  rows. Rounds 43 and 46 both probed the fix with flat actions built by hand from disabled rows, so the
  premise was in every probe; the editor's store keeps enabled rows when staff switch "Tier based reward"
  off, so the restore overwrote them and a renamed tier's members got 0 points. Round 43's claude-review
  had weighed that exact outcome and dropped it on the same premise ("which is what the disabled row gave
  before"), and the judge never sees a reviewer's drops. The end-state rule pointed away from the defect:
  "every write of the same flow" and "probe one the fix leaves untouched" send the judge to the flow's
  other writes, while this one was the fix's own write on an input shape nobody built through its real
  writer. SKILL.md section 6 now says "every write that reaches that state", and after "probe one the fix
  leaves untouched." adds: a fix can rest on what another part writes (a comment: the editor saves
  disabled rows); probe it on each shape those writers leave, built through them (a UI form, an API
  outside the diff), not by hand; what passed before the fix and fails now is a finding. The three
  claude-review prompts add, after the base-branch search before a drop: a candidate or a fix can rest on
  what another part of the app writes (a code comment says an editor saves only disabled rows); read that
  writer before you drop the candidate or accept the fix. The skill grows by 193 bytes (257 for the
  sentence, less 17 for "of the same flow" and 47 of unpinned wording: section 2's "existing" review
  comments, section 6's "that" before the new commits, its rebuttal sentence and "repository" before its
  notes, and section 7's "if any"), and the cap goes from 35,179 to 35,372. New test
  TestAFixIsProbedOnTheShapesItsWritersLeave; TestAFixOfAnEndStateIsJudgedAgainstEveryWriteThatReachesIt
  pins the shorter rule and refuses "every write of the same flow", and
  TestReviewersSearchTheBaseBeforeTheyReject the prompts' sentence. Rejected: reading the reviewers'
  dropped candidates in the judge's prompt (339 of claude-review's Rejected bullets in one run were
  re-judged and none became a posted finding: "Nine review rules from the 2026-10-14 run"); a judge prompt
  clause instead of the skill rule (the own pass and recovery rounds verify fixes too).
- **A listed bot's PR is reviewed although bots are skipped** (2026-10-16, spec 54). `skip_bot_authors`
  (default true) keeps every bot's PR out of review, so a PR a GitHub App that writes code for the team
  opened sat ineligible with "bot author"; the operator wants such PRs reviewed, bot by bot, without
  reviewing every dependency bot's. A `[[watch]]` key `allow_bot_authors` lists bots' GitHub logins, and the
  same key on a `[[repo]]` block adds logins for that repository alone (`Config.AllowsBotAuthor`), matched
  as `auto_approve_skip_authors` matches them (`github.SameLogin` of the lowercased logins: any case, with
  or without `[bot]`, so the GraphQL author "helper" of `__typename` Bot is helper[bot]; the matcher,
  `listsLogin`, now serves both lists, so an `auto_approve_skip_authors` entry with "[Bot]" in another case
  matches as well) and validated as it is (`validateLogins`: no empty entry, no whitespace, the error naming
  the block). The engine's `factsFor` sets `PRFacts.AllowedBot` for a bot's PR the watch's
  `skip_bot_authors` skips when either list names its author (it reads the PR's repository for the
  `[[repo]]` list only then, as for `manual_repos`), and `eligibility.Classify`'s bot rule lets that PR
  through: it meets the other filters as a person's PR would, `skip_authors` first, so a login on both lists
  is skipped with skip_authors' reason, and with `skip_bot_authors = false` the list changes nothing. Its
  author is still a bot: its remarks count only in magnum's threads (`repliesOf`), nothing in the PR is
  trusted, and auto-approval treats it as any PR its watch reviews (`auto_approve_skip_authors` keeps it
  out). The PRs skipped before the list needed no new guard: the poll classifies a known PR again only when
  GitHub reports a change, but the daemon's start runs `reclassifyIneligible` before its first poll, which
  passes every open ineligible PR with Details through `onSeenPR` as changed, so a bot's PR first seen
  ineligible is queued ("ineligible → queued (now eligible)") with no head change and the first poll's
  dispatch starts its round, and one open since the repository's first sync that `skipBaseline` marked
  goes back to baseline (`restoreBaseline`), as the first sync left it: each where a newly seen PR would be.
  The board, the card and `magnum tui --json` name a skip rule only for a skipped PR, so nothing new shows
  there. New tests TestAListedBotsPRIsReviewedAlthoughBotsAreSkipped (engine: "Helper" lets helper's PR,
  in GraphQL's form, through under a `[[repo]]` block that adds nothing, and another bot's stays "bot
  author"), TestAnIneligibleBotPRBecomesEligibleAtTheNextPoll (engine: after a restart on a `[[repo]]`
  list, the skipped new PR is queued at the start and reviewed by the first poll, with no head change, and
  the skipped baseline PR is back to baseline), TestAnAllowedBotPassesSkipBotAuthors and
  TestSkipAuthorsWinsOverAllowBotAuthors (eligibility), TestAllowBotAuthorsRefusesAnEmptyOrSpacedLogin and
  TestAllowsBotAuthorMatchesTheListedBots (config). Rejected: `skip_bot_authors = false` per repository
  (every dependency bot's PR there would be reviewed too); a label on the PR (the bot would have to set it).
  The gap the live daemon showed after it restarted on the list (2026-10-16): the App's PR stayed
  ineligible with "bot author" and no event, because GitHub gives an App's PR the `authorAssociation`
  NONE (an App is never an owner, member or collaborator, whatever its installation writes; the test fakes
  said MEMBER), so once the list lifted the bot rule `skip_departed_authors` rejected it, and neither
  `onSeenPR` nor `restoreBaseline` wrote the reason of a PR another rule still skips. Now the departed rule
  reads only people's association (a bot's PR the bot rule lets through, listed or under
  `skip_bot_authors = false`, where every one read as having left before, is never departed), and a PR
  classified again that another rule now skips takes that rule's reason with a `pr.ineligible` event
  "ineligible → ineligible: <reason>" (`reskip`; the same rule writes nothing), at the start and at a
  poll. New tests TestAListedAppsPRLeavesIneligibleAtTheRestart (engine: the live configuration and row,
  with and without the skipped-baseline mark), TestAReclassifiedPRNamesTheRuleThatSkipsItNow (engine) and
  TestTheDepartedRuleNeverSkipsABot (eligibility).
- **The fix loop decides only on the re-review it forced** (2026-10-16, spec 56). On talkable#11932 a
  loop's forced re-review (round 53, a recovery) posted with one optional P3 left at 22:25 while `magnum
  daemon-restart --drain` held the daemon, so its next cycle waited for the restart in phase reviewing. A
  reply came at 22:28 and queued a reply round; the restart at 22:31 found the PR waiting in line, and its
  recovery (`recoverReviewingLoop`) kept the loop for what it took to be its re-review. The reply round
  (round 54, the judge alone on the same head) ended `replied` with nothing to answer, and the hook
  (`fixAfterRound`) handed it to `continueFixLoop`, whose first rule ends a loop whose re-review did not
  post: "fix loop ended: the re-review did not post (replied)", the PR in needs attention under `fix`
  although its review stood. The hook now gets the round's job as dispatch launched it and passes on only
  the loop's re-review (`notLoopsReReview`): the forced round dispatched at or after the loop's force,
  which the row now records (`FixState.ForcedAt`, set by `fixReReview`; the new `roundJob.dispatchedAt`;
  a row written before takes any forced round), whatever its setup made of it (a re-review, a recovery, a
  continued turn). Only the loop forces while its row exists, since `magnum review` and a second loop are
  refused. Its head is not asked: the forced round reviews the PR's head at dispatch, which a push of the
  operator's may have moved past the fixer's, and `continueFixLoop` already reads that move. A post-merge
  review, a reply round, a CI check, an audit pass, a full pass the scheduler started, a round nobody
  forced, a forced round dispatched before the loop's force and any round after the loop's re-review ended
  are recorded at info as `fix.round_ignored` ("round 54 ended replied: a reply round, not the re-review the
  fix loop forced on 76cd67b", with the round, its outcome and head and the loop's data), the row is left
  as it is, and the loop goes on as the restart's recovery would. A next cycle a drain refuses now marks the
  row held (`FixState.Held`, `holdNextCycle`, compare-and-set; the row is kv JSON, so no migration): no round
  that ends afterwards is the loop's, and the recovery starts a held cycle at once on the last review posted
  at the loop's head, also while the PR waits in line for a reply round or another round (the restart, a
  drain lifted without one); with a round in flight or paused it waits for that round's end, which the hook
  ignores before it goes on. The next cycle's row drops both fields. The status comment no longer says that
  the next round of a held loop reviews the fixer's push. A row a loop left this way is not repaired in code
  (the operator decides), but a forced re-review never ends replied, so the attention line of "fix loop
  ended: the re-review did not post (replied)" names the round the loop mistook ("the loop took a reply
  round for its re-review, which had posted: the review stands") with `magnum fix` and `magnum review` as
  the remedies, while a re-review of the loop's own that did not post still reads as written. New tests
  TestAReplyRoundNeverEndsTheFixLoop (the 10-16 layout: the re-review posts one P3 under a drain, a member
  replies, the drain's command ends after the tick looked at the held loops and before its dispatch, the
  reply round ends replied under a second drain, the loop stays held with `fix.round_ignored`, and the
  restart starts cycle 2), TestAHeldNextCycleStartsAfterTheRestart (the 10-16 restart with the reply round
  in line: cycle 2 starts at once, and the next round is the forced re-review of the fixer's push),
  TestTheFixLoopActsOnItsOwnReReview (clean, next cycle, capped, with the force's time recorded) and
  TestASchedulerRoundWhileTheLoopWaitsIsIgnored (seven rounds the loop did not force, each posting a clean
  review, leave the row as it was, and the loop's own re-review then starts cycle 2) in engine, and
  TestAMistakenReplyRoundIsNamedInTheAttentionLine in attention. Rejected: treating any round's end as the
  loop's re-review (what happened); matching the re-review by the fixer's head, which would strand a loop
  whose forced round reviewed the operator's later push, and which a reply round on the same head passes
  anyway; a new phase for the hold, which every reader of the phase (the board, `magnum status`, the
  recovery, dispatch's fixing hold) would have to learn.
- **The fixer compacts its conversation before a cycle when its context is nearly full** (2026-10-17,
  spec 57). The fixer (claude-fix) is one Claude Code session resumed across every fix cycle of a PR
  (`fixStart`), and nothing rotates it as `max_session_rounds` rotates the judge. On a long PR
  (talkable#11483) the operator saw it near its full context; Claude Code then compacts by itself at the
  limit, in the middle of a turn, and can lose the finding it was fixing. Now, before a cycle prompts a
  fixer it resumed (its session was live, or `ensureAgent` resumed a parked one), the job reads the
  context from the pane's last status lines, as the model switch reads the model
  (`agents.Manager.ContextUsed`, the kind's new `context_pattern`: a Go regexp with a `used` or `left`
  group, the newest match counting; claude's reads the operator's `418k/1m (41%)` and Claude Code's
  "Context left until auto-compact: 8%" as 92%). At or above the new `[pipeline] fix_compact_at`
  (default 70, 0 = off, at most 99) it types `/compact` into the idle pane as `/model` is typed
  (`agents.Manager.Compact`: the turn ends once the agent was seen working and is idle on two polls, at
  most 10 minutes; its `last_prompt_at` is set and the observer never takes that turn for a human's),
  reads again and records `fix.compacted` ("from 82% to 31%"). A figure still at or above the key and a
  compaction that did not finish (timed out, or the agent was busy) park the fixer (`quitToRenew`, as for
  a cold judge) and start it fresh for the cycle with `fix.fresh_session`, saying why; the fix prompt
  carries the findings, so the fresh fixer loses what it declined and ran, not what to fix. A pane with no
  figure leaves the resumed session as it is, with no `/compact` and no fresh session, and warns
  `fix.context_unknown` once per PR (kv `pr.<id>.fix_context_unknown`): a fresh session there would be
  the rejected fresh-fixer-every-cycle below, and a figure missing right after a resume would cost a fresh
  fixer each cycle. A compaction that ended with no figure after it keeps the session too, as
  `fix.compacted` from the figure before it, and warns the same once. A fixer that starts fresh anyway is
  never read, and a kind with `context_pattern = ""` (codex, droid, omp: Codex compacts by itself) never
  is. The loop's row records the cycle's words (`FixState.Context`: "compacted 82% → 31%", "compacted from
  82%", "fresh session (82% after /compact)", "fresh session (/compact failed)"), which the card's `fix:`
  line in `magnum status <ref>` shows after the role and `--json` carries; the status comment says
  nothing. The judge and the reviewers are unchanged. Not verified live: whether Claude Code's status line
  shows the figure right after a `--resume` and right after `/compact`, before the next turn; a status line
  that showed the old figure after `/compact` would start the fixer fresh each time, which the
  `fix.fresh_session` events would show. New tests TestTheFixerCompactsBeforeACycleWhenItsContextIsHigh,
  TestAFixerStillFullAfterCompactionStartsFresh, TestAFailedCompactionStartsTheFixerFresh,
  TestAFigureMissingAfterCompactionKeepsTheSession, TestAFixerBelowTheKeyIsNotCompacted,
  TestAFreshFixerIsNeverCompacted and TestNoContextFigureWarnsOncePerPR (engine), TestContextUsedReadsBothForms,
  TestCompactTypesTheCommandAndWaitsForTheTurnToEnd and TestCompactWaitsQuietlyAndRefusesABusyAgent
  (agents), TestFixCompactAtRefusesABadPercent and TestContextPatternMustCompileAndNameAGroup (config),
  and TestTheStatusCardNamesTheFixersCompaction (cli). Rejected: letting Claude Code auto-compact (in
  the middle of a turn, where it loses the finding); a fresh fixer session every cycle (it loses what it
  changed, declined and ran); a fixed cycle count instead of the figure (blind to the real usage: a small
  PR would be compacted for nothing, a big one too late).
- **A parked session's pane is closed at every park and at the restart** (2026-10-17, spec 58, amends "A
  start clears a dead launch that holds its agent name, and a fresh start closes the panes it replaces").
  Only a fresh start's park and a stop's hard park closed the panes they retired; the idle park, the
  release of a Codex-flagged PR, an eviction, `magnum release` and a lost agent left theirs as shells
  ("Resume this session with: …"). On 2026-10-17 talkable#11932's workspace held 21 panes (2 claude-fix, 3
  codex-judge, 7 claude-review, 7 codex-review, 2 claude-whiteboard) for 4 live sessions, with 19 sessions
  parked and 9 lost, because no fresh start had run on it since. Now every park that worked closes the
  panes of the PR's retired sessions (engine `closeRetiredPanes`): the idle park, of a reviewed PR and of
  one whose next round waits behind a pause, a drain, the cap or a far retry (a round's agents stay live
  when it ends and are parked by that park; there is no park at a round's very end), the Codex-flag
  release, an eviction, a failed `magnum open`'s release, `magnum abort` and `magnum ignore` on any of
  their three tries (the hard one alone did), a fresh start as before, and the park of the cleanup
  (`magnum release`, a closed PR's release, a slot's removal) through `agents.Manager.ParkClosingPanes`,
  which the app wires as cleanup's `Park`. A session the tick marks lost queues the same close for its PR
  (`closePanesJob`, on the heavy worker under the PR's slot-work reservation). The reconcile, at the start
  and every `reconcile_interval`, closes what is left for every PR a session of which records a pane herdr
  has (`closeLeftoverPanes`: one herdr snapshot, the new `store.PRsWithPanes`, then one sessions query per
  such PR through the new `agents.Manager.CloseRetiredPanesIn`), each PR under its reservation, so the
  leftovers of today close at the next restart; it records `pr.panes_closed` only when it closed something.
  A round, an open, a fix or a whiteboard job holding the PR is never raced: the lost close and the
  reconcile skip it, since its setup reuses a lost pane (`EnsureWorkspace`) and a close between its read
  of the sessions and the role's start would take the pane the role is about to start in; the next
  reconcile closes what the PR still has once it let go. The rules of `CloseRetiredPanes` change in three
  ways: a lost session's pane closes like a parked or closed one's (spec 52 kept it for the next workspace
  to reuse, which still happens while it survives; once closed, the next workspace splits a pane instead,
  the same count); a pane counts only while it sits in the workspace its session recorded, so a stale id
  herdr now shows in another workspace is never closed; and a workspace the closes leave with no pane,
  which herdr still lists on a fresh snapshot, is closed too (`pr.panes_closed` names it under
  `workspaces`), since a lost session there would make the next start reuse it with nothing to split
  from. What stays is unchanged: the panes of starting and live sessions, panes no session records (the
  operator's shell), panes whose foreground is anything but the shell, and panes where herdr lists an
  agent working or blocked. A parked or lost conversation keeps its id and resumes in the pane the next
  workspace lays out (a PR whose sessions are all parked gets a new workspace, and the old one keeps only
  the operator's shell). `magnum open` and the board's `o` open what is live: when the role's session is
  lost or closed with nothing parked to restore, or its session still reads live while herdr has no agent
  there (a pane closed by hand before a tick saw it), they focus a live agent pane of the PR, the judge's
  first, and say why ("the codex-judge session is lost and its pane gone; focused claude-review"), as a
  shell role's pane already fell back to the judge's. A parked role is restored by the daemon as before,
  its conversation resumed in a new pane. When every pane is gone but the operator's shell, nothing can be
  focused: herdr 0.9.5 focuses agents only (`agent.focus`; its socket has no workspace or pane focus), so
  `magnum open` names `magnum review <ref>`, as it did for a lost session, and the next round's panes are
  what `o` opens then. New tests TestAnIdleParkClosesItsPane, TestARoundsEndParkClosesItsPane (the park
  after a round whose next one waits behind `magnum pause`), TestTheRestartClosesTheLeftoverPanes (the
  11932 layout: the restart's reconcile closes the 17 leftovers in one event, the 4 live panes and the
  operator's shell remain, no session changes state, and a second reconcile records nothing),
  TestThePeriodicReconcileClosesPanesButRecordsNothingWhenIdle, TestALostAgentsPaneIsClosedAtOnce and
  TestEveryParkThatWorksClosesItsPanes in engine, TestALostSessionsPaneIsClosed and
  TestTheReleaseParkClosesItsPanes in agents, TestPRsWithPanesNamesThePRsWhoseSessionsRecordThem in store
  and TestOpenFocusesALivePaneWhenTheRolesPaneIsGone in cli; TestClosingRetiredPanesKeepsWhatIsStillInUse
  keeps a starting session's pane where it kept a lost one's. Rejected: keeping the panes for a resume
  (the resume needs none: it starts in the pane the workspace lays out, as spec 52's tests show); closing
  only at a fresh start (the case above: 21 panes for 4 live sessions); closing a lost pane at once under a
  round (the race above); a herdr snapshot per PR at the reconcile; closing the whole workspace (it holds
  the operator's shell).
- **The fixer's context figure is awaited after a resume** (2026-10-17, spec 59, amends "The fixer
  compacts its conversation before a cycle when its context is nearly full"). Spec 57 read the figure once,
  right after `ensureAgent` resumed a parked fixer, before Claude Code had drawn its status line: both
  `fix.context_unknown` warnings since its landing came 0.2 s after the resume (talkable#11483, session
  983; talkable-integration#867, session 1014, parked as 938), while the same pane showed `205k/1m (20%)`
  later, which the default `context_pattern` reads. So the compaction never ran on the case it was built
  for, a fixer resumed from a park, and the once-per-PR warning hid the next misses. Now `fixStart` reads
  whether the fixer's session was up before `ensureAgent` (`sessionUp` on `LiveSessionByPRRole`, the test
  `ensureAgent` makes), and for a fixer it resumed from a park `fixCompact` reads the pane every 2 s until
  a figure shows, for up to a minute (`readContext`, `fixContextPoll` and `fixContextAwait`, sleeping
  through the engine's `Sleep`; at most 31 reads, so a clock that does not move still ends the wait). A
  figure within the wait goes on as before (under the key nothing; at or above it `/compact`, then the
  fresh session when needed); none warns `fix.context_unknown` once per PR as before, naming the wait
  ("… context_pattern reads within 60s of its resume, …"). A fixer that was live before the cycle is read
  once, as before, and a fixer started fresh is never read. Any figure read forgets the PR's warning (the
  kv `pr.<id>.fix_context_unknown` is deleted when set), so a later miss warns again. `Compact`,
  `ContextUsed`, the pattern, the status card's words and the events' names are unchanged. New tests
  TestTheContextFigureIsAwaitedAfterAResume (three blank reads 2 s apart on the fake clock, then 82%,
  compacted, no warning), TestNoFigureWithinTheWaitWarnsOnceAndKeepsTheSession (31 reads over a minute,
  one warning naming the wait, the session kept; cycle 3 reads 30% and forgets it, cycle 4 warns again)
  and TestALiveFixerIsReadOnce in engine; the spec 57 tests keep their read counts, since their fixers
  were live. Rejected: reading once right after the resume (what happened: the status line is not drawn
  yet); waiting for herdr's idle status alone (the status line can lag it); a fixed sleep after every
  resume (it costs its whole length when the line is already drawn, and is still too short when Claude
  Code is slow).

- **A reply "Follow-up in <sha>" is a fix, not a won't-fix** (2026-10-17, spec 60; amends "The reply classifier
  reads "added in", "removed in", "closed by … in" and "not adding it""). On talkable-proxies#250 the author
  answered a magnum thread (2026-10-14) with "Follow-up in 9aed21f: the `< 1.9` pin is gone … the probe from
  this comment prints `200`": a fix that names its commit, as "added in <sha>" does. `classifyReply` read
  "follow-up" in the first clause as the deferral it usually is, so the evidence table of the run classed it
  `won't fix` while the retro and a person read it as fixed; one case in 425 answered threads since 10-14,
  but the class reaches the judge's reply contract (a deferral is honoured without a re-check, a fix is
  verified) and the evidence tables. Now a clause "follow-up in <sha>", "follow-up <sha>", "follow up in
  <sha>" or "followed up in <sha>" (a commit of 7 to 40 hex characters, in backticks or not, as the older
  forms take it) is `fixed`: one more alternative of the `fixed` pattern, which `replyClasses` tries before
  `won't fix`, so the deferral pattern is unchanged and "followed up" gained a verdict only with a commit. A
  bare "follow-up" or "follow-up later", "follow-up PR", "follow-up ticket", "Deferred to a follow-up" and
  "follow-up in 12 places" stay `won't fix`, and "followed up in the next PR" stays `other`. The clause
  splitter ends "Follow-up in 9aed21f: the pin is gone" at the colon, after the commit, so the verdict
  clause is "Follow-up in 9aed21f". Precedence is unchanged (an acknowledgement passes the verdict on, the
  first clause that names a class wins: "Good catch, out of scope: follow-up in 9aed21f" stays `won't fix`).
  New test TestClassifyReplyReadsFollowUpInACommitAsFixed. Rejected: a letter and a digit in the commit (an
  all-digit abbreviated commit is a real one; the older entry rejected the same), and reading "follow-up
  commit <sha>" or "follow-up in commit <sha>" (no reply seen takes that form, and "added in commit <sha>" is
  no `fixed` form either).
- **An idle park whose agent did not quit goes hard on its next try, and one stuck agent no longer keeps the
  others live** (2026-10-17, spec 64, amends "A park that fails backs off, and its cause is recorded once"
  and "A fresh start heals an agent that will not quit"). The idle park (`parkJob`) called `Agents.Park`
  and, when it failed, recorded `pr.park_failed` and backed off up to 12 hours; it never tried the hard
  park. Since 2026-10-14 there were 21 `pr.park_failed` events, all on talkable#11932 ("quit_timeout: an
  agent did not quit: its pane was no idle shell after ctrl+c"): session 535 twelve times, 792 three, 882
  six, still failing on 10-17 with a foreground Claude in its pane. The agent counted as idle, ctrl+c did
  not end it, and the plain park was retried for days while the session kept its pane. Now `parkJob` reads
  the class of the PR's last failure from the backoff record (`parkFails[pr].cause`, the one `parkFailed`
  keeps; `parkQuitFailed`), and after `quit_timeout` the try uses `Agents.ParkHard`, as a fresh start's park
  does after one such try (`freshParkHardAfter`) and `parkForStop` on its last. So the second try after a
  quit timeout, once its backoff has passed, is hard. A hard park that works records `pr.parked` with
  "(hard: an agent did not quit at the plain park)" appended (the stuck agent's session is closed, not
  parked, so the next round starts that role fresh) and forgets the failures as any park that
  works (`parkWorked`), so the next failure is a plain try again; one that fails records `pr.park_failed`
  as before (the cause is recorded once, the wait doubles) and is tried hard again while the class stays
  `quit_timeout`. A failure of another class (an agent or a run at work, herdr, an error) keeps the plain
  park, a hard try that fails for another class hands the next one back to it, and `ParkHard` refuses
  everything `Park` refuses (a run in flight, an agent working or blocked), so a working agent is never
  forced. The record lives in the daemon's memory (as the backoff does), so a restart forgets the class:
  the first try after it is plain, and on the second a stuck agent is parked hard (15 of the 21 failures
  came right after a restart). The Codex-flag release, `parkFresh` and `parkForStop` are unchanged; the
  flag release and the idle park share the record, so a quit timeout of the release makes the idle park's
  next try hard too. `agents.Manager.Park` (and so `ParkHard`) no longer stops at the first agent whose quit
  fails: it goes on to the PR's other live agents of the workspace it keeps, which are parked as usual, and
  returns the failures joined (`errors.Join`, so `ErrBusy` and herdr's timeout stay in the chain and the
  class is the same), the stuck agent's session staying live for the next try; a stopped daemon's context
  ends it at once. Before, one pane that ignored ctrl+c left the PR's claude-review, codex-review,
  claude-fix and codex-judge sessions live and idle since 10-16 21:04. New tests
  TestAnIdleParkGoesHardAfterAQuitTimeout (the second try is hard, `pr.parked` names it, the record is
  forgotten and the next failure is plain), TestAnIdleParkStaysPlainAfterAnotherFailure (busy, another
  error, and a hard try that fails busy) and TestAFailedHardIdleParkBacksOffAsAnyFailureDoes in engine, and
  TestAParkThatCannotQuitOneAgentStillParksTheOthers in agents. The three backoff tests that need the failures
  to go on after the first (`TestAFailedParkBacksOff`, `TestAFailedParkRecordsOneEventPerCause`,
  `TestAParkThatSucceedsAfterFailuresClearsTheBackoff`) fail the hard park too (`failEveryPark`) and count
  plain and hard tries (`parkTries`). Rejected: going hard at the first failure (ctrl+c is cheaper and quits
  most agents, and a hard park closes the pane and the conversation with it); never going hard (what
  happened: one session failed twelve times over days); keeping the failure class in the registry for the
  restart case (one more plain try and event per restart, the cost the backoff entry already accepted);
  making the Codex-flag release hard too (the spec names the idle park, and a flagged PR's release is
  tried again on every backoff the same way, so it can follow later).
- **A failed command's log line carries the first line of its stderr** (2026-10-17, spec 67, amends
  "Subprocess transcripts log at debug, failures at warn"). The line of a failed command read
  `exec <cmd> dir=… code=1 dur=… err=exit status 1` and nothing more. Since 2026-10-14 the daemon log held
  112 such warnings for `gh api graphql`, 84 of them at about 11 s, and only 16 surfaced as `poll.error` or
  `poll.ci_error`: the other 96 could not be told apart (a 502, a rate limit, a bad query) or attributed to a
  caller. Now the line of a command that failed (an error, or a code other than 0, at any level, so a probe's
  answer at debug has it too) ends with ` stderr=<line>`: the first line of stderr that is not blank, a
  carriage return ending a line as a newline does, redacted, with control characters turned into spaces and
  invalid UTF-8 replaced, at most 200 runes (a longer line is its first 199 and an ellipsis). A command that
  succeeds or leaves stderr empty or blank gets no such part. Only that one line is redacted and cut, not the
  stream (up to 8 MiB): a token or a key block that starts in it is masked to its end, and the lines after it
  are not shown. Real.Run captures stderr on this path (`Result.Stderr`, which `exitError` already reads), so
  nothing is read again. `Cmd` has no flag that marks a command's output as PR-controlled or sensitive, so
  none is honoured: the checkout's hooks, tests and the agents' commands take the same path, bounded and
  redacted. A command whose first stderr line is PR text (a test's failure message) therefore logs up to 200
  runes of it; the spec accepts that bound. New test TestAFailedCommandLogsItsFirstStderrLine. Rejected:
  logging the whole stderr (up to 8 MiB per failure, and PR output among it; `ExitError.Stderr` already
  carries 64 KiB for the callers that need more); logging the last line instead (gh prints its API error
  message first and usage text after it); an `err=` that wraps the `ExitError` (the line would then carry
  up to 64 KiB).

- **A drain or a pause stop of the skill gate does not count toward its hold limit** (2026-10-17, spec 61,
  amends "A gating proposal always ends"). The gate counted every stop short of a verdict and held the
  proposal for the operator at `gateAttemptLimit` (6), and a drain for a restart stops the gate before its
  next replay like any other stop: skill proposal 2 on 2026-10-14 had six `learn.gate_waiting` events
  (15:34 an error, 16:31 a drain, 17:09 an error, 18:42, 19:13 and 20:11 drains) and `learn.held` at 20:11,
  "6 gates in a row stopped short without a verdict, the last: draining for a restart", four of the six
  being the operator's own restarts (the improve loop lands several commits a day); it sat held 12.7 h and
  was rejected stale, and proposal 5 on 10-17 took a drain stop (09:30) the same way. A drain says nothing
  about the proposal. Now a replay the daemon's own hold stops (`gateHold`: a drain or stop, an
  infrastructure pause, `magnum pause`, a paused reviewing CLI, checked before each replay) comes back with
  `gateReplay.held`, a typed flag set where the check is made and not read from the stop's words, and `halt`
  ends such a gate through `waitsHeld`: the `learn.gate_waiting` event and the retry wait are as before, but
  `countGateAttempt` is not called, so the stop neither counts nor resets the count of the earlier ones
  (`learn.gate_stops`' `attempts` and its last reason stay as the last counted stop left them), and the held
  message of a real stop is unchanged. A budget stop, a usage limit, a login, a replay without a score and
  an error still count, and `gateMaxAge` (3 days) still bounds a proposal that a restart-heavy week keeps
  from a verdict. New test TestADrainStopNeverCountsTowardTheGateHold in engine (six drain stops between
  five error stops leave the proposal gating with eleven `learn.gate_waiting` events and no
  `learn.held`; the sixth error stop holds it, naming the budget); TestAGateThatKeepsStoppingIsHeldForTheOperator
  stays as it was. Rejected: resetting the count on a drain (an error streak a drain interrupts would never
  reach the limit, and the daily restarts would keep a gate that never fits under the budget alive for
  the whole `gateMaxAge`), and reading the stop's English for "draining" (the words are the check's, not
  a contract).
- **The skill editor's format gate names the failing test, not only the end of its output** (2026-10-17,
  spec 65). `formatGateProblems` handed the editor's nudge the last 40 lines of a failing command's
  output, and a failing prompt or format test prints a whole rendered prompt after its `--- FAIL:` line,
  so the 40 lines held the end of a prompt and no test name: learn proposal 3 (2026-10-15 12:08) ended
  `invalid`, "still invalid after a nudge (1 problem)", with a stored reason that began with "..." and
  the tail of a rendered claude-review prompt, and one of the week's five proposals was lost for it.
  `gateOutput` (internal/engine/learn_edit.go) now keeps, within the same `editGateLines` (40): every
  `--- FAIL:` line of the output (a subtest's too), the first `editGateMessages` (3) lines of the
  `x_test.go:12:` form that follow each (the test's own messages, as `go test` prints them indented
  after the FAIL line, up to the next line that is not indented or the next FAIL line), each clipped to
  `editGateLineRunes` (300) since a message can hold a whole prompt on one line, then as much of the end
  of the output as the budget leaves, apart from the lines already kept, behind a `...` line. Whole
  failures are kept in order as far as they fit, and the count of the rest is a line, "… and N more
  failures". An output within the budget is handed over whole, as before, and one with no failing test
  (a build error) is its end, as before; the stored reason, which clips the problems to their first
  2000 runes, now starts with the failing test. New tests
  TestTheFormatGateNamesTheFailingTestWhenItsOutputIsLong, TestAShortFailingGateOutputIsHandedOverWhole
  and TestGateOutputKeepsEveryFailureThenTheTail. Rejected: a larger line budget (the rendered prompt is
  longer than any budget, and the nudge and the stored reason would grow with it).
- **An eval run's inputs cover the stakes lines** (2026-10-17, spec 72, amends "An eval run records its
  inputs, the notes each judge read and the Codex points each case used" and "The operator tells the judge
  what a repository puts at risk"). The judge and the reviewers read the repository's stakes line
  (`Config.StakesFor`, in `judge.go` and `reviewers.go`), but `evalrun.Inputs` hashed only the roles, their
  kinds, the prompts and the judge skill, and `eval.Baselines`, `eval.JudgeBaselines` and
  `eval.FullReplayFor` reuse a stored replay whose `inputs` or `reviewer_inputs` match: after a stakes edit a
  gate would have compared a candidate that read the new line with a baseline that read the old one and
  credited the difference to the skill proposal. No harm yet (proposal 5's baseline postdates the lines).
  Now `inputsOf` ends with every set stakes line of the config's `[[watch]]` blocks (by owner) and
  `[[repo]]` blocks (by `owner/name`), each with its block's kind and lower-cased name and sorted by that
  key, so the order in the file is not an input; it is written after the roles whatever role filter the
  hash takes, so both `inputs` and `reviewer_inputs` change with a stakes edit (the reviewers read the line
  too, and a judge-only replay takes a full replay's reports only when its reviewers read what its own
  would). Only lines that are set count, which is all `StakesFor` reads: a config with no stakes line hashes
  as it did before, and adding a block without one replays nothing. The operator's config sets them, so the
  first baseline after the daemon restarts on this build is replayed once, which is what the spec asks for.
  The hash is the run's, not a case's: an edit to one repository's line replays the baselines of every
  case, and a line moved from a watch to a repository of it is another input although `StakesFor` gives the
  same text; a watch's `include` and `exclude`, which decide which repositories a watch's line reaches, are
  not hashed. `ReviewedOtherwise`'s words for a reviewer-inputs mismatch now say "other prompts or stakes
  lines, or ran with another role config". New tests TestAStakesChangeChangesTheInputs and
  TestTheStakesLinesCountInTheOrderOfTheirKeys (evalrun). Rejected: hashing the effective `StakesFor` of
  each case's repository (the hash is made from the config alone, once per run, before any case); hashing
  every block's line even when empty (a watch added without stakes would replay every baseline); hashing the
  rendered prompts (they need a case).
- **An `app/<name>` entry in a login list is refused** (2026-10-17, spec 72, amends "A listed bot's PR is
  reviewed although bots are skipped"). `allow_bot_authors`, `skip_authors` and `auto_approve_skip_authors`
  match logins with `github.SameLogin`, which trims only a trailing "[bot]", so an entry written as GitHub's
  URLs write an App, `app/helper`, matched no author: the list did nothing and said nothing. `validateLogins`
  (the two lists that already refused an empty or spaced entry) and the new `validateNoAppForm` (called for
  `skip_authors` of a `[[watch]]` alone, which no check covered) now refuse an entry with a "/" in it, in the
  loader as the other login refusals are made, naming the block and the entry as written: `watch acme:
  allow_bot_authors entry "app/helper" must be a GitHub login: write helper or helper[bot], not app/helper`
  (the login is what follows the last "/"; an entry with nothing after it, such as `app/`, is told to have no
  "/"). `skip_authors` is refused for the "/" only: the eligibility check has always trimmed an entry's
  padding and skipped a blank one, so a config with ` dependabot ` or `""` there keeps loading. A config that
  carries such an entry stops loading until it is written `helper` or `helper[bot]`. New test
  TestAnAppPrefixedLoginIsRefused (config). Rejected: reading `app/helper` as `helper[bot]` (a second spelling
  for every list, and the README and the lists' comments say GitHub logins); running all of `validateLogins`
  on `skip_authors` (a new refusal of blank and padded entries the check never minded).
- **The texts on a pooled repository's `[[repo]]` keys and `magnum eval`'s usage line are pinned to the
  code** (2026-10-17, spec 74). `Repo.worktreeKeys` bans six keys for a repository with a `[[pool]]`
  (setup, teardown, wt_hooks, copy_files, strip_env and env) and lets the other eleven stand, but the
  error that refuses them named eight of the eleven (not auto_approve_skip_authors, allow_bot_authors
  and trackers), the comment of `config.defaults.toml` nine (not required_checks and trackers) and
  that of `config.full.example.toml` six (not stakes, auto_approve_skip_authors, allow_bot_authors,
  required_checks and trackers). All three now name the eleven. New test
  TestTheTextsOnAPooledReposKeysNameEveryKeyTheCodeAllows (internal/config/docs_drift_test.go) sets
  each `Repo` key alone on an empty block and asks `worktreeKeys`, so the allowed and the banned lists
  come from the code and a key added to `Repo` moves them; it checks that the error's "only … apply to
  it" list and its "( … configure per-PR worktrees" list are exactly those two, and that the sentence
  "Its no_findings_event … [[pool]] repo too." of both example files names every allowed key and no
  banned one. `evalUsage` (`run|score|list|show`) likewise left out `baseline`; it is now
  `run|score|list|show|baseline`, and TestEvalUsageNamesEveryRegisteredSubcommand compares it with the
  subcommands `newEvalCmd` registers. Rejected: a list of the allowed keys in config.go for the error
  to print (a third copy beside `worktreeKeys`, which the test would still have to check against the
  comments) and a list kept in the test (it would drift as the texts did).
- **A cut settles its turns side by side, and a reviewer still at work is told to stop its background tasks
  after a 10-second grace** (2026-10-17, spec 66, amends "A cut interrupts every turn before it waits for
  any", "A cut shell command is pressed until it stops" and "A reviewer a push or the round's end cuts short
  is told to stop its background tasks"). `cut` settled its turns one after another, and each claude reviewer
  waited the whole `InterruptWait` (60 s) for its agent to go idle before it was told to stop its background
  work: since 2026-10-14T14:21Z 18 of the 24 `round.warning` events said a claude reviewer "still works 1m0s
  after it was interrupted" (11 at the 9 restarts on a moved head, 7 at round ends), and each then stopped its
  background tasks when asked; with two claude reviewers a restart waited two minutes before the new round
  started, four times. A claude reviewer whose background tasks run does not go idle at its interrupt; the
  stop message is what ends them. Now `cut` settles every interrupted turn on a goroutine of its own
  (`settleSafely`, which turns a panic into a warning) and, once all are settled, records what each said and
  ends the runs in the turns' order, shell roles first, as before, so the messages and the result's warnings
  read as they did and a cut takes as long as its longest settle. Each turn's waits count from its own
  interrupt (`waitIdle` takes a deadline), so the waits of one settle on a shared clock never stretch
  another's. `settle` waits `cutGrace` (10 s, a constant beside `InterruptWait`) for an agent to be seen idle;
  one still at work then whose transcript shows background work still running is told then (`askStop`, with
  the same words as before: `headMovedStopText` on a push, `stopBackgroundText` at the round's end), the wait
  for idle goes on to `InterruptWait` after the interrupt, and what is left is read after it, up to
  `StopGrace` (`backgroundStopped`). An agent idle within the grace gets no message then; work its transcript
  still shows once it is idle is stopped as before. A `round.warning` is recorded when the agent still works
  `InterruptWait` after its interrupt, as before, and when work it was told to stop still runs or it could not
  be told; a stop that worked is now the info event `round.cut_settled` ("claude-review settled 10s after it
  was interrupted for the restart; asked it to stop the 2 background tasks it started: it did", data `run`,
  `role` and `seconds`, from the interrupt to idle) where it was a warning. Codex reviewers (whose background
  work `BackgroundTasks` cannot read) and shell roles are never messaged, as before; a shell role's presses
  are unchanged, and they now run beside the agents' waits instead of before them. New tests
  TestCutSettlesItsTurnsInParallel, TestACutReviewerWithBackgroundTasksIsToldToStopAfterAGrace,
  TestACutReviewerIdleWithinTheGraceIsNotMessaged and TestACutSettleThatPanicsOnlyWarns;
  TestACutShellCommandIsPressedUntilItStops now checks that the presses do not wait for claude-review's
  settle, and TestAPushTellsACutReviewerToStopItsBackgroundTasks reads the info event. Rejected: a shorter
  `InterruptWait` (a reviewer finishing a tool call needs it); messaging at once (an agent that is going idle
  anyway would get a useless prompt).
- **`magnum doctor` and the daemon say when herdr's Codex session hook is off** (2026-10-17, spec 68).
  herdr learns a Codex session's id from the SessionStart hook it installs in `$CODEX_HOME/hooks.json`
  (`bash ~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh session`), and Codex keeps each hook's trust in `config.toml`'s
  `[hooks.state]` (`"<hooks.json path>:session_start:<group>:<index>"`, with `trusted_hash` and
  `enabled`). On 2026-10-16 the operator answered a hooks dialog, the entry of herdr's hook became
  `enabled = false`, and since 11:36Z 33 of 34 codex-judge sessions had no session id (the one was a
  resume of an older parked session; before, 45 of 59 had one). Without an id `resumable` never resumes a
  judge (29 sessions ended `closed`, never `parked`), `TurnError` cannot read the rollout (107 WARN lines
  "no Codex rollout to read the turn's error from: session id \"\" is no file name"), and
  `helperRefusal`, the only check for a Codex helper's cybersecurity refusal, is blind; nothing in magnum
  said so. Now `magnum doctor` has a `codex session hook` check when the codex kind's `session_source` is
  `herdr` and a session role starts it (a shell role's `codex review` needs no id), one line per Codex
  home those roles read (`agents.Manager.CodexHome`, `codexHomeFor` of the role's env, as every reader of
  a Codex home): `agents.ReadCodexSessionHook` reads hooks.json and `[hooks.state]`, and the check warns
  when no SessionStart hook names `herdr-agent-state.sh` ("missing", fix: reinstall herdr's Codex
  integration) and when every such hook's entry has `enabled = false`, naming the entry and what goes
  blind ("no session id: judges are never resumed, and a helper's Codex refusal is not seen", fix: set
  `enabled = true` in that entry). A hook with `enabled = true` or no entry passes; a home without
  hooks.json is skipped (herdr not installed is the herdr check's), and a missing `config.toml` or
  `[hooks.state]` disables nothing. It only reads. The observer records `agents.session_id_missing`
  (warn, subject `tool:<kind>`) once per kind and Manager, a daemon start, when a session of a kind whose
  `session_source` is `herdr` ends a turn magnum prompted (stored status working, set no earlier than its
  `last_prompt_at`, then idle or done) while neither the row nor herdr has a session id; for codex the
  message says what the Codex home shows of the hook (missing, or the disabled entry by its
  `session_start:<group>:<index>` without the path, since CODEX_HOME may be a pane env value) and what
  goes blind; `magnum status` is unchanged. The rollout warning of `TurnError` is logged once per session
  (the new `rolloutWarned`, kept as `compacting` is), not at every turn. New tests
  TestDoctorWarnsWhenHerdrsCodexSessionHookIsDisabled in cli, TestACodexAgentWithoutASessionIDWarnsOncePerStart
  and TestTheRolloutWarningIsSaidOncePerSession in agents. Rejected: magnum turning the hook back on
  itself (Codex's hooks state is the operator's trust decision, as magnum answers hooks dialogs only
  under `on_hooks_review`); reading the rollout by `session_meta` without an id (more work, and not
  needed once the hook is on); warning at the run's completion (the pipeline settles a judge's run from
  its result file before the observer sees it idle, so the judge, the case at hand, would never warn);
  warning at any working-to-idle change (a session's startup output can read as working before its first
  prompt, when no id exists yet).
- **A lost agent's pane error line is kept before its pane closes** (2026-10-17, spec 69, amends "A parked
  session's pane is closed at every park and at the restart"). The `agent.lost` event carries no cause, so
  the line the CLI printed before it died (a Codex flag it rejects, a model it refuses) went with the pane
  once spec 58 closed a lost session's pane; before that the pane stayed until the next start reused it and
  the operator could read it. There were 17 losses on 2026-10-12 and 7 on 2026-10-16, the outage of codex
  0.163.0, whose cause took 79 minutes to find. Now `CloseRetiredPanesIn` reads the pane with `paneError`
  (what `clearDeadLaunch` already does before its own close) for each pane whose newest retired session is
  lost, after the idle-shell check and before the close (a pane left alone is not read; a parked or closed
  session's pane is not read either, since nothing failed there), and `pr.panes_closed` gains `last_lines`,
  a map from the role to the line, of the closed panes that showed one (the newer session's when two closed
  panes of a role do); the message gains "(<role>: <line>)" for each role, in role order. `paneError` is
  unchanged, so the line is what it keeps: a line that starts at column 0 with error, fatal or panic,
  redacted and cut to 200 runes, never an indented or boxed line a tool printed, which the PR's code can
  steer; a pane that shows none adds nothing, and the event keeps its old shape. The close and the engine
  (`closePanesJob`, the reconcile) are otherwise unchanged. New test
  TestALostPanesErrorLineIsKeptBeforeItCloses (agents). Rejected: keeping a lost pane open until the
  operator reads it (what spec 58 stopped: 21 panes on one PR).
- **A fixer whose pane never shows a figure is waited for once per PR, not on every resumed cycle**
  (2026-10-17, spec 71, amends "The fixer's context figure is awaited after a resume"). Spec 59 made
  `readContext` read a resumed fixer's pane every 2 s for up to a minute until a context figure shows. A
  pane whose status line never matches `[kinds.claude] context_pattern` (a status line without the
  percent; a stock Claude Code status line shows a figure only near full) never shows one, so every
  resumed cycle of such a PR would wait the whole minute before its prompt, and `fix.context_unknown`
  speaks once per PR, so the later stalls would be silent. Now `readContext` (internal/engine/fix_compact.go)
  reads the PR's kv `pr.<id>.fix_context_unknown` first: while it is set (the minute was waited once and no
  figure came) a fixer resumed from a park is read once, with no sleep and no second warning, as a fixer
  that was live is; the first miss still waits the minute and sets the kv through `warnContextUnknown`,
  and a figure read at any cycle deletes it as before, so the next miss waits the minute again and warns
  again. The warning's text, `Compact`, `ContextUsed`, the pattern and the events' names are unchanged.
  The kv is also set by a miss after a `/compact` (a figure was read before it), so the cycle after that
  one reads a resumed fixer once too: a late status line there costs one skipped check, not a fresh
  fixer. The existing TestNoFigureWithinTheWaitWarnsOnceAndKeepsTheSession needs no change: its cycles 3
  and 4 run on a live fixer, which was read once already. New test
  TestASecondResumeWithoutAFigureDoesNotWait in engine (cycle 2 waits 31 reads and warns; cycle 3, resumed
  from a park again with no figure, adds one read and no warning; a figure at cycle 4 clears the kv;
  cycle 5 without one waits the minute and warns again). Rejected: waiting the minute on every resumed
  cycle (what spec 59 left for such a PR); a flag a figure cannot clear (a pane that starts to show a
  figure, after the pattern was fixed, would never be awaited again); a shorter wait on later resumes
  (the same cost, smaller).
- **`magnum retro`, `magnum notes --curate` and `magnum fix` are held through a drain instead of refused**
  (2026-10-17, spec 63; amends "`magnum retro` queues behind a running learn job"). Since 2026-10-14T14:21Z,
  14 of the 18 failed operator requests were refusals during a drain for a restart: 11 retros ("no retro
  now: draining for a restart", the improve loop asking every 90 s on 10-14 14:40-14:55), 2 fixes ("the
  daemon is draining; try after the restart": talkable#11932 on 10-14, whose next fix came two days later,
  and talkable#11483 on 10-16, next four hours later) and 1 curation. A `magnum review` during a drain was
  already queued, and a queued retro already survived one. The earlier entry's line "a queue cannot wait
  them out" no longer holds for a drain: it ends with the restart, and the improve loop restarts the daemon
  several times a day. Now `refusingHold` is `holdReason` less the drain (a stop or an infrastructure
  pause, which still refuse with their words, as does a pause of the agent's CLI), and under a drain:
  `magnum retro` is queued as behind a learn job (`queueRetro`, kv `learn.retro_queued`, "queued: starts
  after the restart (the daemon is draining)"; a second request says one is queued already and when it
  starts), and `startQueuedRetro` starts it once nothing holds it, after the restart or once the drain is
  lifted; a curation request is queued (`queueCurate`, kv `notes.curate_queue`, the new why `drain`,
  "starts after the restart", which `magnum notes` lists as "waits for the restart after the drain") after
  the supersede of a stale proposal it names, which still happens at once, so the queued curation starts
  from the notes now and reads it; and `magnum fix` runs every refusal of `prepareFix` (the drain's moved
  to `startFix`), so a request refused after the restart is refused now, and is otherwise held
  in a row of its own, kv `pr.<id>.fix_held` (when it was asked, the PR's head then, who asked), answered
  "held; the fix of <pr> starts after the restart if the review on <sha> still stands (the daemon is
  draining)", with a `fix.held` event. The restart (`startHeldFixes`, right after `recoverFixes`) and a
  drain lifted without one (`continueDrainHeldLoops`, through `drainHeld` as for the loops a drain held)
  start cycle 1 through `startFix` as the request would have (by `magnum fix`, so a pinned PR is unpinned)
  while the PR sits at the head it was asked on and `prepareFix` passes; otherwise the request is dropped
  with `fix.dropped` at warn naming why (the head moved, the PR closed, nothing left to fix) and an info
  toast. `magnum abort` and the other stops of the PR (`endFixLoop`) take a held fix back, and `magnum fix
  --wait` on one says there is nothing to follow before the restart instead of reading the missing loop as
  one gone without an end. A dry run under a drain says it would hold the fix. No migration and no new PR
  phase. New tests TestARetroAskedDuringADrainStartsAfterTheRestart (restart and lifted drain),
  TestRetroRequestRefusedUnderAnInfraPauseOrAStop (formerly ...WhileDrainingOrRunning),
  TestACurationAskedDuringADrainStartsAfterTheRestart (the supersede case under a second drain, lifted),
  TestACurationRequestIsRefusedUnderAnInfraPauseOrAStop,
  TestAFixAskedDuringADrainStartsAfterTheRestartWhenTheReviewStands (restart and lifted drain),
  TestAFixAskedDuringADrainIsDroppedWhenTheHeadMoved and TestAbortDropsAFixHeldForTheRestart in engine,
  TestFixWaitOnAFixHeldForTheRestartDoesNotFollow and
  TestNotesListSaysACurationQueuedDuringADrainWaitsForTheRestart in cli; TestAQueuedRetroWaitsOutADrain
  and TestADrainStartsNoFixCycle now expect the queue's answer and the running loop's refusal. Rejected:
  refusing and asking the operator to retry (what happened: 14 refusals, two fixes delayed by days); a
  loop row at cycle 0 marked held for the fix (every reader of `pr.<id>.fix` would have to tell it from a
  running loop: `magnum review`'s refusal, a second loop's, autofix, the board, `--wait`, the restart's
  recovery); and queueing the fix as a request left pending until the restart (the CLI's wait would time
  out, and the request would outlive its answer).
- **The daemon records each agent CLI's version and names a launch failure shared across PRs** (2026-10-17,
  spec 75). On 2026-10-16 mise's `codex = "latest"` installed codex-cli 0.163.0 at 11:24, which died at its
  TUI bootstrap ("account/read failed during TUI bootstrap") in every judge pane: four PRs parked, 6 forced
  reviews in 36 minutes, 9 round.judge_restarted, 7 agent.lost, and 79 minutes until the operator found the
  new version and pinned 0.162.1. Each PR's attention line named its own failure, and only `magnum doctor`
  printed CLI versions. Now the daemon reads the version of every agent kind its roles use (a shell role's
  tool and the judge in reserve count, as in doctor) at its start and at every tick's health check, through
  `Deps.LookPath` (exec.LookPath on the daemon's PATH; nil in tests and dry runs) and the runner, as doctor
  reads it (`<kind> --version`, its first line): kv `kind.<name>.version` (`KindVersion`: version, the
  binary's resolved path and mtime, when it was read, the version before the last change and when it
  changed). The command runs again only once the binary's path or mtime differs from the recorded one (or
  the one this run failed to read, which is tried again when it changes or at the next start). The
  daemon's PATH finds codex as mise's shim, a link to mise itself whose file never changes when mise
  installs another version, so a command that resolves to a file named mise is stamped by the binary
  `mise which <kind>` names, which runs at every check (the version is still read through the shim). A first reading is only
