- **A notes apply settles its claim by what the disk holds, and a critic rejection promises no curation that cannot
  run** (2026-10-23, spec 01 of the 2026-10-23T16-45 run, amends "A notes proposal is applied by a claim, a write and a
  record" and "The notes critic decides curation proposals"). The run's code-health lens proved three faults with
  throwaway tests over commits 94f2ea02..65ad2781.
  - Evidence. (1) `notes.WriteState` ended with `return os.RemoveAll(old)`, after the harness swap and the notes
    write had both succeeded, and `ApplyNotesProposal` took every `WriteState` error for "nothing was written": it
    released the claim and wrote `notes.apply_failed`. With the old script directory unremovable (mode 0500) the
    registry said `pending`, the disk held the proposal's target, and an `.old-*` directory stayed. Two more error
    paths of `WriteState` (a restore that fails, a new harness that cannot be moved aside) leave a mixed or missing
    harness, and the released claim hid it from `RecoverNotesApply`, which settles exactly those states but only
    for proposals still `applying`. (2) A critic rejection or re-curation set `KVNotesRecurate` and the toast said
    "A new curation runs.", but `maybeCurate` returns before `dueCurations` when `[notes] curate` is empty, so no
    curation ran and the mark stayed until an asked-for curation stored a proposal. (3) `syncNotes` runs at every
    reconcile without the notes lock. Since the claim-write-record apply it has a second writer: a read between the
    harness swap and the notes write recorded a mixed state as an import version, and a read before `finishApply`
    made `applied_version_id` point at an import, because `Dedupe` finds the latest version. Nothing swept the
    `.old-*` and `.new-*` directories a write leaves.
  - The write. `WriteStateReport` returns nil once the swap and the notes write are done and names an old harness
    it could not remove as a `Leftover` (`WriteState` keeps its signature and drops it); the apply writes
    `notes.write_leftover` (warn) and goes on. Tests replace the write through `writeNotesState`.
  - One rule for a claim's notes. `whatTheNotesHold(live, prior, target)` says whether the files hold the target,
    the state the claim found, half of each (the notes of one and the harness of the other) or neither, the target
    first. `RecoverNotesApply` decides by it (finish, release, complete the write, import what is there) and so does
    an apply whose write failed (`settleFailedWrite`): it reads the notes again; as found, it releases the claim
    (`notes.apply_failed`); as meant to be written, it records the proposal applied (`notes.write_error` names the
    error); in any other state, or notes it cannot read, the proposal stays `applying` with its claim
    (`notes.apply_unsettled`) and the next scan's recovery settles it. The apply does not run the recovery itself:
    the notes lock is not reentrant, and the scan comes within the daemon's `curateCheckEvery`.
  - The sweep. At every reconcile and at the start (`syncNotes`), for each repository with notes,
    `sweepNotesLeftovers` removes the directories named as `WriteState` names them (the harness's name, `.old-` or
    `.new-` and eight characters of `rand.Text`'s alphabet, directories only) whose modification time is over an hour
    old (`notes.Leftovers`, `notes.SweepLeftovers`). It takes the notes lock without waiting, since a write holds it
    for as long as it needs its old harness (a renamed directory keeps its old modification time, so the age alone
    protects nothing; the lock does), and leaves a repository with a proposal applying alone, since the recovery
    may still want what the write left. A held lock or an unremovable directory is tried again at the next reconcile.
  - The reconcile and an apply. `syncNotes` skips a repository with a proposal `applying` (one query on the
    proposals, after the notes are read: an apply claims before it writes, so a read that saw a write in flight
    finds the claim), also at the start, where the recovery runs first. A `pending` proposal writes nothing, so it
    does not skip: that would stop the import of hand edits and the measuring of limits for the proposal's seven days
    (the spec's "waiting or applying" is read as the second).
  - The critic. After a rejection or a re-curation, and unless the critic stepped back, the mark is set only when
    `curationRuns` (a curator is set up and `[notes] curate` is not empty; `maybeCurate` uses the same function).
    Otherwise no mark is set and the event and the toast end "No curation starts by itself: `magnum notes <repo>
    --curate` asks for a new one." The critic's stop paths are tested: an error from the agent, a context the
    shutdown ends, a usage limit that pauses the kind, an agent that cannot start and inputs that cannot be built
    each end the critique `stopped` with no attempt, the agent closed, and a new critique only after an hour (and
    after the pause).
  - Tests, failing first (a mutation of each rule fails one): in notes TestAnOldHarnessThatCannotBeRemovedIsNotAFailedWrite,
    TestWriteStateReportNamesTheLeftoverAndOnlyThat, TestSweepLeftoversRemovesOnlyOldWriteDirectories and
    TestSweepLeftoversOfARepositoryWithNoDirectoryIsEmpty; in engine TestAnApplyWhoseOldHarnessCannotBeRemovedIsApplied
    (mode 0500, applied, version recorded, one leftover event, no apply_failed),
    TestAnApplyThatFailsBeforeAnyWriteReleasesTheClaim,
    TestAnApplyThatFailsBetweenItsTwoWritesStaysApplyingAndTheRecoverySettlesIt,
    TestAnApplyWhoseWriteErroredAfterTheTargetWasInPlaceIsApplied,
    TestAnApplyThatFailsUnderNotesSomeoneChangedStaysApplyingForTheRecovery,
    TestWhatTheNotesHoldIsOneRuleForTheApplyAndTheRecovery,
    TestAReconcileDuringAHalfFinishedApplyRecordsNoImportVersion,
    TestAReconcileBetweenAnApplysWriteAndRecordLeavesTheCurationsVersion,
    TestTheReconcileSweepsTheDirectoriesAWriteLeftOnceTheyAreAnHourOld,
    TestTheSweepWaitsForTheNotesLockAndForAnUnsettledApply, TestACriticRejectionPromisesACurationOnlyWhereOneCanRun
    (reject and recurate, with curate set, off and no curator) and the stop paths TestACriticThatReturnsAnErrorStopsTheCritiqueAndIsTriedAgainAfterAnHour,
    TestACritiqueWhoseContextEndsIsStoppedByTheDaemonNotCounted, TestACritiqueThatHitsAUsageLimitPausesTheCriticsKind,
    TestACriticThatCannotStartStopsTheCritique and TestACritiqueWhoseInputsCannotBeBuiltStopsBeforeTheAgentIsAsked.
  - Rejected: releasing the claim on every error of the write (the old rule: it hid the states the recovery exists
    for, and released a claim over a write that stood); an apply that runs the recovery at once (the lock is not
    reentrant, and the next scan does it); the notes lock in `syncNotes` (a judge holds it while it edits the notes, which takes minutes, and
    the reconcile and the start's import must not wait for it; the claim says an apply is in flight); skipping `pending` proposals too (see
    above); sweeping by age alone, without the lock; removing a leftover that cannot be removed by changing its mode.
- **A change the base does not need is a finding** (2026-10-23, spec 05 of the 2026-10-23 run, item 1, approved
  by the operator that day). On talkable/wordpress#48 the PR rewrote the tools' event transport because GTM
  "ignores gtag("event")". Round 1's own pass took the PR's new checks failing on the base as proof, though they
  assert the new shape and fail on the base by construction; the judge's own probe then proved that the base's
  `gtag('event')` commands reach the GTM container with every parameter (`eventModel.*`, fresh per event).
  SKILL.md section 2 counted a false claim as a finding only "with impact", which the judge read as a runtime
  failure: it posted a `Description: ✗` body line, rejected claude-review's matching candidate as `speculative`
  ("no demonstrated runtime failure"), and the re-review said LGTM. The team closed the PR as not needed: a GTM
  trigger, the `eventModel.*` variables and one GA4 tag were enough. talkable#12050 closed the same way: site
  validations refuse the blank or non-positive rate the PR guards and production held none, while magnum's
  rounds had those facts, built the bad rows only through a raw writer and posted P3s. Of 312 review bodies since
  10-14, 49 carry a `Description: ✗` line, and one of them disproves the PR's stated reason; of the 7 reviewed PRs
  that closed unmerged, these two closed as not needed. After "a false claim is a finding unless you proved it has
  none." section 2 now says: "At `base_sha`, check the failure the PR says it fixes by its effect, not by the PR's
  new tests: when the base does not fail so, or code, configuration or a validation every writer passes already
  meets its goal (stored rows: give the query that counts them), the change is not needed: one finding naming what
  does it, P2 when merging leaves code or steps to maintain or hides an error the base reports, else P3; **Fix**:
  close the PR, or keep it with the true reason. This is the author's call." (494 bytes). P2 rather than always P3:
  section 6 honours every decline of a P3, so "the change itself stays" would still end in LGTM, while a P2's
  decline gets its reason checked at the base, and a product decision is still honoured. The next run counts the
  findings that say a change is not needed and their replies; the target for `Description: ✗` lines that dispute a
  stated reason is none. Test: TestSkillSaysWhenTheBaseDoesNotNeedTheChange. Rejected: merging section 2's claim
  list into one sentence to save 67 bytes (it moved four pins).

  TestAMergedPRsWithdrawalInDoubtDropsItsPendingRecord, TestAWithdrawalOutOfAttemptsLeavesNoPendingRecord,

  "green" from "never read", and the planned count of approvals posted while CI ran that then went red was skewed.
  A NULL rollup now answers `unknown` and still lets the approval through, as green does; a rollup that was read
  and is empty (no checks) stays `green`, and `required_checks` still decides by the stored checks when it can.
  Test: TestARollupNeverReadIsUnknownAndStillLetsTheApprovalThrough. Rejected: refusing on an unread rollup (the
  approval as the operator would stop waiting on a poll failure, which the poll's own warning reports).
- **Every round decides the dispatch gates of the judge's approval again** (2026-10-23, spec 07 of the 2026-10-23
  run, items 4 and 5; amends "The judge's own approval passes the approval's gates"). The dispatch gates (draft,
  muted, the watch's own filters, the files that change workflows, the agents' instructions or an unreadable file
  list) are functions of the registry, and the CI gate was already asked again at each prompt, so the record of the
  paused round's answer (`pr.<id>.no_approval_round`, set at a fresh round, kept by a continue, deleted at the
  round's end and at a failed setup) copied what a recomputation gives. It also hid a case: a continue that became
  a fresh round (its judge's session was gone) read the old key and wrote no `round.approval_refused`. The key,
  its three call sites and TestAContinueKeepsTheDispatchGatesAnswer are gone; `planApprovalGates` decides for every
  kind of round, and `round.approval_refused` is still written once per head and reason (the existing
  `pr.<id>.judge_approval_refused` mark), so a continue of the same head repeats nothing. Same registry, same
  answer (TestAPausedRoundsContinueKeepsItsRefusalWithoutARecord runs a real stop and continue); a PR that changed
  while its round was paused (it became a draft or muted) now gets the current answer, as any fresh round does
  (TestAContinueDecidesTheDispatchGatesAgain, TestAContinueThatBecameAFreshRoundSaysWhyItCannotApprove). A stale
  key of a round paused across the upgrade stays unread in the registry. `approval_hold` keeps its key: it counts

- **A stalled slot release is resumed by the reconcile** (2026-10-23, spec 07 of the 2026-10-23 run, item 6). A
  pool slot whose release stalled (an eviction whose fetch a restart cancelled, a GitHub outage) stayed
  `releasing` until every held slot of the pool was in use and a PR waited for a slot (`needSlot` resumed it only
  then, `store.EvictableSlots` lists held slots only). review15 stayed `releasing` from 10-22 11:18Z, and review18
  and review5 stalled at 09:58Z and 10:00Z of 10-23: 3 of 18 slots out of the pool while held slots existed. Each
  reconcile now queues the resumption of one: the slot in `releasing` or `dirty_schema` the longest, for over 30
  minutes (the slot's `updated_at`), whose PR is not closing (cleanup's), that this process does not release at
  that moment, none of whose release steps runs (the newest step event of `slot:<name>:release` is a begin nothing
  ended, written after this daemon started and under 2 hours ago: the longest step, the schema reload, takes 30
  minutes a try, twice), not tried in the last 30 minutes (so a release a guard keeps refusing is retried at
  most every half hour, not every 10 minutes), and only when the heavy worker has nothing else queued or running
  (`heavyIdle`: the reconcile is a heavy job itself). It queues `evictJob` under the existing key
  `evict:<repo>`, so a resumption already queued or running counts, and the job reserves the PR, parks its
  sessions and releases through the steps' own guards (Guard first, then the steps after the last completed one,
  all idempotent); `slot.release_resumed` says it. Stop condition of the spec, checked: can a resumption race a
  release's own step? The releases that run on the heavy worker (an eviction, the cleanup's, the Codex-flagged
  PR's) are serial with the reconcile that queues the resumption, and the resumption is queued only on an idle
  worker. The ones that do not (a stop's hand-back, a failed `magnum open`) run on a request's goroutine, between
  two steps of which no begin event is open, so they go through `releaseSlot`, which marks the slot as released by
  this process for the time it runs (`releasingNow`), and the resumption skips such a slot; a source-scan test
  keeps the engine's calls of the slot manager's `Release` in that one place. A release run by another process
  (the CLI) shows as an open begin event. What is left is the window between the check and the job, which the
  PR's reservation (`reserveEviction`, taken by the job before it touches the slot, refused while a round or
  other slot work holds the PR) closes as it does for an eviction. Tests: TestAReleaseStalledForOverHalfAnHourResumesOnTheNextReconcile,
  TestTheTicksReconcileResumesAStalledRelease, TestAReleaseWithAStepRunningIsNotResumed (a step begun a minute
  ago, ended, a dead daemon's, over two hours old, none), TestAReconcileResumesOneStalledReleaseTheOldestFirst,
  TestAStalledReleaseThatFailsAgainIsTriedEveryHalfHourAtMost, TestAStalledReleaseOfAClosingPRIsLeftToCleanup,
  TestAReleaseThisProcessRunsIsNotResumedBetweenItsSteps, TestEveryReleaseTheEngineStartsGoesThroughReleaseSlot.
  The cap (added the same day, at the operator's request): a resumption that fails again would be retried every
  half hour for good, each try a fetch or a schema reload on a machine under memory pressure. After
  `releaseResumeCap` (3) resumed releases of one slot in a row that ran and ended without the slot free, the
  reconcile stops resuming it: one `slot.release_given_up` warning and one toast, until the slot differs from what
  the last try left, by state or `updated_at` (the operator's repair or release, a `needSlot` resume: those are not
  counted). The slot's own failures move its `updated_at` too (a failed step leaves its error on the row), so the
  record keeps the state and `updated_at` as the last failed try left them and compares against those. The record
  is one registry key per slot, `slot.<id>.release_resumes` (JSON: when it was last tried, the failures, that
  snapshot, given up), not process memory: the daemon restarts every few hours (20 starts in 2.4 days) and each
  start reconciles at once, so a count in memory would give a slot three more tries per restart. It also holds the
  30-minute spacing between tries, which a refusal by the guard (it leaves the row alone) needs. The record goes
  when a try leaves the slot in another state than `releasing` or `dirty_schema` (free, or broken) and when another
  path changed the slot. Only a try that ran and failed counts: a resumption the PR's reservation turned into a
  no-op (nil), and a daemon stop, count nothing. The toast names `magnum release <slot>` to run once the cause is
  fixed (`release` takes a slot's name, and resumes a `releasing` or `dirty_schema` slot's release) and `magnum
  slots repair <slot>` for the case it breaks: `slots repair` takes a free, broken, provisioning or lost slot only,
  and refuses `releasing` and `dirty_schema` (ErrConflict), so it alone would send the operator to a command that
  fails. A reload that fails twice in a row already breaks the slot (`resetSchema`, then `slots repair` applies),
  so a persistently failing reload leaves this loop at its first resumption; the cap covers the other causes (a
  fetch, a guard that keeps refusing, the dependency steps, an unreachable GitHub). Tests:
  TestAStalledReleaseThatFailsThreeTimesInARowIsGivenUp (a failure that leaves its error on the row, a refusal that
  leaves the row alone), TestAGivenUpReleaseStaysGivenUpAcrossARestart,
  TestAGivenUpReleaseIsResumedAgainWhenTheSlotChangedByAnotherPath (its state; its updated_at),
  TestAResumeThatRanNoReleaseIsNotCounted, TestAReleaseThatEndsFreeStartsTheCountOver, and the key pinned in
  TestEveryKVKeyTheEngineWritesKeepsItsString.
  The next run counts slots `releasing` for over 30 minutes; the target is none. Rejected: resuming at every tick
  (a failing guard would write a warning per tick); resuming inline in the reconcile (it would hold the reconcile's
  other work behind a release that takes minutes); resuming only `releasing` (a restart that cuts the schema reload
  leaves `dirty_schema` the same way); the cap in process memory (above); naming `magnum slots repair` alone in
  the toast (above).

  comment first (the reviewed commit it applies to, or outside) and then looks near it, by the head of each

  **A rejected finding** (`builder.rejectedNear`; `raised = rejected`, and `duplicate` before the review, which is

  finding** (`builder.postedNear`) keeps the cross-head match, as the operator ruled: it stays open as a thread on

- **A skill proposal that master moved under expires by itself** (2026-10-23, spec 03 of the 2026-10-23 run).
  Three of the six skill proposals so far ended stale against master. Proposal 6 (candidate 0654ebc3 on base
  901b9651) had been `held` since 2026-10-20 13:20 UTC and no longer applied: `git apply --check` failed on
  `SKILL.md` and on all three judge prompts, a 3-way merge conflicted in three `SKILL.md` hunks, and the
  simplify clause it edits had moved into `prompts/judge-shared.md`. While it was held `magnum learn --propose`
  refused and the scheduled editor did not run (`editWait` waits while a proposal is gating, passed or held),
  although the retro had queued 25 new general inputs; the operator's two exits were `n` (an input is
  dismissed only on its second rejection) and the 7-day expiry. A proposal that can no longer land holds a
  decision for nobody, so `expireLearnProposals` (the loop's scan, every 10 minutes) now also tries every
  `held` and `passed` proposal that is not 7 days old against the checkout's master (`masterMoved`): the
  change its branch's tip makes from its parent is replayed onto master with the new
  `gitx.Client.ReplayConflicts`, which is `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only -z --no-messages
  --merge-base=<tip>^ <master> <tip>`, run in the proposal's own worktree (git 2.40 or later). It is the
  merge a rebase of that one commit does, which is how the landing replays it, but it writes objects only: no
  branch, index or work tree moves, in the worktree or in the operator's checkout. A conflict (exit 1) expires
  the proposal at once, by the same compare-and-set from `held` and `passed` as the week's expiry: the reason
  and the `learn.expired` event say "master moved: <files>" (at most six named, then "and N more"; the event
  data carries all in `moved`), the worktree and branch go (`dropCandidate`), and its inputs stay `new`
  (`DecideLearnProposal` moves none for this state, so nothing is dismissed). The scan runs `maybeEdit` right
  after the expiry, so the editor starts in that same scan when new evidence waits. A `gating` proposal stays
  with its gate; a branch master holds already is recorded as landed first (`landedAlready`), as at the week's
  expiry; a revert proposal expires like an edit (a revert whose files the operator edited since would undo
  that edit, and `magnum learn --revert` refuses to start one then). A check that cannot be made (git older
  than 2.40 or any other failure, logged once an hour; a branch or a worktree that is gone) tells nothing and
  leaves the proposal waiting, as before. No race with a landing: the scan, `maybeLearnLand` and the
  operator's land request (`requestLearnLand`, through `handleRequests`) all run one after the other on the
  tick's goroutine, and every decision is a compare-and-set, so an expiry never begins in the middle of a
  rebase or a fast-forward. Rejected: a real `git rebase` as the dry run (a clean one moves the branch and the
  worktree, so the check would put them back, and one cut short by a stop leaves a rebase in progress that the
  landing takes for a moved candidate); `git apply --check` (it needs master's tree, which only the operator's
  checkout has); checking in the checkout; expiring only `held` proposals; a toast for each expiry (the
  `learn.expired` event says it, and nobody had a decision to make); rejecting proposal 6 by hand (the
  operator's call: it expires at the first scan after the daemon restarts on this build). Tests, failing first:
  TestAProposalMasterMovedUnderExpiresAtTheScan (held and passed expire with the files named, a young one that
  applies and a gating one stay, each check runs in the proposal's own worktree against master, inputs stay
  `new`), TestAProposalMasterHoldsAlreadyIsLandedNotExpiredAsMoved, TestAProposalWhoseCheckCannotBeMadeStaysWaiting
  (git refuses, no branch, no worktree) and TestAHeldProposalMasterMovedUnderExpiresAndTheEditorStartsTheSameDay
  (a real repository and real `git merge-tree`: a commit elsewhere leaves it held, a commit on the lines it
  edits expires it and the editor starts in the same scan) in engine, with the existing week-long tests
  unchanged; TestReplayConflictsNamesWhereACommitNoLongerAppliesAndMovesNothing in gitx.

- **The reply classifier reads a repeated agent tag and bare declines** (2026-10-23, spec 03 of the 2026-10-23
  run). Of the 196 replies of the window, 12 were `other` where a person reads a fix or a decline. Three were
  "(Claude) (Claude) Added in <sha>" and "Applied in <sha>" on one PR: `classifyReply` stripped the agent tag
  once (two other fixes, phrased without a verdict word, stay). Seven were bare declines no pattern took: "Not
  changed here." four times on one PR, "but not changing it here", "No change." and "Still open, with no fix in
  this PR". Replayed over the 1,111 stored replies,
  the change moves 3 of the 123 `other` rows to `fixed` and 10 to `won't fix` and no row of another class. The
  tag is now stripped in a loop. "Not added", "Not changed" and "No change", each alone in its clause, join
  the `won't fix` verdict patterns; "not changed here" (also "not changing it here", after "I'm" or "we are"

  change needed in the helper." and a question ("Why is this not changed here?"); a fixed or not-a-bug clause

  TestClassifyReplyReadsADoubledAgentTagAndBareDeclines.

- **`magnum stats` counts the reviewed heads to a pass and the merges on magnum's approval alone** (2026-10-26,
  spec 02 of the 2026-10-26 run; amends "Finding provenance, then `magnum stats`"). Every improve run computed
  convergence again with its own definition and the answers disagreed: verdict `clean` at the first review gave
  41%, "no new or open P0-P2" 61%, distinct heads on merged colleague PRs 52.5%; and the share of merged
  auto-approved PRs whose only approval of a person was magnum's, in the operator's name, came out 14, 19, 20 or
  26 of 40 on one repository, as each analysis counted the operator's hand approvals and bots its own way. One
  definition now lives in code, read-only (no migration, no event, no gate; nothing changes in reviews).
  CONVERGENCE (`convergence` in `--json`, `stats_convergence.go`): the cohort is the PRs that merged or closed
  in the window (`merged_at`, else `closed_at`) with at least one posted review; the unit is a distinct reviewed
  head (`target_sha`) of the PR's posted judge reviews (outcome `posted`, a review id, the earliest run per
  review id: `store.ReviewedPRs`), in the order their runs were created, every review the PR ever had, less the
  runs created after it ended (a post-merge review); a second review of a head already counted (a reply round,
  a same-head re-review, a CI check) adds nothing, neither a head nor a pass. A review passes when it leaves no
  P0, P1 or P2 new or still open (`previous_findings.open`, by `store.ParseReviewResult`; an open P3 stays
  optional) and its verdict does not block; one whose result does not parse does not pass. Rows per repository
  and in total, others' PRs and the operator's own apart (`config.SelfMatch`, the logins `autofix = "own"`
  reads): PRS, PASS@1, PASS<=2, 5+ (passed at the fifth head or later, or five heads without passing), NEVER,
  the mean (two decimals) and nearest-rank p90 of the heads to pass of the PRs that passed, and MERGED OPEN
  (merged while the last review before the merge, a same-head one included, had a P0-P2 new or open). A line
  counts the open PRs that already have five reviewed heads. Two more split the window's posted P0-P2 findings
  of re-reviews (a round after the PR's first posted review; a round's findings by the last run that recorded
  them, as the value section reads them) by the judge's title suffixes into new, missed earlier (with its
  share) and fallout of fixes, the rounds that were full passes apart (47 of 69 missed-earlier findings since
  10-12 came from full passes, which read the whole PR again by design): a round is a full pass when the last
  `engine.round_start` event of its PR at or before its first run says `full_pass` of the head that first run
  reviewed (`store.PostedReview.RoundTarget`), the only per-round record of one (`kvPRFullPass` keeps only the
  last). Not the posted review's head: a push during the reviewers restarts the round in place on the new head
  with no start of its own (14 of 108 full-pass starts since 10-12 were followed by a `round.restarted` before
  the next start), and the judge's review is of that head. A start of another head is an earlier round's,
  which a round whose start the engine failed to write does not inherit. The starts are read from a day before
  the first run of the earliest round with a finding in the window: the engine writes a round's start seconds
  before the pipeline creates its runs, so a round that began just before the window, or a paused full pass
  continued in it (the continue keeps the round and its first run), has its start before the window.
  `titleFalloutMark`, `titleMissedMark` and `splitFindingTitles` moved from the engine's fix loop to
  `store.FindingOrigin` and `store.SplitFindingTitles`, so the fix cap's message and the stats read one
  definition. APPROVALS (`approvals`, `stats_approvals.go`):
  for each repository with `auto_approve` (`config.AutoApproveFor`; every one the registry holds, a row of zeros
  when none merged in the window, so that no merges reads apart from no `auto_approve`), never one share across
  repositories that enforce a review and ones that do not, the PRs merged in the window (MERGED); AUTO-APPROVED,
  those on which an approval magnum posted by itself stood at the merge (`store.AutoApproval.Stands`: posted,
  and not withdrawn or dismissed; one that ended with its PR, one being withdrawn and one whose withdrawal
  GitHub refused still stand); MAGNUM ONLY, those of them no person approved, shown with its share of
  AUTO-APPROVED; PAST APPROVAL, those of them merged at a head after the one magnum approved; UNREVIEWED, those
  of these with a `pr.merged_unreviewed` event; MISSES, the retro's misses of class `miss` on the MAGNUM ONLY
  PRs, less the declines it routed to the notes as misses (`store.MissFilter.NoRoutedDeclines`: magnum's own
  finding that its author declined as wrong, over-ranked or missing the repository's context, stored as class
  `miss` under its thread's link, which the `declines` row carries too; 16 of the 74 class-miss rows were such
  declines), which would read as a defect another reviewer caught on a merge that rested on magnum alone. A
  person's approval is an `APPROVED` entry of `latest_reviews_json` or of `review_gate_json`'s opinions (each
  misses approvals the other has) whose login is not a bot's (`[bot]` or `-bot`), not the author's and not one
  of magnum's own automatic approvals; the operator's by hand counts. The join that tells magnum's approval from
  the operator's own by the same login: neither GitHub's review id nor the body with the hidden
  `magnum:auto-approval` marker is in the registry's review snapshots (the Details read neither), so it is the
  head: the same login and the same commit as a posted `auto_approvals` row (any of them when the entry names no
  commit, as GitHub's entries do once a force-push dropped the approved commit: then the login and the time
  alone) and, where the entry says when it was submitted (`latest_reviews_json` does, the gate's opinions do
  not), no later than a minute after magnum recorded its post. GitHub keeps one latest review per login, so an
  approval of that head by that login after magnum's is the operator's by hand (their approval of the head after
  magnum's, and the PR merged before magnum's follow-up saw it, is the case the time catches). A row the
  operator posted with `magnum approve --as` or the board's `A` (a `review.manual_verdict_begin` event names its
  `approval_id`) is theirs by hand, not magnum's automatic approval. The snapshot stops at the last Details read
  before the merge, so an approval given in that last interval is missed. Rejected: verdict `clean` as the pass
  (it treats a review with only P3s as a failure); cohorts by the first review (young PRs have had no time to
  need five heads, so the newest cohort looks fastest: censoring); a per-PR counter in kv (the runs are the
  record, as for the fix cap); any gate or regression signal on these numbers (fewer heads to pass can be bought
  with fewer findings; they are a trend to read next to the misses, never a target); a store of review ids for
  the join (a migration for a measurement the head already answers). Tests, failing first:
  TestStatsConvergenceCountsHeadsUntilNoSeriousFindingIsLeft (a pass at head 1, a P3-only review that passes, an
  earlier P2 still open and a blocking verdict without a P0-P2 counted that do not pass, a second review of one
  head and a nudge of one review that add nothing, a round after the merge dropped, own PRs on their own rows, a
  PR that never passed, MERGED OPEN, the open PRs with five heads, `--repo`, the text and the JSON keys),
  TestStatsPrintsConvergenceInAWindowWithoutRounds (PRs reviewed before the window that ended in it),
  TestStatsConvergenceSplitsReReviewFindingsByOrigin, TestStatsConvergenceTellsAFullPassByItsRoundsOwnStart (a
  full pass a push restarted on a new head, one that started a minute before the window, one paused before it
  and continued in it, a round whose start was never written) and
  TestStatsApprovalsCountsMergesOnMagnumsApprovalAlone (a person and magnum; magnum only at the merged head;
  magnum only past the head with a merged_unreviewed event and a miss; magnum only past the head without one;
  the operator's hand approval after magnum's, counted as a person's; bot and author approvals ignored; an
  approval only in `review_gate_json` counted; a withdrawn approval and an approval by hand through
  `magnum approve --as` that are not magnum's; a miss on a PR a person approved and a routed decline, not
  counted; an approval of a commit a force-push dropped, magnum's by the login and the time, and the operator's
  later one, a person's; a repository with `auto_approve` that merged nothing in the window, a row of zeros,
  also under `--repo`) in cli, TestStatsCommandJSON's key lists, and TestFindingTitlesSplitByTheJudgesSuffixes
  moved to store. The improve loop's run log records PASS@1, 5+, the missed-earlier share and MAGNUM ONLY from
  `magnum stats --since <since> --json` each run (landing.md).

- **The fixer fixes the same defect in the PR's own lines too, as a trial, and improve runs count recurring
  posted classes** (2026-10-26, spec 03 of the 2026-10-26 run; the operator approved the fixer's part as a trial
  the same day). The operator's own PRs that ran the fix loop held 159 of 660 posted rounds (24%), a mean of 12.2
  rounds per PR against 2.66 for colleagues' PRs; talkable#11483 had 47 rounds and 26 fix runs, and 4 of the 5
  `fix.capped` loops were on it. On those PRs 37 findings were "in the fix for" another finding, 25 of them P1 or
  P2. The review side already flags a class: a merged finding's **Fix** names every other `path:line`, a missing
  guard in a set is swept and posted whole, and the re-review sweeps the set again before it calls a fix done. The
  fixer, though, changed only the line a finding named (section 1: "Change only what a finding or an external item
  names"), so a sibling reached it only when the judge named one. In one case the fixer covered one rule and a P2
  for its sibling rule came at round 4, which a search for the first rule's name would not have found; two more
  leftovers were the same defect in other code of the PR. Section 5 of the fix skill now has a step between
  changing the code and running the specs: look for the same defect in the rest of the PR's own lines (`gh pr
  diff`, since the fix prompt carries no base ref): the other members of the set the finding's code belongs to
  that the PR adds beside it (sibling rules, call sites, branches, parallel copies, untested guards of the same
  kind), fix each one the finding's own probe proves there, in the same commit, prove its guard as the next step
  says, and leave lines the PR did not add alone. When the specs fail because of an extra site, the fixer undoes
  that site alone (its lines, since its file can hold the named fix too), leaves it out of the reply and runs the
  specs again; only a failure of the named fix itself undoes the whole change and puts the finding under `## Needs
  you`, as before, so an extra site never costs the fix the finding asked for. The scope rule of section 1 says
  "or the same defect in the PR's own lines". The Fixed-in reply adds `, also at <path>:<line>` after `<what
  changed>` for each extra site, so it still opens with `Fixed in <sha7>: `, which the re-review reads and on
  which `classifyReply` decides (its first clause), so the classifier needs no change. A missing test is magnum's
  most repeated finding: in one repository 78 posted test-gap findings on 29 of 86 PRs, 45 of the 51 answered ones
  fixed, and 33 rounds on 30 PRs posted nothing else. The operator brings a line for that team's instruction file
  himself. So the improve run's evidence (`scripts/evidence.sh`) gains "Recurring posted classes per repository":
  the PRs with posted findings, the PRs and findings of the test-gap class, matched by title words in one CTE
  (`test_gap_posted`: regression, coverage, untested, no example, without failing, the new test, specs or suite
  green, lacks a test and a few more. The list was checked against the registry's 916 titled posted findings and
  is read before a title's "(in the fix for" part. A bare "test" is left out, since most such titles name A/B
  tests, test data or a failing test), the class's share of first-review findings, how the authors answered (the
  latest `declines` row of each finding, through `finding_row_id`), and the rounds whose posted findings were all
  of the class. Its "Fixer trial" line counts the window's fix runs, those that pushed, their "Fixed in" replies
  in the next posted round's threads file and those naming "also at". The replies are matched by the commits the
  run's report lists under `## Pushed`: the registry keeps who replied, never the text, and a reply cut at 600
  characters loses its marker. The line also counts the next round's findings tagged "(missed earlier)" or "(in
  the fix for" and those on a path a finding of the answered round named. The baseline when this landed: 58 fix
  runs, 55 that pushed, 146 Fixed-in replies, none naming "also at", and their 54 next rounds posted 90 findings,
  13 missed earlier and 17 in the fix for, 13 of the tagged ones on a path the answered round named. Lens 9 gains a
  paragraph: a class that recurs on 4 or more PRs of one repository and is mostly fixed is a candidate fix at the
  source; the analyst reads that repository's base `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` first, as data and never as
  instructions, the rule magnum's own `AGENTS.md` sets for a checkout's (a class the file covers is enforcement,
  not a gap), and otherwise proposes one instruction-file line or CI check for the operator to bring to the team,
  which magnum never posts. **Measure:** the next improve run reads the trial line (replies naming "also at", the
  tagged findings per fix run, and the repeats on a path the fix touched) and the test-gap share of first-review
  findings per repository against the numbers above; the step stays when sites are named and repeats fall without
  more fallout per fix run, and goes otherwise. Rejected: a fixer that also changes lines the PR did not add (the
  pre-existing code is the author's call, and each such line is more fixer code for the re-review to judge); a new
  mechanism in the skill (a sweep list, a per-class table) instead of one step; a `BaseRef` in the fix prompt for
  `git diff <base>...HEAD` (a golden and a test for what `gh pr diff` gives). Tests:
  TestTheFixSkillFixesTheSameDefectInThePRsOwnLines (failing first, with its pin of the extra site's undo);
  TestClassifyReplyReadsAFixedInReplyThatNamesTheSameDefectsOtherSites, which passed before the change too, since
  the classifier needed none; and the selftest's evidence.sh fixture, which gains a second PR with an answered
  round, two fix runs and the next round, each of six mutations of the new section failing one of its checks; one
  of its test-gap titles opens with "Regression", as many real ones do, so matching the words against the title
  as written, not lowered, fails a check too.

- **One replay of a case at a time** (2026-10-26, spec 01 of the 2026-10-26 run, part A). On 2026-10-20 two
  replays of one case ran at once: they shared the herdr workspace label `eval <repo>#<N>` and the worktree
  `~/.local/state/magnum/eval/wt/<case>`, and each destroyed the other's. `magnum eval run` refuses to start
  while the skill gate runs, but nothing kept two runs of the CLI apart (eval-at.sh before and after a change,
  started side by side) or a gate that started during a run, and the gate's guard cases (the next entry) come
  from the operator's corpus, the cases eval-at.sh replays in improve runs. `evalrun.RunCase` now takes an
  exclusive lock per case name (`<eval root>/locks/<case>.lock`, a `dblock` flock with the holder's pid and run
  written in, so a replay that crashes or is killed frees it) right after its option checks and holds it to the
  end of its cleanup (the worktree's removal and the app's close run before the release); `Started` is when it
  took the lock. A second replay of the case tries again every 5 seconds, honors its context between tries (a
  cancelled wait ends the case with an error that says what it waited for), and says once, through
  `Deps.Warn`, which run it waits for (the CLI's stderr, the daemon's log). Replays of different cases still
  run side by side. The lock covers `magnum eval run`, eval-at.sh (which runs it) and the gate alike, since all
  three replay through `RunCase`. Rejected: refusing the second replay (an improve run's eval-at.sh would fail
  instead of measuring) and dblock's 100 ms polling (a replay waits for a review round, minutes). Left open:
  two different cases of one PR still share the workspace label `eval <repo>#<N>`; the spec keeps different
  cases running side by side. Tests, failing first: TestTwoReplaysOfOneCaseNeverOverlap (the second starts only after the first
  ended, says once that it waits for the first's run, and a replay of another case runs meanwhile) and
  TestAReplayWaitingForItsCaseStopsWhenCancelled in evalrun.

- **The gate guards what master finds, and a won miss is replayed twice** (2026-10-26, spec 01 of the 2026-10-26
  run, parts B to E). The gate entry above says `learn.SelectCases` fills the places after the targets with "the
  newest other cases of both corpora"; it walked the merged corpora backward, and the learned corpus ends with
  its 29 `decline-` cases, so every such place went to an `expect = "absent"` case, which tests noise only.
  Across 8 gates, 0 of 20 compared rows had a defect found at the baseline: `GateRow.Lost` and Judge's "lost
  ... after a second replay" never fired and could not. Proposal 7 had 32 targets, 26 skipped past `gate_cases
  = 6`, all 6 compared rows targets. Both landed proposals passed on one candidate replay that went from 0 to 1
  found (proposal 5 on miss-182, whose five earlier stored replays found 0; proposal 7 on miss-543), and 22 of
  the 51 cases with a stored replay had a newest replay that found a defect, none replayed since skill version
  2. Guards: `learn.SelectCases` takes `learn.Guards` and adds, after the targets and before the newest-other
  fill, up to `[learn] gate_guards` (default 2, 0 to 10, 0 = none) cases whose newest stored replay found a
  defect, the least recently replayed first, so successive gates take turns through them; their places come on
  top of `gate_cases`, a guard is never a target, flagged and unwatched cases are skipped as before, and
  `GateCase.Guard` and `GateRow.Guard` (JSON `guard`) mark them. `learn.GuardsFrom` builds them over the
  replays made before the proposal (`eval.RunsBefore`), for which cases guard as for their order, and the
  gate takes the same replay as a guard's baseline (`Guards.Replay`), so every gate of one proposal takes the
  same guards with the same baselines whatever was replayed since (the gate's own replays of the base, an
  improve run's eval-at.sh), and a resumed gate cannot drop a guard whose base replay showed a regression; it
  leaves out the candidate's own replays (a gate that stops short after its candidate lost a guard keeps
  guarding it), and, for which cases guard and for their baselines, every gate's replays of its candidate,
  any proposal's: a guard and its baseline come only from replays not made by a gate's candidate. A stored
  run says what it replayed only by its label, `learn.GateRunLabel` ("learn gate of proposal N: candidate",
  "second", "baseline", "baseline judge", the same since the gate began), which the engine writes and
  `GuardsFrom` reads back. Another proposal's candidate run read a skill that may never land: one that found
  a defect master's skill does not would make the case a guard on that replay, the next candidate would lose
  it twice, the base would lose it too, and the gate would write a false `learn.guard_lost_at_base` warning
  and toast after three wasted replays. The order (`Guards.Last`) still counts those replays, the newest
  replay before the proposal in any run: a gate replays its guards only as its candidate's first and second
  replays (the base only for one the candidate lost twice), so without them a guard's last replay would never
  move after a gate that passes, and every later gate would take the same least recently replayed guards
  again. The order counts every replay attempt, scored or not (`learn.lastReplayed`): a gate goes on past a
  guard's candidate replay that ends with an error, a refusal or a cut (a guard is no target), and if only
  scored replays counted, a case that never scores (its head gone, say) would keep its place, and waste a
  replay, in every later gate; a case a stopped `magnum eval run` lists as skipped (`eval.OutcomeSkipped`)
  was not replayed and does not count. A replay not made by a gate's candidate can still have read a skill that never landed: an operator's
  `magnum eval run --candidate` and eval-at.sh's "after" replay at an unlanded builder commit carry no gate's
  label and can make a guard. That case is accepted: when the next candidate loses such a guard twice, the
  gate replays the base, the base's replay (a baseline run, which counts) is then the case's newest replay
  and found nothing, so the case leaves the guard pool, and its warning comes at most once per such case.
  A case's newest replay (`eval.NewestReplay`: scored, at the corpus's
  head, full or judge-only, any inputs of those runs) is the one replayed last (`eval.ReplayedAt`: the case's
  start, else its run's), in whatever run:
  a gate's base run is made at its first baseline replay and takes a lost guard's base replay after the
  candidate's runs were made, so the newest run's replay would make every guard that caught a regression
  leave the pool. The gate's `learn.gate_start` event counts the guards (`guards`). A guard's baseline is
  lazy: the candidate replays first, and one that finds every defect that replay found passes with it as its
  Before (`Stored`, and a note naming its run and inputs), nothing of the base replayed; a loss is replayed
  again, and a second loss takes the base's score: the newest stored replay with the base's inputs that is
  the guard's baseline or was made after it (`eval.Baseline.At`; one an earlier gate of the proposal made,
  say), else a replay of the base now (an older replay of the base never stands in for a newer one that found
  more). A defect the base finds and the candidate lost twice is a regression; one the base lost too skips
  the row (`lost at the base too`) with one warn `learn.guard_lost_at_base` event (the proposal, the case, the
  run that last found it, the base's inputs hash) and one toast per proposal and case (the registry reserves
  the pair, since a resumed gate decides the guard again), which name case and run ids only: the review at
  master no longer finds what it did, the drift of a model, the notes, the code or a hand edit, and the signal
  a later canary would be built on. `learn.Regressions` (Judge's fail rule) never counts a loss or a new hit
  against a `Stored` baseline of other inputs. Judge-only, a guard's judge reads the reports of a full replay
  whose reviewers read the candidate's prompts, and none is made for a guard, so a case guards a judge-only
  gate only with such a full replay made before the proposal (`learn.GuardsFrom`'s `reviewers`), its place
  otherwise going to the next case that has one: the least recently replayed cases are the least likely to
  have one at the reviewer prompts of the day, so a judge-only gate would leave both places out and never
  rotate them. A miss target whose
  first candidate replay found more than its baseline (`GateRow.WonOnce`) gets one more replay, a stored
  second one of a gate that stopped short reused, and counts as improved only when that one finds more too
  (`GateRow.Confirm`, `Confirmed`, `GateCase.SecondRun`); otherwise it is not improved ("found by the first
  replay only") and the dismissal after two failed gates applies; a proposal that regressed already gets no
  confirmation (it fails either way), and such a win counts neither way for its input (`GateRow.Rechecked`,
  which `Confirm` sets: `TargetGate` gives no outcome for a win no second replay checked, since nothing showed
  the candidate does not find it, so it never counts toward that dismissal), and `RuleOnlyDeclines` does not
  change. `magnum learn --review` marks a
  guard `+` and shows each row's note. The improve run's hand path names the targets plus 2 guards:
  `magnum eval guards [--n N]` prints them with the gate's own selection (no candidate, no proposal), reading
  only, for eval-at.sh. Measure, per `learn.gate_done`: the compared rows with Before.Found above 0 (0 of 20;
  expect 2 per gate), the share of first miss wins the second replay confirms, `learn.guard_lost_at_base`
  events per week, and the gate's duration (about 2 to 3 more rounds). Rejected: a threshold on the summed
  noise (a single-defect case counts true findings as noise, and per-case noise swung 13 to 6 and 5 to 10 in
  one gate); a daily canary before the guard event shows drift; guards inside `gate_cases` (32 targets crowd
  them out); the CLI version in the inputs hash (no evidence of drift); reusing a stored replay with the base's
  inputs older than the guard's baseline as a lost guard's base score (a stale one would hide the drift the
  guard reports); counting the replays made since the proposal, a gate's own or eval-at.sh's, for which cases
  guard or in their order (a gate resumed after a drain could take other guards and drop a regression it had
  found); storing a gate's guard names for a resumed gate (the replays before the proposal give the same
  answer with no state); confirming a won target after a regression (a replay that changes no verdict); a
  field of its own for a gate run's kind (the runs stored so far carry the label alone, which has named the
  kind since the gate began); leaving the gates' replays of their candidates out of the order too (the guards
  would stop taking turns); detecting the replays of an unlanded skill outside the gate, by their label
  (eval-at.sh's labels are free text) or by walking master's history for their inputs hashes (the cost of
  hashing every commit's prompts and skill at every gate).
  Tests, failing first: in learn TestSelectCasesReservesGuardPlacesPastTheTargets (32
  targets and 2 guards give 8 runnable cases), TestSelectCasesRotatesGuardsLeastRecentlyReplayedFirst,
  TestAProposalsGatesTakeTheGuardsOfTheReplaysMadeBeforeIt, TestAGuardWhoseBaseFoundWhatACandidateLostStaysAGuard,
  TestAJudgeOnlyGateGuardsOnlyCasesWithAFullReplayOfItsReviewers,
  TestAGuardComesOnlyFromReplaysNotMadeByAGatesCandidate (another proposal's candidate and second replays left out,
  an older operator's or base's replay still guarding),
  TestSuccessiveGatesTakeTurnsThroughTheGuardsTheyReplayed (two gates' candidate and second replays move the
  order, the baselines stay the operator's), TestAGuardWhoseCandidateReplayEndedWithoutAScoreGoesToTheBackOfTheNextGate
  (an unscored replay moves the order, a skipped one does not),
  TestJudgeFailsAGuardTheCandidateLostTwiceAndTheBaseFinds, TestAGuardTheBaseAlsoLosesIsSkippedNotARegression
  and TestJudgePassesAMissWinOnlyWhenTheSecondReplayFindsItToo, with TestSelectCasesPutsTargetsFirstAndCapsTheRest
  extended; in eval TestNewestReplayIsTheNewestScoredReplayAtTheHead, TestNewestReplayIsTheLatestReplayNotTheLatestRun
  and TestRunsBeforeKeepsOnlyTheReplaysMadeBeforeATime; in engine
  TestTheGateReplaysAGuardsBaseOnlyWhenTheCandidateLostItTwice (replays counted per run kind),
  TestAGuardLostAtTheBaseWritesOneEventAndToast, TestAWonTargetIsReplayedAgainAndAStoredSecondReplayIsReused,
  TestAWonTargetInAGateThatRegressedElsewhereCountsNeitherWay (two failed gates leave the input new),
  TestAResumedGateKeepsItsGuardsAndTheBaseReplayItMade and
  TestAJudgeOnlyGateGuardsCasesWithAFullReplayOfTheCandidatesReviewers (a guard kept, one lost twice that the
  base's judge finds, one lost at the base, and a case without a full replay whose place goes to the next),
  TestAnotherProposalsCandidateReplayIsNoGuardOfTheNextGate (no false warning, no base replay; a case master
  found too guards on master's replay) (mutations of the guard places, the lazy baseline, the base's reuse,
  the report, the confirmation, the reservation of the warning, the judge-only rule, the engine's run label
  and the second replay's kind each fail one), with the gate tests' replay counts raised
  by the confirmation; in cli
  TestEvalGuardsPrintsTheCasesTheGateWouldGuard and TestLearnReviewShowsTheGateAsATable extended; in config the
  range of `gate_guards`.
- **`ignore_checks` makes magnum treat a named check as absent wherever it reads CI** (2026-10-26, spec 04 of
  the 2026-10-26 run, asked for by the operator; amends "The judge sees the head's failing checks", "A head
  whose CI turns red after the review gets a judge check", "The approval's CI gate counts only the checks
  required_checks names" and "The judge's own approval passes the approval's gates"). A new check, "Entire
  Gates", from a third-party app the team installed, appeared on talkable/talkable at 13:35Z; by the evening
  it was on 28 PRs, 26 of them open, it failed on every one, and the operator says it always fails. On
  talkable#12105 and talkable#12107 it was the only failed check and `prs.ci_json` read FAILURE: on #12105
  the judge posted its clean verdict as a comment (the head's checks fail), on #12107 the CI-red follow-up
  queued a judge-only round at 17:08Z whose `pr.413.ci_followup` record named only that check, every clean
  review on such a head ended "CI is red: Entire Gates failed, unrelated" instead of LGTM (the skill's
  section 7 reads `failing_checks`), and with no `required_checks` on the repository the automatic approval
  counted every check and waited for one that never passes. The rule: `ignore_checks` on a `[[watch]]`, and
  on a `[[repo]]`, whose list adds to its watch's (`config.Config.IgnoreChecks`, as
  `auto_approve_skip_authors` does), in `required_checks`' grammar (name globs, `workflow:<glob>`,
  `store.RequiredNames`; a bad entry fails to load through the shared `validateCheckGlobs`); default none.
  One helper defines the checks magnum sees: `store.SeenCI` leaves the named checks out of a head's stored
  checks, tallies the counts and Total again, and, when the checks are the head's and every one (Complete),
  derives the state from the rest (FAILURE when one failed, PENDING when one runs, SUCCESS when they passed
  or skipped, "" when none is left), so an ignored check that failed no longer holds GitHub's rollup at
  FAILURE; checks of another head or a list GitHub cut at 100 keep the rollup, since magnum cannot tell what
  the rest did, and a list that names none of the checks returns the stored CI itself, so nothing changes
  without the key. `store.PR.IgnoringChecks` puts the derived state into `CIState` too (the rollup the
  approval's CI gate reads) only when that rollup is the one the checks were read with: after a Details
  fetch that failed, `ci_state` (the radar's) can be newer than `ci_json`, and a derived SUCCESS from older
  checks would approve while a rerun runs, so the newer rollup decides as before. The readers: the judge's
  `failing-checks.json` (`pipeline.addFailingChecks`: a head whose only failed checks are ignored gets no
  file), the CI-red follow-up (`ciRedOf`, which reads the PR's repository from the registry only when a
  stored check failed, and `ciPollWorth`: an ignored check queues no judge check and never enters the
  record, and one a record holds from before the key counts as no longer failing, so its wait drops), the
  approval's CI gate (`ciGateOf`, which the automatic approval, its standing re-gate and the judge's approval
  gate share, so `failingCIRefusal`, the base tip's comparison and `requiredCIOf` read the seen checks: an
  ignored check is never compared with the base tip, and a `required_checks` entry that names only ignored
  checks names no check on the head, so the derived rollup decides), its ignored-checks note
  (`ignoredChecksNote`, which never names an ignored check), and the board's and `magnum prs`'s CI
  (`prsSource` passes the seen checks to `prsCI`, whose state, counts, workflows, failing jobs and required
  checks follow). Left as they are: the poll's change detection (`fetchDetails` compares GitHub's own rollup
  and counts with the stored ones, which stay as GitHub reported them, so a config change applies at once
  and a failure beside an ignored one still reads the checks again), `ciStatus` and `fillDetails` (they
  write the stored checks), `store.BoardRow.CIState` (no reader), the base tip's `CommitChecks` (only
  matched against the head's seen failures), and the webhooks' check hints (change detection). A derived
  state reads the latest run of each check, while GitHub's rollup also counts superseded runs: on a head
  with an ignored check, a superseded failed run no longer holds the approval. It changes nothing GitHub
  enforces, and the globs are the operator's configuration, never a PR's; no event, log or toast names a
  check for them. Rejected: reusing `required_checks` (it narrows only the automatic approval's CI gate and
  the board's readiness, and leaves the judge's `failing_checks`, its approval gate and the CI-red follow-up
  reading the check); the base-match rule (it lets a check through only when it failed on the base tip too,
  and this check need not run on the base branch); a sentence in the review skill (the skill is at its byte
  cap, and the judge reads CI only through `failing_checks`, so a check magnum leaves out never reaches a
  review). Tests, failing first: in config TestIgnoreChecksLoadsOnAWatchAndARepoWhoseListAddsToTheWatchs,
  TestAMalformedIgnoreChecksEntryFailsValidation and TestIgnoreChecksIsValidOnAPooledRepository; in store
  TestSeenCILeavesOutTheIgnoredChecksAndDerivesTheStateFromTheRest (a failed check left decides before one
  left that runs) and TestAPRIgnoringChecksTakesTheDerivedStateAsItsRollup; in pipeline
  TestFailingChecksLeaveOutAnIgnoredCheck; in engine TestAnIgnoredCheckThatFailsAfterTheReviewQueuesNoJudgeCheck,
  TestTheAutomaticApprovalPassesAHeadWhoseOnlyFailedCheckIsIgnored (the rollup FAILURE and the checks
  complete; it waits while another check runs, goes ahead on the base-match rule when another check fails on
  the base tip too, and a standing approval stays where without the key it is withdrawn),

- **The fixer replays its commits when the branch gained only a base merge** (2026-10-27, wave 1 item 6 of
  the companion-fix design, section 5.7). On talkable#12114 GitHub's "Update branch" merged master into the

  change on GitHub is a merge of the base. A new command, `magnum fix-sync --from <start head> --branch

  the fixer's own. It fetches the branch and the base from origin and replays the fixer's commits
  (`--from..HEAD`, `gitx.ReplayOnto`: `git rebase --onto <tip> <from> --no-update-refs`, signed as the
  repository's config says, since these are the fixer's commits) onto the branch's new tip only when every
  commit on the tip's first-parent chain since the start head is a merge, the oldest of them on top of the
  start head (`gitx.CommitsAfter`; a merge of the base is one commit there, without the base's commits it
  brings), and the PR's own diff against the base is the same at both (`gitx.OwnDiffID`: the `git patch-id
  --verbatim` of `diff-tree --patch --unified=0 --full-index <merge base> <head>`, the PR as GitHub's
  base...head shows it, with the base as fetched; without context lines a merge that changes other lines
  keeps the id, as line numbers and the order of files do not count, while one that resolved a conflict in
  the PR's lines, slipped a change in, re-indented a line or changed the spaces in it, or brought a branch
  the base lacks changes it: `--stable`, which `PatchID` keeps for the skill editor's landing, ignores
  whitespace, and YAML, Haml, Python and Makefiles read it). It prints "replayed N commits onto <sha>; HEAD
  is <sha>" (exit 0), and the fixer runs the specs of the changed files again and pushes once more, never
  with force, naming the new SHAs; specs that fail after the replay push nothing (a replay the base merge
  broke never goes out), and the findings go under Needs you. Anything else changes
  nothing and prints "refused: <reason>" (exit 1): a commit that is not a merge, a merge that changed the
  PR's own diff, a rewritten branch, a branch that did not move, an operation in progress, uncommitted
  changes to tracked files (a rebase refuses them, and specs dirty tracked files such as a schema dump), no
  commit of the fixer's, and a merge among the fixer's own commits: the base merge of a conflicting PR
  (spec 5.6) would be made again by a replay without its resolutions, so that case is refused and the
  unpushed merge goes to the author as the failed push already sends it. A replay that conflicts is
  aborted (the shared `rebase` helper of `RebaseOnto`, which now names the unmerged paths and looks at what
  is in progress and aborts on a context that outlives a stop), and the checkout is as it was. A replay that
  changed the checkout and could not be undone (its abort failed) or confirmed (HEAD unreadable after it)
  prints "failed: <reason>" with what is in the way (exit 3), never "refused", which tells the fixer that
  nothing changed; the fixer pushes nothing. These commits were never on GitHub, so the
  skill's history rule allows the replay; it now says "never force-push, rebase, amend or reset a commit
  that is on GitHub", and its push rule runs the fix-sync line once on a push rejected because the branch
  moved, with a clean work tree, and stops as before after a refusal, a failure, a prompt without the line
  or any other push failure (`push failed: …; fix-sync refused: <reason>`, or `fix-sync failed: <reason>`).
  The prompt names the line in its one
  paragraph (`FixPromptInput.FixSyncCommand`, `agents.FixSyncLine` with the job's start head, the PR's
  branch and base), never derived as the fix-reply line is, since only the job knows the base, and left

  `pushedHead`: `pushedHead` already takes any listed commit at HEAD that GitHub shows, and the report
  lists the replayed commits; but when the poller saw the merge during the run, the PR row's head was the

  wave 1 review; amends "The fixer merges the base when the PR conflicts with it" and "The fixer replays its
  commits when the branch gained only a base merge"). The `abort_merge` step aborted a merge alone, so a
  rebase `magnum fix-sync` left in progress (its abort failed, or it was killed mid-replay: exit 3) held
  the slot: the skill forbade the fixer to rebase, and the settle's `Slots.Resync` failed at its switch
  ("cannot switch branch while rebasing"), as every later checkout and release did, until someone aborted
  by hand. The step is now `abort_in_progress` (`slots.abortInProgress`): it aborts what `gitx.InProgress`
  names, a rebase, merge, cherry-pick or revert (`gitx.AbortOperation`, `git <op> --abort`, which replaces
  `MergeAbort` and refuses any other op before git runs), with a `slot.aborted` event that names it (it
  replaces `slot.merge_aborted`), after a `slot.discarded` event for the tracked changes the abort drops
  (the switch's own event found none left). It runs where it ran, after the resync's and the release's
  guard, so never over a person's changes. The skill now says that exit 3 means the replay changed the
  checkout and fix-sync could not undo it or could not confirm what it made, and lets the fixer run `git
  rebase --abort` once when the line says a rebase is still in progress, its only rebase command. Tests,
  failing first: in slots (real git) TestResyncAbortsARebaseOrACherryPickLeftInProgress ("cannot switch
  branch while rebasing", "while cherry-picking"); in gitx TestAbortOperationEndsWhatInProgressNames; the
  exit-3 and `git rebase --abort` lines of TestTheFixSkillSyncsAPushTheBranchMovedPast.
- **`magnum fix-reply` exits 2 for a line the fixer got wrong** (2026-10-27, the wave 1 review; amends "Every
  reply of the fixer goes through `magnum fix-reply`, which signs it"). A non-numeric `--comment` (a
  thread's `PRRT_` node id), an unknown flag, an argument, and both or neither of `--comment` and `--issue`
  exited 1, which the skill reads as "could not confirm: run the same line once more", so the fixer ran
  the wrong line again. They are `invalid` now, exit 2, the fixer's to fix (`FixReplyOptions.Check` returns
  the outcome: a pull request the pane's `MAGNUM_PR_URL` names wrongly stays an error, exit 1, since
  nothing the fixer types mends it), a `--comment` that does not parse says that it takes a review
  comment's number id, and the skill says that exit 2 refuses the reply or the line. An invalid outcome's
  line reads "refused (N problems); nothing posted: …". Accepted, and not mended: someone else's comment
  between a lost answer and its retry makes the retry post a second copy, since `postedLast` takes the
  same reply only when nobody else wrote after it (the rule that lets the same answer to new pushback go
  out). Tests, failing first: TestFixReplyChecksTheOptions (postreview) and
  TestFixReplyRefusesWhatIsNotAFixersReply (cli: a thread's node id, an unknown flag, an argument, both and
  neither exit 2 with status invalid), and the exit-2 line of
  TestTheFixSkillProvesEachGuardFixesRegressionsAndSignsItsReplies.
- **The fix-sync line names the slot's checkout** (2026-10-27, the wave 1 review; amends "The fixer replays
  its commits when the branch gained only a base merge"). The line took the checkout from the fixer's
  current directory, so a fixer whose shell stood elsewhere (a subproject, a temporary directory) ran
  nothing (exit 2) or ran in another repository. `agents.FixSyncLine` takes the checkout and the fix job
  passes the slot's path, as the db-lock line does (`--checkout <slot path>`; "" leaves it out). Tests,
  failing first: TestTheFixSyncLineReplaysInTheCheckoutItNamesFromAnyDirectory (cli, real git: the line
  run from a directory outside any work tree replays in the slot) and the slot's path in
  TestAPushAfterAFixSyncSettles, TestTheFixSyncLineNeedsTheBranchAndASafeBase,
  TestTheFixPromptNamesTheFixSyncCommand and the four fix goldens.
- **A slotless fix request looks for a free slot before it reads GitHub or fetches** (2026-10-27, the wave 1
  review). `prepareFix` runs in the daemon's tick, and for a PR whose slot the pool took back it read the
  other reviewers' items on GitHub, and on a review that found nothing fetched the base (up to 30
  seconds), before `fixSlotFree`, which reads the registry alone, refused it for no free slot. The look
  comes first now, after the other cheap refusals. A request it refuses has its slot freed for the retry
  (`needSlot`) before the later refusals run, so a slotless request that would be refused for nothing to
  answer may free a slot first; the retry then says why. Before, a rate-limited read of the other
  reviewers held such a request instead of refusing it for no free slot; now it is refused, and the retry
  goes on. Test, failing first: TestAFixWithoutAFreeSlotRefusesBeforeItReadsGitHubOrFetchesTheBase (three
  GitHub reads, and a fetch on a review that found nothing).
- **A conflict call names 20 paths and counts the rest** (2026-10-27, the wave 1 review; amends "The fixer
  merges the base when the PR conflicts with it"). `attention.ConflictCall` joined every path the fixer
  listed under Needs you into the message, the card and `magnum status`; the prompt names at most 20. It
  names the first 20 too, then "and N more", which `fixCallRe` reads back. Test, failing first:
  TestAConflictCallNamesTwentyPathsAndCountsTheRest.
- **The status comment says why a clean review brought no approval** (2026-10-28,
  docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-auto-approval-explained-design.md; amends "Auto-approval leaves the PRs of
  listed authors to a person": "the status comment never spoke of auto-approval"). On talkable#12092 one
  reviewer did not finish ("codex-review (busy)") and on talkable#12100 the PR edited
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: both reviews were clean, no approval came, and the author and the operator
  asked why, which only the operator's card and a `review.auto_approve_refused` event said. Every refusal of
  the gates now has a class (`publicRefusal` in `autoapprove_gates.go`; `autoRefusal` carries `why`, the
  class and `waits` through `authorRefusal`, `autoGateRefusal`, `missingReports`, `changedFilesRefusal`,
  `ciAnswer.refusal` and `standingGateRefusal`), and the refusal record (`AutoApproveRefused`) keeps it as
  `public`. Under the posted line of the status comment one line (`approvalLine`, `publicText`) names the
  `auto_approve_as` login as plain text, in the third person, and gives the class's fixed words, never the
  record's reason: `workflows`, `agent_config` and `too_many_files` say that the login must review and
  approve the PR in person; `unheard` that one of Magnum's reviewers did not finish and that the next
  review or the login's decides; `ci_runs` and `ci_fails` that the approval waits for the head's checks
  ("Some fail now."); `stopped`, from the PR's held stop, which wins over the record, that Magnum stopped
  approving it; and `post_failed`, which the last failed post writes with no refusal event
  (`review.auto_approve_failed` says it; the card then reads "its approval did not post, …"), that it did
  not post and that the login was told. The line shows only in the posted stage, not while a held review's
  full pass follows, when the login is set, the record's head is the PR's and its run the last posted
  round, whose review is the PR's last, the round left nothing to fix, the PR is open and not the login's,
  and GitHub's latest reviews hold no approval of the head by the login. `noteStatusComments` reads the
  records and the holds once a tick (where a watch auto-approves), and the line goes into the view's body
  and its state, so it moves the header's time; it lags auto-approval by a tick, and a reason that changes
  within its class edits nothing. Silent, the comment reading as on a watch without `auto_approve`: both
  author lists (the operator kept the rule of 2026-10-16 on 2026-10-28), every watch filter of a forced
  round, the operator's own PR, their review in progress, a head the login approved, a reason that carries
  an error's text or heals at the next poll (an unreadable run or round record, a missing or unreadable
  file list, an incomplete review list, a retried post), the states the stage already shows, and any gate
  added later without a class. A record written before the class existed gains it on the next pass,
  rewritten as it stood (its time kept), with no second event. A withdrawal's dismissal message uses the
  class's clause (`publicReason`) in place of the gate's raw reason ("found nothing to fix, but the PR
  changes its own CI workflows or actions, so alice must review and approve it in person"), and "Magnum no
  longer approves it automatically" for a gate without a class; that message is also the row's end reason,
  the withdrawn event's and the toast's (the card keeps the gate's own words). Nothing changes when Magnum
  approves, it reads nothing new from GitHub, and no migration. Rejected: the review body (it posts before
  the gates decide, and checks and stops change after it); a comment of its own (each notifies people and
  repeats the status comment's lifecycle), so no line where `status_comment` is off; an `@` mention (it
  notifies at every edit, and the operator already has the card, the event and the toast); moving
  `noteStatusComments` after `autoApprove` in the tick (the one-tick lag is accepted); a stored basis hash
  of the facts (the line is rebuilt each tick from the head, the round, the stop and GitHub's latest
  reviews). Tests, failing first (engine, the login `alice`): TestACleanReviewOfAWorkflowChangeSaysWhoMustApprove,
  TestAReviewThatMissedAReviewerSaysSoWithoutTheRole, TestTheApprovalLineGoesWhenTheChecksPassAndTheApprovalPosts,
  TestALaterRoundsWithdrawalBringsTheLineBackOnTheNewHead, TestAnUnchangedClassEditsNothing,
  TestAStoppedAutoApprovalSpeaksInTheThirdPerson, TestNoApprovalLineOnceTheLoginApprovedTheHead,
  TestTheAuthorListsAndFiltersLeaveTheCommentAsWithoutAutoApproval, TestNoApprovalLineWithoutAutoApproveOrALogin,
  TestAnOldRefusalRecordGainsItsClassWithoutASecondEvent, TestAFinalPostFailureSaysTheLoginWasTold,
  TestTheWithdrawalMessageUsesThePublicWords and TestApprovalLineNeverCarriesTheRecordsWords; the
  withdrawal tests of the gates, the workflows and ignore_checks now expect the class's words.

## Learned rules

The self-improving review loop appends these: the skill editor's decisions and the reverts of skill
versions, newest last. People add their entries to the sections above, never here.

- **The judge checks a version a change sets or bumps (API, runtime, SDK) with `date` against the
  platform's support and deploy window (P1 when expired) and its packages and lockfile against the
  release line (P2), and ranks a race with a window of seconds or less and a small loss on one record
  P3, even when the loss stays** (2026-10-17, the skill editor's proposal for m193, m183, m182, m175,
  m167, d196, d194, d164, d161, d157, d145, d128, d121, d120, d116, d115). An expired version and a new
  API version over old packages pass the build and were missed; an earlier version rule in the
  platform-rules paragraph did not move the replays, so the check now sits in section 2's Look-for list,
  in the reviewers' prompts and in the own-pass prompt, with an explicit `date` step. Four declined
  findings ranked a narrow race too high. The reviewers also check whose role an API key or token
  carries when a new check reads the acting user's role, because a stand-in user answers for the wrong
  identity; the skill already states the key case. To make room, the skill shortens the prepass,
  readiness and evidence bullets (the prompts say the same), the machine-failure list, one verdict
  sentence and a section 7 clause that section 5 repeats; no rule was dropped.
- **The judge ranks a rare precondition with a cheap repeat or a brief harm P3 (an outside actor
  deleting what the code created, all probes failing, weeks of failures dropping an item from a
  low-stakes sweep, a short race against a restore or import, a late write missing from an aggregate),
  and the reviewers and the judge's own pass look for nine shapes the replays missed: consent read from
  free text, a secret sent to a host built from request input, a find-or-create that adopts a record it
  does not own, restore and bulk paths that skip the editor's guards, placeholder values, copied
  templates and stale derived values, specs that assert a bound the change raises, stubs of the guarded
  call, and error claims made without reading the call chain** (2026-10-24, the skill editor's proposal
  for m548, m547, m546, m545, m544, m543, m542, m540, m539, m538, m506, m505, m504, m503, m502, m501,
  m500, m499, m498, m497, m496, m331, m313, m281, m274, m273, m222, m217, m216, d701, d611, d596, d463,
  d427, d400, d398, d261, d254, d242, d240). The simplify prompts drop a proposal whose saving the
  author must re-verify. Why: the declined findings had a rare trigger or a cheap repeat; the misses
  were shapes the skill covered only in part. The skill holds the priority rule; the checks sit in the
  uncapped prompts. To make room the skill shortens the readiness, prepass and notes lines, the
  machine-failure list, the Checks example and the reread clause; no rule was dropped.
